I have had the Patricia II wedge in black for about 1 year & wore them regularly in season. When I saw the Patricia at a good price in navy (from 6pm), I purchased them because I thought they would fit just like my Patricia IIs. I was wrong, and paid the price with return shipping that 6pm doesn't pay.

The crocs website says that crocs aren't suppose to fit like other sandals - they are suppose to be looser & thus more comfortable - I normally wear an 8-1/2, so have now tried both an 8 & a 9 in the Patricia shoe (I have an 8 in the Patricia II). The Patricia 9 swims on my feet & they would be a hazard to walk around in. The size 8 fits my left foot (which is my wider foot) but is too narrow on my right foot. When I placed the shoes sole to sole, I did notice a slight difference in the width, which, apparently, my foot notices too. I can only conclude a manufacturing defect. But, it is this shoe specifically or the form for this shoe? (others have written the shoe is narrow).

Consequently, if you have a wider foot, order the Patricia II instead of this one & if you are a 1/2 size, order down, not up.

My mom always had these shoes for my sister and I when we were babies (or a very similar style), so I thought they'd be great everyday shoes for my one year old.  She already had shoes she was about to grow out of, so I got the next size up in advance so we'd have them when she was ready to wear them.  I tried them on her when they arrived to check on the width issue based on other reviews, and it seemed she'd be able to wear them.  In the six weeks since then, her feet have not just grown in length but width as well, because now that her feet are long enough for the shoes, there is absolutely no way I can velcro these shut without squeezing her poor little feet!  In addition to that, the first time I even tried to get them on her, the loop that holds the strap in the middle popped right open (the seam came apart).  I immediately got on my computer to print a return receipt only to discover the return policy is only 30 days on these (I'll admit I'm used to returning items to stores that have 90 day policies).  Now I have a pair of damaged, too-small shoes that we will ever even use.  What a waste!!

After owning the boots a couple months a piece of rubber broke off the front of the sole, but it was no big deal, it was by the toe and not the part that touches the ground.

They are advertised to be water proof, but one day about a week after buying them I was out walking in a very heavy rain, and walked through a few shallow puddles a couple inches deep, by the time I got home my feet were soaked, so much for them being water proof, actually I would not wear them if it was raining hard or I expected to be walking in wet grass or whatever because the water always soaked through.

The final straw was about 4 months ago when the soles separated from the uppers on both shoes, the holes were big enough for me to put three fingers in by the time I stopped wearing the boots.

I started wearing Crocs when I began college in Boulder, CO, which is the birthplace of Crocs. I'll continue to wear Crocs out of loyalty, but I'm not ecstatic about these "classic" Crocs. I put classic in quotation marks, because Crocs loyalists know that they were once made in the USA, and the shoes that were made in the USA were sized in ranges and were made of superior material that was a tad bit softer. Please know that I'm traditionally not a hooah-hooah "Made in the USA" minion, but there are distinct differences between the USA- and Mexican-made Crocs. Crocs made in Mexico are made of a similar (but different) material that has a slippery finish, and they are sized in whole-sizes only. I resisted buying Mexican Crocs because of these material and fit factors, and so I wore down my USA Crocs to the end.

I wear a 10.5 running show, and in the USA size Crocs I wore men's XL (10-11), which were perfect! For the Mexican Crocs I ordered M11, but they were too large: too much play in the toes and too much length between the heel of the shoe and the heel of the foot. I returned them for Mexican M10, which is what I settled on. They're good with room in the toe, but I would have liked an extra half-inch on the heel. This is why the USA sizing scheme was better FOR ME. I acknowledge all feet are different.

My perspective: I am a long distance runner. I run from 4-25 miles so the amount of miles daily can vary. I have had some challenges with injuries over the last year as well starting with metatarsal bone bruising and ended up now with a MCL Sprain and Pes Anserinus tendinitis. I spend a lot of time looking for the right shoes. I have both the NB Vazee Pace and the Vazee Rush. Of the two I prefer the Rush (though many of my runner friends prefer to Pace).

This shoe is built on the same last as the New Balance Zante which means it has a fairly snug midfoot and a decent size toe box. It has more toe box height for me then the Zante and more than the Pace. The overlays are structured in such a way as they don't hit any of my hot spots. The cushioning is New Balance RevLite (I think) and this is a much firmer material that has good energy return and spring. However it is NOT mushy/cushy or like walking on clouds. The heel/toe drop is 6mm which is middle of the line. The toe is upturned which does give you a feeling of springing forward. I find this shoe very comfortable to run in and can do long distances. It doesn't have a ton of support - however it's not a minimal shoe. The heel, in particular, is not super structured nor does it have hard plastic in it - this is music to my achilles which often react to other shoes with very plastic/hard heel counters. These do stretch a bit but like any running shoe you should not need to break them in. The vast huge majority of people I see buying running shoes are buying them WAY TOO SMALL. I cannot tell you how many people I see complain and I can SEE the tip of their toe is practically coming out the front. You should have at least one fingers width from the top of your longest toe to the tip of the shoe - and if you go long distances you can often desire even a bit more. I think it's vanity that people insist they wear a X size shoe. I've seen feet so stuffed into shoes it looks like they are have rolled sausages and one hit will cause them all the flesh to pop out like those old biscuit packages! Stop buying shoes too small folks. Who cares what the size is. My size in these is 1 full size larger then many of my street shoes but about normal for me in running shoes. I wear a 6.5M or 6.5W and sometimes a 7M normally in flat's or heels. I bought these in 7.5M and they are just fine. If you have a foot that usually fits a M then just make sure you are sized appropriately. If your foot tends to run wider (but not so wide you always buy wide shoes) then make sure you go up at least a 1/2 size...or buy the wide 1/2 size longer. These are consistent with my other shoes for length but they are a bit pointy so take that into consideration.

If you are someone who wants cushy marshmallow cushion then you should look more at the New Balance Fresh Foam line (as revised) because they are softer and more "cushy" and also wonderful shoes for all distance running. I've been wearing my Rush all day on weekends and walking all over and doing some of my running (I rotate shoes to prevent injuries) and they have satisfied me in all conditions. I highly recommend them IF you are someone who likes a firmer shoe but with good rebound and energy, likes mid range drops (4-8MM), does not require a ton of stability or support, and just really likes a comfortable non confining shoe that is great for multi purpose!one hit will cause them all the flesh to pop out like those old biscuit packages! I purchased the Black Micorsuede shoe, and went down a size according to Amazon specifications. While this shoe DOES fit, due to the fact that I wanted to insert some of those squishy shoe pads, I returned them for a size up. They have a hard sole, but the shoes themselves are exceptionally flexible and appear to be made out of a kind of suede-like material that easily absorbs water. They have a velvety type texture to them, in case you were wondering how suede-y they are. The shoes I got actually didn’t have any kind or odor at all, unless you put your nose within an inch of the shoes, and at that close there was no smell of gasoline. They actually smell sort of like new shoes.

The size 6 I got (I wear a 6.5 or 7) was about 9 5/8” long, from heel to toe and 3 ½” wide from the widest part where the toes are.

PROS:
-Cheap and lightweight.
-Fast shipping.
-Fits fairly true to size. (I wear 6.5 and the size 6 would have been fine if I didn’t want to put shoe inserts in them.)
-True to color.
-The suede felt very soft, and wasn’t worn away.
-Little to no odor (like many people complained).
-The flexible nature of the shoes allow you to stretch out your toes.

CONS:
-Cheaply constructed.
-Very squishy and flexible canvas-like material, so I can see these wearing out quickly.
-Definitely not the kind of shoes you’ll want to wear in the rain, or even after a rain. They will soak up water quickly.
-While these shoes have a loop to pull through the buckle, there aren't any holes to sufficiently tighten the shoes. If you want holes, you’ll have to make them yourself.

TIPS:
If you’re going to wear shoe inserts (which I would recommend since these shoes are very cheap), you should go true to size. I just bought these locally and I can tell you they look even better in person than the photos. I am neurotic about my shoes fitting and am consistently disappointed in fit within 6 months after almost any shoe or boot purchase. On the metal sizing tool at most shoe stores, I am an 9D; in most sneakers, I am an 8.5D; in work, hiking and cowboy boots, I vary from 8.0E-8.5D. Bottom line, my foot size is pretty random. Couple this with variances among brands and models, I feel like a hopeless case. Physical context: I'm 5'7 and range from 175 to 200 lbs.  On my previous boot purchase, I ordered 4 pairs of the same boot in order to get the right fit. Sure enough, 6 months later, I was disappointed. The boots had broken in so much that my feet were swimming in them.  So today, when I bought the Lucchesies, the sales gal convince me to ditch my socks and put on these pantyhose footy things.  With them, I got my feet pretty snug into an 8D (as mentioned, I often end up with an 8-1/2 or an 8E).  I'm home now, and I've been wearing them with the aforementioned fru-fru socks for an hour and my feet are really settling down. I have high hopes in these stretching out to be the best fitting boots I've ever had. As the title says, "we'll see..."  As to quality -- these are really, really nice.  I've had several brands like Fry, Justin and Dan Post, and I really like what I'm wearing here.  I intend to update this review from time to time as these boots break in, so stay tuned. The ankle support on the trail is practically non existent.  The worst part of all is there is NO TRACTION what-so-ever!  I slipped on leaves, small rocks, ladge, leaves, and pretty much whatever I walked on besides blacktop.  When things were wet it made everything a million times worse!  It took me much longer because I had to be overly cautious walking so I wouldn't fall.  Even being extra careful I still fell 4 times.  I would never buy these shoes again, and if I would return them after putting 110 miles on them I would do it tomorrow!  Traction and lack of ankle support are huge problems with this boot.  Comfort and easy breaking in are the pros.

Birko-Flor = Faux Leather. Not a leather upper. Don't get me wrong, this is a great sandal from a fantastic shoe maker BUT I had expected the "upper" - meaning the parts of the shoe that go over the foot - to be leather. It is not. The "upper" material is listed on the box as "Birko-Flor" which appears to be fancy, German-shoemaker-speak for faux leather. Feels like vinyl on the outer-facing side; feels like polyester felt or faux wool on the inside that comes into contact with your foot. Very comfortable, but am wondering how the faux leather is going to hold up over time. The footbed-liner - meaning the part of the foot your foot sits on - is actually leather. A final note about the color: "Graceful Toffee" is a glossy, metallic brown. It looks like glossy mid-value brown indoors, but outside, in the sunlight, it looks more metallic, like a warm bronze. Very pretty, but did I mention it's not leather??

I always do my research online. I usually love ASICS, and Amazon for that matter. I have to say, I have never been so disappointed by ASICS or Amazon.

I have a really serious pronation problem, which means that I need extra support in my shoes. I knew that ASICS have shoes that have great heel cups... little metal things inside the cushiony shoe that keep your feet from turning out of the shoe. After an ill-fated trip to the ASICS store where I was entirely ignored (I assume because I don't look like the typical runner), I did hours of research to find an ASICS shoe that had the "heel clutching system". I looked on the ASICS site as well as Amazon and several others.

My shoes showed up today, and to my surprise, the "heel clutching system" was no such thing. It was a mere plastic line that went around the heel and would have offered absolutely no support. The shoes were flimsy and seemed like they would break down with about one month of wear.

ASICS did not make this clear at all, and Amazon's absolute lack of information on these shoes was entirely misleading. So, I'm returning these and re-starting the hunt to see if I can find something decent. Beware the misleading information!

Huge upgrade from using Chuck's for squats and deadlifting.  I never believed in using a specialized shoe when I had a pair of perfectly good and flat Chuck's. The wider toe area let my foot spread out flat and I actually felt a difference in my stability.  I will not try to convince anyone that a specialized shoe will increase their lifts but I will definitely vouch that you WILL feel more sturdy with 500 pounds on your back when squatting.  You WILL feel great when you get home and take your shoes off after a heavy lift day.  You will NOT feel that bunched up feeling in your toes that you may get with a pair of good ol' Chuck's.  The shoes are way lighter than they look and are pretty comfortable right out of the box.  I can only imagine how great these will feel after breaking them in for a year.  They got the extra padding near the ankles and the cupping of the heel right also.  I have no doubt that I will purchase another pair when these finally tear apart.

I think this is a great bag in general . This bag does not provide any secure type locking system or rfid pockets so maybe not ideal for travel. Easily fits more than you can imagine including a tablet but there is no padding ( might make it heavier). If you overload, although the wide strap helps, you might want to buy those wrap cushions designed for backpacks. Front strap pocket ok but too small for a phone or oversized sunglasses. Maybe could be used for a credit card wallet.

What I liked:
-Multi pockets
-lightweight
-water resistance
-attractive
-wide adjustable strap
-good size without being too small or large
-water bottle pocket ( although very tight squeeze for 16 oz bottle)
-side pocket for sunglasses

What could be improved:
-needs to have rfid pockets and maybe some toggle closure for more security.
-Zippers don't always glide easily so not sure about longevity
-Lining in middle pocket is taller than zipper so gets caught every time ( maybe I got a defective one)
- have at least one side zip pocket instead of all top entry ( slings twist around so you can easily access and most have a side entry pocket which makes it easy to leave the bag on your body while you access a pocket)
-would be nice if large pocket had a divider for more organization.
-Needs some updating for a quick access phone pocket that also fits larger phones (like the hidden quick grab ones that most of the travelon bags have)
-Wish strap could be used in either direction

Be aware that the upper straps on many of the Arizona sandals are NOT real leather, they are called Birko-Flor, which is a synthetic with a fuzzy fabric backing.  Amazon does not specifically state Birko-Flor next to each color name. The description at the bottom of the page adds to the confusion because it is the same description for ALL the colors on their website, regardless of the strap material. While a few colors have the word "leather" next to the color name, and some others state Birko-Flor, the MAJORITY of colors say nothing at all. I assumed that if it didn't specifically state Birko-Flor in the color name, it was real leather. Not so! I ordered the Ice Pearl color and it is synthetic. You have no way of knowing this until you get it at home and it states so on the shoe box. Amazon should clearly state which colors are real leather uppers and which are Birko-Flor, so customers know what they will be getting. I am disappointed at Amazon for not being clear in their description,and at The Birkenstock company for compromising the sandal quality by producing them with an inferior synthetic material in the first place. If the rationale was to make them more comfortable by having a soft fabric backing next to the skin, this could still have been achieved with real leather on top and fabric on the back. I was eagerly awaiting these sandals, and now have to return them. At $110, I expect real leather, not "pleather".

The Boulder X was my second choice for an approach shoe. I initially bought 5.10 Guide Tennies, but the first pair was too big and when I went down a half size they were too small. So I jumped brands. I ordered both the Boulder X and the Mix (also La Sportiva). I was really impressed with the fit of both shoes (having European half sizes basically gives them American quarter sizes). The heel was snug and I had no slippage (something lacking in the 5.10s). The Boulder X has a lace around the heel that really snugs things up.

My overall impression of the Boulder X was that it was rugged. It has a nice looking edging zone at the front of the toe. The lugs were nobby and looked like they would be good for hiking. There is a lot of lacing, which is both good and bad since they are a pain to get on and off but there is a lot of customization to fitting. The rubber seemed pretty sticky, picking up plenty of dog hair as I tested them out around the house. They definitely look and feel more like a hiking shoe than a climbing shoe. They are a lot stiffer and have a lot more support than a climbing shoe or more minimalist approach shoe. Just testing them out in the house I noticed they were quite warm

While I liked the Boulder X I did end up sending them back in favor of the Mix. The Mix is much lighter and more flexible. The rubber seemed softer and stickier. The trade off is in support and durability. I feel like the Boulder would probably last longer and perform better on longer hikes. But currently most of our approaches are less than an hour, so I opted for the more comfortable of the two shoes. But if I find myself doing longer approaches the Boulder X is top on my list.

I have yet to put them to use in the field so I can't say 100% how much I like or dislike them, but have looked at all the major brands of gaiters as I have needed to replace a pair that is no longer made (which I loved) - and these are the ones I have decided I like the best. I use these for hunting elk in Colorado (requires protection from snow, mud, and moisture) so the fit has to be just right and I don't want sag as I walk otherwise the noise will kill me. Plus I am really picky about my gear. From wearing these around the house I believe they are the best option for what is out there today. OR Expedition Gaiters were significantly noiser, generally disappointed with the Black Diamond ones, and it was a split decision between these and the Kenetrek Gaiters (which are the only ones I can say are "designed for hunting"). I chose these over Kenetrek because 1) some guys has said the snow would "ball up" on the softer Kenetrek fabric and 2) the top clasp on the Kenetrek is not heavy duty and I could see it breaking in the field.
Fit is good on these but I did order a size down as I read other reports that they did run a bit big - I wear a size 10.5 mountaineering boot and I ordered a Medium for a good fit (MH Size chart said I should order a Large). Definitely durable/well made, all MH stuff is and if anything does break I know the company will 100% stand behind it. I read some reviews saying the top clasp was "tough to adjust", which it is but it is designed to be adjusted 1 time and then you don't touch it - and it doesn't move on you. For that reason I like it. Plus the little bit of elastic in the back helps a snug fit on the leg as well as to keep that top closure snug.
If they don't perform as I hope I will update this posting.

Let me start off being clear as to what I do with work boots such as these. I work on a farm in Kansas and the conditions here are unpredictable and can be harsh. This is the main reason I went with this specific boot. I needed something that was durable, water-proof, comfortable and well built. Well, let me explain where the other two stars went. They are truly water-proof, no doubt about that. If that is a concern then rest easy, my feet stayed dry no matter how saturated these boots got! Comfort was a lil on the larger side of the 10.5D that i wear so I slapped some Dr. Scholl's work inserts in and they snugged right up. I would recommend a half size smaller or stop by a store and fit a few to be sure. The composite toe is a thing of beauty! It is light weight yet held up to cattle stepping on my toes and all while suffering no comfort loss. Now we get to the bad parts of the boot. I purchased these on April 6th and a little over a month ago the rubber sole on the tip of my right toe split horizontally. I figured no big deal, little glue and all is well, that worked for two days. Either way it split on a mold seam and is a hazard and a nuisance. Next the glue holding the leather to the sole has started releasing just behind my big toe on the right boot. the leather is peeling away form the rubber sole and is just a case of poor manufacturing. The same separation is happening on the left boot's outside arch. This is a smaller separation but the other started small and grew quickly. I don't abuse my boots and keep them clean and oiled often. So what I am getting at is it was the adhesive Justin Boots used in making these boots and not the leather that has failed. Very disappointed in this product, maybe I got a fluke, maybe they are all built this shoddy, but i don't feel they were worth $160.00+ and probably wont purchase another pair.

I bought these when they came on sale, mostly on the strength of the extremely positive reviews. I wish I'd seen them in person first. One reviewer said they had great arch support. You can tell from the picture there is zero arch support. One review said they didn't flop when you walk, which sounded far too good to be true for a flip flop and most certainly was. These flop with the best of them. Several people said they could walk around in these all day with complete comfort, and I don't agree with that either.

Maybe if you're used to $2 Old Navy flip flops you'd like these. They'd be a step up from those, for sure, but overall these particular Skechers struck me as a cheap plastic shoe like the kind you buy at Payless (where I used to work.) One reviewer said she could "dress them up" by wearing something other than shorts, and I don't agree that they look dressy enough to wear to, say, dinner. They had a strong off-gas smell when I opened the box, and there is nothing to absorb sweat in the bottom. Great if you wear them to the pool, but if you're wearing them to walk around on a hot day (like summer) you'll be slipping and sliding if you sweat even the tiniest bit. Gross. Just a cheap shoe, out of many cheap summer shoes you could buy and probably already have a pair or two, like we all do. Just don't pay full price.

By the way, I normally wear a 7 to 7.5 in sandals, but I bought an 8 based on what some reviewers suggested and that was the right size for me so the reviews were right on the money there. Also, as many reviewers said, the straps thankfully aren't a hard plastic like you see in even cheaper sandals. They don't cut into your toes and feet. That's not enough for me to keep these, though.

I've been running for years. Half marathons are what I enjoy. My favorite shoes for several years were Mizuno Nirvanas, which are unfortunately discontinued now. I've tried Mizuno Inspires, Asics Kayanos, and Brooks Adrenalines trying to find that next best shoe.

As a runner well into my 40s, I like the idea of something with more cushioning that the Hokas provide. However, I overpronate and a support shoe works best for me. Hoka never had that before the Constant.

I have a love-hate relationship with these shoes.

Things I love:
- The ride and cushioning is fantastic. My knees, hips, and back don't seem to get as beat up on longer runs when I'm wearing these.
- The low heel-toe drop makes my muscles work differently. I like it, but it does take a little getting used to.

What I don't love:
- Blisters. I get blisters on the outside of both big toes. Tried a 10.5 and it was too little. Went to an 11 and still get them, although not as bad. This has never been a problem in other shoes. Even my best socks and generous body glide on the offending area is not enough to stave off the blisters. The hot spots show up at 3-4 miles. Furthest I've dared run with these is 6 miles.

I wish they worked for me. I want them to work. I love the ride, but just can't deal with the blisters. My experiment with Hokas has been a failure, but your mileage may vary.

The left shoe is very comfortable but the right shoe was made wrong and I can't wear it more than a minute. I measured the thong that goes between your toes from the inside edge of the shoe to the thong and the right shoe thong measures 1/8" to the right  from the thong on the left shoe, making the right shoe unbearable to wear. Wanting to try the closest thing in the Mizuno line to the Cursoris, and having read that the toe-box was wide in the Hitogami, I wrongly thought these would fit similarly to the Cursoris. Definitely pay attention to the shoe fitting application amazon has begun using to check fit before ordering. I ended up ordering these a half size too small. According to the shoe fitter the foot-bed exactly matches the size 12 asics I've owned. Because the shoe was too small for me to run in, I can only give superficial information on the shoe itself.

The materials and build quality is what I expect from Mizuno. The laces are a bit strange: they seem stiff and inflexible and appear designed not to slip between eyelets. I'm not sure how this would have worked out for me, as I rely on the slippage to fine tune lace adjustments while running. I either tighten or loosen the lace and let the change work down to the bottom of the lace while moving in the shoe. I can't tell how well these would do that, but the stiffness and surface roughness give me pause.

Adidas Men's Superstar 3g Slide Sandals are, by comparison to other regular sandals, high quality materials, very well made (not excellent), and feels great to have on. Considering the pros and cons for this particular design, the pros are;
1. These are great pair of sandals to wear around the house, there are very comfortable at the bottom of the feet, as well as at the top strap.
2. The materials feels premium, I haven't seen or experienced any defect on these sandals except the logo and other prints on the feet pad rubbed off after 3 weeks of usage.
3. The design is beautiful, just by looking at it side by side with other sandals. I'm proud of wearing them around at the public pool, gym, and to the grocery store without feeling ashamed.
4. The cushion feels wonderful at THE BOTTOM of the feet when it is NOT wet.
5. Durable even after several washes in the washing machine.
The con
1. I can not emphasize on this enough!!! It is a terrible sandals to wear to take a shower!!! The foam absorbs water and it becomes unbearably annoying when walking around with soaked sandals around the house.
2. It will smell terrible, like a damped sock, if you wear them in the shower. The smell is hard to get rid of even if you wash them in the washer.
3. During hot weather, if you have sweaty feet, this sandals will be unwearable because the foam will generate heat around the top strap (yes, the top strap is padded). The padded strap is good for comfort when walking around but terrible if it is humid.

Overall, I'll give it 3 and half stars out of five. Despite Adidas the good intension of providing great comfort with the cushions and pads to make this sandals feels great, it is those same things that also set these sandals back, specifically when they are wet or when it is humid.

This will be a slightly emotional review because once upon a time I really, really LOVED these shoes. I've probably had at least 10 pairs over the years. I'd worn them around the world, London, Hong Kong, and then came the new pair and my trip to Japan ... and the failure. Now I had noticed the pair before this one wasn't up to quite the same quality. They didn't seem to last as long and like others who have reviewed this shoe the sole split in the end and I had to toss them. But I was in denial. They weren't quite as good but they were still my beloved Newports so I blindly ordered another pair.

The pair arrived promptly (thanks to Prime!) and I put them right on. They seemed even worse than the last pair. However, we've been together so long - I just wasn't ready to admit Newport had changed. Then in Japan I had to admit it - it was time for me to say goodbye to Newport. Yes, on my wonderful honeymoon, to the amazing land of Japan I had a full shoe blow out. While out seeing the sites it started to rain. No problem, I thought, we have rain coats and an umbrella. But the more we walked the more my feet felt soaked. Odd, I though, these shoes are pretty solid. I sat down and realized BOTH SOLES HAD CRACKED. Both. At. the. same. time! (photos provided) So cutting the day short we returned to our hotel room and I said my final goodbye to my Newports and into the trash they went. I sat, dried my feet, toasted what Newports once were and vowed to never be fooled by Eastland again - no more Newports!

My advice, don't get these. Eastland has decided to stop investing in the relationship. Find someone better, there's plenty of shoes in the sea.e. Eastland has decided to stop investing in the relationship. Find someone better, there's plenty of shoes in the sea.

Disclaimer: I have only had these shoes two days, but I absolutely love them. As others have said, there is no break-in. They came out of the box feeling like they were molded to my feet. I've worn them steadily preparing for a trip to Yellowstone and have had no areas of rub or chafe.
Sizing: the guy in the store told me to go up a half-size, and he was right. Both my husband and I felt our standard shoe size was too tight. I am normally a 7.5. The 8 felt just right, but I need orthotic arch supports. I went up another half-size to accommodate the arch supports and they fit perfectly. Usually I will find the arch supports raises the top of my foot too high and it rubs -- but not in these. Amazed there is no pressure there, no rubbing. My husband tried a half-size up. The length was good but width felt tight. Not all of the models offer Wide yet.
Based on the mid feeling so well broken-in out of the box I am doing a 2nd-day to get the same shoe in low for normal wear on the trip. I would never normally consider ordering a shoe 10 days ahead of a trip, but I am really confident these will surpass my current broken-in day shoes in spades!
One other comment. A big local independent outfitter has just begun carrying these. They told me a man came in and tried on every single hiking boot they have (~ 20 models) and walked all over the mall in each. He decided on the Oboz. They are very impressed and the kid who waited on me told me he couldn't wait until he could get a pair.

Buying shoes online is one of the hardest things you can do which is why I hardly ever do it. Let me explain why this is a really dumb idea. 1) People now have to buy the next larger size which will still use the larger amount of material and 2) People like me will just give up buying shoes online out of frustration. I just want a pair of shoes. I don't want repeated trips to the UPS store! I see lots of shoes online that I would like to buy but most of the time I think, "Well it's probably not going to fit" so I don't bother. Who wants to keep shipping shoes back and forth? I'm a size 9 (occasionally a half-size down or up) over-pronator with a wide forefoot and an average heel, so I look for stability, motion control, and arch support in a running shoe in a wide size (D).  I've had good experiences with some men's Asics in a medium width, but I liked the looks of this women's shoe so much that I decided to try it.  I do love the looks, but alas, the D size isn't a true wide, which I can usually wear:  while the size-9 length of these fits me well, both the toe box and midsection are so narrow that the shoe is too snug even with thin socks.  They are extremely breathable because they're mesh, but because of that I'm not sure they'd stretch enough even with a professional stretcher to be wearable with crew socks, and they'd be quite uncomfortable to work out in.  Correction:  I got these in a size 9.5.  So even though I'm normally a size 9, that would be way too tight in this shoe.  Also, perhaps because they're all-mesh, they don't offer as much stability and cushioning as most of the Asics I've had, which is surprising, considering that on another website the manufacturers says they're "Built for mild to moderate overpronator who requires a blend of enhanced cushioning and stability."  I didn't notice either one.  I would have loved to be able to keep these shoes, but I'll have to return them and either go back to wearing men's sneakers or find something in a true wide.  PROS: Beautiful shoe, good price, looks great if you can wear it. CONS:  Not a true wide even if labeled "D"; less cushioning and compensation for pronation than some descriptions indicate.

I guess I am too naive about women's shoes. After spending hours in a shoe warehouse looking for ANY cross-trainers in wide widths and leaving with no options, I did some research online, then came to Amazon where I spent even more hours reading reviews. I purchased four pairs of cross-trainers and not a single one worked. Learn from my mistakes.

As a reference, my bigger foot (left) is 9.5" from big toe to heel, the ball is the widest part of my foot at just over 4" and my heel is 2.5" wide. I typically wear a size 7.5. I have a bunion on my left foot, very high arches, and my pinkie toes are a bit hammertoed from years in ill fitting high heels. I am making a concerted effort to wear better shoes, even if it costs me more. Unfortunately shoemakers refuse to recognize women with foot widths over 3". I ordered all these shoes in 7.5 D because I didn't see them any wider. That may have changed by the time you are reading this. Zappos tells me I should have ordered a size 8. Take my review for what it is: my one-time opinion.

Pair 1: NB 797 7.5 D. As I took these out of the box I knew they were doomed. Seriously, these don't look like "wide" shoes at all, I wish I'd gotten the "normal" B width to compare. This must be a joke, right? After putting them on I noticed what is a constant problem for me. The toe box of the shoe is too narrow, while the heel/opening is gargantuan. Pinkie toes are pinched and bunion is sensitive. Length is also cutting it close, like half a thumb left up front. Seems low on the sides but that's probably for the lateral movement. Also, the insole seems to be floating in the shoe. It's not too narrow, it's just not glued down so it seems like it might keep coming out every time I take the shoe on and off.

Pair 2: NB 711 7.5 D. These are the cutest in my opinion. I seriously want these to work. But they look so narrow. What. the. heck. Ah, super lightweight, not a lot of seams, narrower heel for sure. Also less padded around the shoe opening than #1. After leaving it on for just a few minutes, my bunion is throbbing slightly. That does not bode well. Length is cutting it close. If this came in an 8 4E, it would be a keeper.

Pair 3: NB 20 Minimus 7.5 D. These are definitely the least appealing to me. I mean they aren't bright white, but not my cup of tea. Anyway. Definitely the widest of the bunch. Ample room on the outside of the foot, it's weird, they sort of lean in, in a way that makes my bunion feel the bottom seam of the shoe. So it's not the pressure from the top or side that is irritating it, it's the lip of the shoe insert. Oh, there's no insert. Well I guess just where the upper and lower parts of the shoe meet. Looking at it you would be able to tell what I'm talking about; it definitely leans. The sides and back come up a little higher on the ankle, still not above the outer fibula bone-end, or the interior navicular bone-bump, so I like it more. I'm also clearly a dum-dum for ordering a 7.5. Still, this feels the best so far except for lean and it's effect on my bunion. Is the lean important to "minimal" shoes? Also, the box mentions running, which is not what I'm interested in. The listing online says cross-trainer.

Pair 4: Asics Gel Unifire 7.5 D. These are also a joke. The leather detail work on the uppers irritate my bunion from the start. The toe box is too narrow for the rest of my digits too. Actually the length on this seems better, but that is the only thing that is okay with this shoe. It feels nicely padded, I'll give it that. A big nope, all in all.

So all four of these go back, what a delight. This isn't a waste of my money and time at all, nooooo. I have now ordered NB Mens 623s and 608 in both 2E and 4E. I've also ordered from Zappos the Asics Gel 180 in 2E for women and the Asics Gel Acclaim in 2E for men. I think the biggest problem is Amazon's lack of selection (not even color-wise, just pure options!) at wide widths, and potentially no standardization of sizes, just like clothes. Are wide shoes just the unicorn of footwear or does Amazon just not care?

UPDATED 7/15/15: I had originally rated these as 4 stars, but have had to change it to 2. I am wearing these shoes for the second time and am only a few hours into wearing them and am so disappointed that the loop that holds the strap down at the buckle just completely fell apart so now the strap is winging out with nothing to keep it down. ORIGINAL REVIEW: These shoes are great - so pretty and very comfortable! I feel like I have a pretty normal foot and the actual SHOE fits fine - what is a little on the large side though is the straps that go across the top of the foot. I'm wearing the buckle on the very last hole and feel like I will probably need to have my husband add another one as they stretch out. But you can see that the strap across the toes and over the bridge of the foot is not adjustable, so it fits somewhat loose on me. It doesn't make any difference in the wear - I did just fine in them, but I do need to stay aware so my ankle doesn't accidentally twist if my foot does slip because the straps don't fit tight.  On the other hand, the fact that the straps aren't tight meant that even at the end of a 10-hour workday and the regular swelling that you go through during a day, they still felt great at the end of the day and had no pinching or rubbing anywhere.  Overall, I love the shoes and will definitely get a lot of great wear from them! If you have wider or or fuller feet, you should be just fine ordering your normal size.

I've had great luck with these shoes, BUT I tried them on in store before ordering and found that I had to order about 1.5 sizes above my typical running shoe. These are a great trail shoe with a minimalist feel (light and flexible, low heel-toe drop, etc.) but maintains enough cushion for me to run ultra distance. I ran a mountainous 50k and had zero issues with them. The only issue I've had was with my first pair. I learned after a long run that I had to trim the sole insert due to rubbing under my arch. Likely, this was not an issue with the shoe itself, but an issue with how my arch sat on the arch. I would highly recommend to those looking for a lightweight, responsive, but sturdy feeling trail shoe. They do tend to split around the crease of the ball of your foot, others have complained about this, but it doesn't affect anything other than cosmetics. They're inexpensive compared to other ultra shoes, so worth it to me.

I had ordered a different style before this pair (Fila Skele-Toes Bay Runner 3 Lighted Sandal (Toddler/Little Kid/Big Kid),Monument/Castlerock/Hot Pink,12 M US Little Kid) and had to return them because they were faaaaaar too narrow for my daughter's foot. She had yet a different style last year (Fila Skele-Toes Bay Runner 3 Lighted Sandal (Toddler/Little Kid/Big Kid),Dazzling Blue/Lime Punch/Hot Pink,1 M US Little Kid) that were snug, as these types of shoes should be, and were a bit of a chore to get on. They did fit though. They lasted as long as it takes for a child to wear holes in them by dragging their feet to stop themselves on a swing...

All-in-all, I will continue to buy Skele Toes more because my daughter likes them than them being a good shoe for kids. You need to know that fit is going to run small and can vary greatly depending on the style of shoe you choose. It can be a wrestling match to get your child's foot into them.

I would suggest that buying them from a third-party seller, or even through Amazon, will run you the risk of receiving obviously worn returned items or complete knock-offs.

They will likely not last any longer than your average kid's shoe with regular use, especially due to hard tugging to get them on pulling at the seams and glue, and the thinness of the uppers of some of the styles.

This is Susan's son, first off; the shoes were purchased for me, so I felt it made sense for me to write the review. And, as a bit of a forewarning, I'm in the process of sending these back as I type this review because these shoes just did not work for me at all.

I found these in a local shoe store and really liked them when I tried them on, particularly the lightweight feel, but they didn't have a size that fit well, so we bought them on Amazon a half-size up later that day. They arrived August 12 and I've worn them repeatedly in the three days since. However, after wearing them and being on my feet for a few hours at a time, I've come to the conclusion that these shoes would only work for a relatively small niche of people; that is, people with narrow feet who live in cooler climates.

Below the mesh upper is another, relatively thick layer of fabric that negates any breathability the mesh upper might confer to the foot; add to this the synthetic covering of the memory foam insole and you have a recipe for a shoe that retains heat very well. While this may be a blessing in colder weather, in Texas heat, it's a veritable nightmare for your feet as, after less than an hour, your feet will be hot and sweaty and you'll be wanting to remove the shoes with all haste.

Normally, I love Skechers' memory foam insole, as my Avillos have it and I wore those until the insole started coming apart at the seams and flaking off (I got a good several years' use out of them, so I'd say I got my money's worth; they're still functional even now), but with the way the insole is designed on these Persistents, if you have anything but a very narrow foot or tend to walk on the outer edge of your foot, the memory foam insole might as well be nonexistent. I took a measurement and, at the arch of the foot on a size 11, the insole measures a measly 2 inches in width; for comparison, my own foot at the same spot is 3.5 inches wide. Granted, I have a wide foot, so that's not the best comparison, but I've generally found with Skechers that I can reliably go up a half-size if a wide is not available (and it wasn't in these in the color we bought) and be perfectly comfortable. Not so this time. I found the inside half of my foot was resting off the edge of the insole, which was not the most comfortable experience.

Nevertheless, these shoes DO have some good points. I said this shoe was a good concept with a less than stellar execution and I meant it. The idea of a lightweight, flexible, and casual slip-on shoe that you could wear with most anything is a very attractive one and in those respects, it actually succeeds. Skechers states on their website that a Men's 9 weighs about 6 or 7.5oz (I can't remember exactly) and I wouldn't be surprised if the 11 weighed more than 8-9oz; they are very flexible and the upper has a good amount of give that I've only found surpassed by Converse All-Stars High Tops. And they are also casual, looking good with shorts or jeans or cargo pants, though whether or not they would actually go with anything is dependent on color (the black or charcoal, I think, would work with just about any outfit, the latter especially).

However, because of the shortcomings of the stifling upper and the too narrow insole, the places you actually want a shoe to succeed (particularly a walking shoe), these fall far short of what I was hoping for them to be.so that's not the best comparison, but I've generally found with Skechers that I can reliably go up a half-size if a wide is not available (and it wasn't in these in the color we bought) and be perfectly comfortable. Here's some background on me: I have a wide forefoot and a narrow heel. I have a tendency to supinate in my natural gait. My use for these shoes was for general training indoors between weights, cardio, and infrequent classes. When I realized my old shoes (also New Balance) were no longer cutting it, I contacted New Balance support for suggestions, and this was a recommendation based on my needs. I purchased these in my usual 8's in a wide - same as my last pair of New Balance shoes. These shoes offer cushion, and the foam has great responsiveness. At first, it feels like walking on air. Going from a studier shoe to the 822v2 was a completely different experience -- one I very much enjoyed.  After a few sets of lunges and squats, I noticed the fatal flaw in these shoes when my feet were inexplicably unsteady. With my narrow heel, this shoe offers no support and stability at the back of the shoe. The heel is basically all foam padding without any structure. This caused a lot of slippage. After switching to cardio, I noticed the heel bunching up at the bottom where the heel meets the sole of the shoe. I tried lacing them tighter and with different lacing patterns to keep my heel in place, which only caused my foot to go numb towards the outside metatarsals.  I discussed this with my chiropractor, who is also a fitness junkie. UPDATE: I'm coming back a short time later to say these shoes are truly a disappointment. I used to love the New Balance brand, but these are a joke. Shagwear designs some of the cutest wallets out there. Prefer an eye-catching design over a $90 metal name-brand label on a tired print? Then these may be for you.

Over the past five years, I have owned three Shagwear wallets (their Canadian flag/maple leaf, the travel passport style, and a floral one). They are conversation starters wherever I go. People really want to know the story behind a stylized Canada goose or whether that's the Canadian flag on the back of my wallet. Yes, yes it is. Am I Canadian? Yes, I am. No, I don't know your cousin Bob in Toronto but let's talk about health care now.

Shagwear would earn more points if they made their wallets to last more than a year. I'm not really that hard. I do not whip out wads of cash or pile in loonies and toonies by the dozen. Nor do I carry 72 loyalty cards because I don't think I can name 72 Canadian stores, let alone shop in that many. Unfortunately the seams on their wallets were sewn by gophers in Albertan mountain camps, pressed down by little paws, and no actual use of string or thread appears to meld the sides. The seams split easily when aggressively used -- say, by slipping your debit card into a slot once a day. It tears or wears away at the worst spots, right where cards line up or along the middle seam separating the cash pocket. Argh.

Be gentle with zippers that tender hands have sewn in because they aren't made for a lot of wear and tear. Or rip and zip. They tend to pull away at one end and there's no way to really secure the zipper once it comes away.

Four years ago, I purchased this Merrell shoe from a local retailer and was pleased with the fit and durability. This old pair is starting to wear, but the sole remains intact and attached to upper shoe body. With this good experience, I decided to buy a second pair online through Amazon. Price was about the same as local retailer, or maybe even slightly higher. The shoes arrived on schedule, new, and fit as expected.

However, although this pair is 6 months old, the sole is separating from the shoe body. The gap is about 2 inches long and looks as if insufficient glue (or poor quality glue) was used to attach sole to upper shoe body. I've had to inject glue into the gap to keep sole from further separation.
I like the Merrell brand, but now wondering about their manufacturing quality control. Maybe these shoes are 'seconds' (but not marked or advertised as such). Maybe these are not Merrell's, but instead a knock off copy. Don't know.

I've owned a couple pair of the Classic Crocs and found them amongst the most comfortable shoes I've ever owned - while the tread is unworn. As it wears, it becomes more slippery when wet. I bought the Bistro Clog because its sole solves the possible hazard. However, this pair is the first non-vented Croc I've gotten. I found, when wearing the shoe indoors exclusively,  that I had water build up from body heat. I needed to dry the shoes twice during the time I wore them. I was wearing socks for medical reasons, and the wicking of the fabric became an issue. I'll never get an unvented Croc again. However, the main reason I write is about the fact that the two shoes were NOT the same size. The opening to the left foot was a full 1/4 inch larger than the right foot. Sitting side by side they looked like two different sizes - which of course they weren't as they are molded. It is the opening that is a quarter inch different - which in my case makes the foot slide too much. I assume each foot is molded from a different mold. I'm not clear how that great a variation can happen, but it is enough to make the left "too large" for me as it produces too sloppy a fit. Crocs are made in different places. These say "made in Vietnam". The Classics I'm wearing as I write this were made in Mexico; they're fine and fit well, but they have the traditional sole that becomes very slippery in time - not so safe for these old bones.

I have bought and worn 4 pair of these MW411 walking shoes.  I love the fit and feel. My concern is I don't get full use out of these shoes due to poor bonding of the glue between the sole and shoe body.  Every single pair has failed in the exact same way.  The bottom separates from the body at/near the toe area then the separation gradually gets worse until the whole sole is separated down to the middle of my foot.  At that point, I throw them away and buy another pair.  I haven't tried gluing the sole back to the body as I've seen in other reviews.  The shoes fail at about the 4-5 month point for me.  Given my walking habits, that's perhaps 500 to 600 miles walked.  So I can't fault the shoe entirely.  That's a lot of miles!  But I do think New Balance should recognize this defect and use better glue.  I'd like to wear a hole in a pair or have the sole wear thin just once instead of watching what looks like a perfectly good pair of shoes come unglued! I bought a pair of these boots in early 2012 from a local vendor....so this is a post-three year review. They were the black leather ones. I've worn them through several Boston winters and the uppers held up perfectly fine as long as you take care of them....salt in particular will mess up leather...even the nicest of leathers....so some care/upkeep is needed on these...but again that goes for all nice things. The only real (minor) issue with the leather is that the dye is not very deep...minor scrapes on black (or I imagine other off-natural colors) immediately shows and only shoe polish of the right color takes care of it.

The laces that shipped with broke after a year, so I replaced them with more durable ones. Meh no biggie.

The original heel was junk and wore out exceedingly quick....this is sort of expected since I walk five miles a day or so routinely on concrete, but was still sorta weird how quick it went....I had it replaced at the four month mark. What was a bit more disappointing was that the outsole went bad really quickly. In particular the outsole on these did not do well with any sort of moisture...be it from a rainy fall/spring or winter. Now I know these are "dress boots", but all it took was a few rainy days of walking into work on concrete to cause legit wear to the outsole... (and yes I do dry my boots every night after I wear them...)Thankfully I monitored this and then went and got rubber outsoles put on the boots after the first six months. They look fine...better I'd say actually and have been far more durable....basically they've lasted ~3 times as long as the original outsole...same with the second heel I got...although I'll need to be replacing that again soon too.

The uppers on these have been fantastic and have broken in very nicely...no complaints there. I have probably walked 1000 miles in these things, albeit with different heels and outsoles based on what they shipped with. I am considering getting another pair in a different color, but I just wish they'd ship these things with a more practical heel and outsole rather than keep the ones that are on now. I'd even bet the things would be slightly cheaper since you'd be using rubber rather than whatever leather/stuff they use now. This is the one thing preventing me from just buying another one....it'll cost ~$60 to refit these boots once I get them with a heel and outsole that will last and at that point I might as well just be shopping for a slightly better pair.

I tried out a second run wearing a thicker footie sock and felt the shoe rubbing at my heel... The left shoe laces are straight and the right shoe laces veer to the right. If you look closely at the picture I have posted, you can see the top right lace is almost diagonal and the top left lace is straight across (my ankles and feet are together in this photo). That was enough for me and I decided to return them. I wanted to like the shoes so bad because I LOVE the mizuno brand. This product, however, is NOT the same mizuno quality that is deserving of a $109.00 price tag. I don't believe these are real mizunos considering all of the trouble I've had with these shoes. As a runner, the quality and science behind a shoe is very very important to me. This just is not a comfortable shoe for running or anything to be honest. I just hit the one year mark wearing these boots. I am tempted to buy them again but not for the comfort factor. I still think this boot is the best looking steel toe work shoe I have seen and I've looked at a lot of them. Style and weight are the main reasons why I purchased it a year ago. Even though this is a higher topped shoe, it is considerably lighter than a Timberland low-top shoe I had previous to this one (The Titan).  And that is a contributing factor of why I would purchase it again this year. The other reason I am considering it again is durability. The stitching, leather and everything about it on the upper has held up well...really well. I think the sole has a little more wear on the heel than I would expect but it hasn't fallen apart, worn down so much that is smooth/slick, started "flapping" or anything like that. In other words, if the upper would get me a couple years, which I think it would, it is doubtful the sole would.  As far as comfort? These boots are not really comfortable. To be fair, there are very few shoes I find comfortable, so part of that is me and part of it is the shoe. There seemed to be a couple of hot spots in the foot bed. I knew this going in and knew I would need to put an orthotic in the boot—which I did—a $30.00 orthodtic. This made the comfort level tolerable.  Another thing to consider, depending on where you live is: This is a hot boot. I live in SW Florida, so hot boot is not necessarily a good thing. All waterproof work boots may be hot, I don't know. I know I appreciated the warmth of the boot this past winter but haven't been too fond of it this summer. As far as waterPROOF goes, I don't think so. It is very water resistant but not waterproof. I have spilled/poured water a couple of times right on the area where the tongue begins and got a wet-ish foot. I have no complaints with their waterproof claim, however,  when it comes to walking through puddles, wet grass, etc. They perform well there.  I get a boot allowance from work of $100.00 per year (or as needed). If I didn't get that, I doubt very much that I would have bought this boot, considering I have to add the orthodic just to make it comfortable. Again, some of this dissatisfaction is probably me. Will I buy it again? Probably not this year since I since I have a considerable amount of life left in them. I cleaned them up and oiled them yesterday and they still look pretty dang good. I think this year I will go with a Keen brand shoe that I tried and liked. It is a low shoe-type steel toe. I wanted to have a lighter shoe that I can wear the times when I have inside work and have these boots for rougher outside type work. I would say I work 50/50 inside/outside. If the Keens hold up well this year, I will probably buy these Dunhams again next year to try and maintain a couple pairs of shoes to switch off with. If they were more comfortable, lighter, cooler and closer to a hundred bucks, I would buy them right now!

In terms of looks, the color and finish of the cherry red leather is gorgeous. However, the design of the boot is not quite as nice as I had anticipated. My shoe size is generally a US women's size 9.5, which is not small. But the length of this boot makes it look as if I'm wearing clown shoes. It doesn't help that the rubber sole of the shoe sticks out pretty far from the shoe itself, making my foot look much bigger than it really is. Also, the toe of the shoe is fairly rounded, making this look more like a work boot than a fashion boot.

All in all, it's a well-constructed, good looking boot, but it is not very comfortable to wear and not a good choice for women with larger feet. I regret buying it.

I got these as a birthday gift this year, because I'd been trying to find a good dupe for Jeffrey Campbell's Lita boots. They arrived on time, new in the box and had never been worn. I promptly wore them to a wedding the same week and I was able to wear them all day, walk with ease (which is huge since I typically resemble Bambi learning to skate when I put on anything higher than my Chuck's) and was even able to walk in both grass and gravel. Walking on very smooth floors like tile or polished wood is hard though, you have GOT to add some grip tape to the soles of you don't have the time to break them in first. They are rediculously slippery on smooth surfaces. I put mine on and went out on the road and just paced for a while to get the soles good and scuffed, which really isn't so bad if you just call a friend or something to distract you while you do it. I have paired them with everything- skirts, dresses, jeans. You name it and these boots have matched it! I can't WAIT until fall because they look especially cute with a fluffy sweater :) Anybody looking for a fairly innexpensive Lita style boot that will hold up well, get these! A few small care tips- Don't throw out the stuffing or the dust sleeves when you get your boots. If you brush them off with a towel, re-stuff them, and re-bag them after you wear them, and store them in the original box, they will retain their form a lot better. If you don't, the suede will crease faster than usual and they won't look as good. Plus, suede can sometimes be a bitch to clean, so the dust ruffles and box keep everything out of harm's way. Just buy a roll of grip tape and some nice inserts for your arches and you'll be shocked at how long you can go in these.

It felt like the hinges would snap or the lenses would pop out anytime. I am extremely disappointed because I thought Amazon would not sell fakes but I am wrong.  At first, I was a bit afraid of ordering because after reading many reviews, it seems some frames were fake and problematic, but I thought I would take a chance anyways since there were so many great reviews. (However, now I question whether these reviews came because the buyer never owned an authentic pair of Ray Bans before to compare..). But the hinges on this squeaks so much, and the entire frame seems like it can break any minute!  As I never owned a pair of Ray Bans and to make sure I wasn't delusional, I went to a Sunglasses Hut in my local mall to compare the frame in store to the one I received (exact model), and none of their frames had this problem. They all felt different- much stronger and better made!  Overall, I strongly STRONGLY recommend others to not buy Ray Bans from Amazon and instead go to a store and buy it :( I know it seems a lot cheaper here, but the difference in quality is worth it, and most importantly you won't waste time and money returning a fake product like I am >:(.

When I first tried these on all I could think was "wow"! They are extremely cushiony feeling and as a heavier person who is trying to start running, I thought that might help lessen the impact on my joints. The price put me off a bit, so I decided to think on it. I went to my local running store (which is a farther drive) today to try them on again. I looked at them in comparison to a few other shoes and they felt by far the most cushioned. I jogged around the building briefly and they felt pretty good, so I went ahead and purchased them.

I took them out for their first walk/run this afternoon. At first they still felt good and I liked the cushioned feel. As I started running after a walking warm-up, I noticed my calves hurt - which is unusual. I kept my running intervals a bit shorter and walked more in between. By about 3/4 mile in, I noticed my feet were feeling almost pins and needles like they were getting ready to go numb. I've had this happen with cheap shoes before, but was not expecting it with these! Once that started, I slowed back to a walk longer and started paying more attention to how my feet were landing. I have a neutral stride and these were definitely making me land on the inside of my heel with my arch almost collapsing to the inside - basically making me over-pronate. I finished walking the 2 miles and only jogged a few strides here and there to test them more, and noticed that unlike my other running shoes (Saucony Ride) which have a nice breakover to roll me to my toe to push off again, these didn't have much breakover at all. It took a lot more effort to push off with every stride due to the excessive cushion. By the end of my 2 miles of mostly walking with intermittent jogging, my achilles was sore as well.

Though the cushion seems like it would be nice for someone who is new to running or on the heavier side, I can say that it did nothing but make me work harder. I took them back to my running store immediately and exchanged for the Brooks Glycerin 13, which are in the same category and same price and still feel good even if the cushioned feel isn't as evident from the first step. The Nimbus 17 might work for someone who naturally supinates, but was not at all what I was hoping it would be.tore immediately and exchanged for the Brooks Glycerin 13, which are in the same category and same price and still feel good even if the cushioned feel isn't as evident from the first step. So I haven't worn shoes like these since my Jr High School dancing days. I stayed away from them as an adult dancer, because I could remember hating how the heal would constantly slip around, making even simple steps a nightmare.  We are doing a show that unfortunately requires us to have Grecian style shoes.  After reading the reviews, I opted to order in my street shoe size.  When I tried them on, the length was perfect, but they were a little looser than I like (reintroducing my fear of the slip-off heal problem). I've since worn them several times to rehearsals and class.  There aren't nearly as bad as I remember!  After tightening the strap to it's tightest slot, I found I could dance without fear of heal slippage. They're comfortable, they look beautiful, and are adjustable to accommodate the width of your foot. I wouldn't order a half size smaller as I think that would be too short. My personal preference would still tend toward heal-less shoes, but if you need a elegant style shoe for performance, or like a heal on your dance shoe, these are certainly a good buy.

I usually wear 7M-7.5M in loafers, mocs, and find that the 7M (width: 3.25"; length: 9.5") in this style does not fit my wide feet well although the length is perfect. I've been wearing similar sandals since the late 60's -- first Ganter Fusstrainers, the best but no longer available, then Kenkoh, definitely a notch below in quality and comfort, but acceptable. 2. The soles fall apart quickly. My wife and I both wondered what I was tracking into the house until I examined a couple of pieces of detrius and realized that they were pieces of the soles of these sandals.

After trying a few different pairs on at the store, I decided to purchase these online. After less than a week of wearing them, I've decided to return them.

The quality of these sunglasses are great. They feel very well built and sturdy. However, the lenses are extremely HEAVY, thus they constantly would slide off of my nose. I could be sitting completely still in the car, and they would start sliding down. Obviously, this was annoying, as I was constantly having to adjust them.

I also found that the lenses would become smudged very easily. I don't do anything particularly arduous wearing my sunglasses, but I was constantly having to wipe them off.

The other minor issue I had with them was that they are very wide. I have a pretty large head, yet the arms barely hugged my head. When I would put these sunglasses on top of my head, they would fall off / down with minor movement.

I was satisfied with the quality - in some ways - of these sunglasses, and I'm sure they would work for some people. But, for the amount of money spent on these, and Persol's reputation, I was disappointed.

I love the looks of this bag and the size of it. The size is wonderful. Yesterday I went to a rally and I was able to fit in a water bottle, a book, a baggie full of snacks, my wallet and cosmetic case, a scarf in case it got chilly on the evening, and all of the smaller items that tend to end up in purses. There are many compartments to help organize everything, which I love. The reason this bag only got 3 stars instead of the 5 stars it deserves, is because of the straps. I got a backpack purse because I need to use it as a backpack. My shoulders start to ache when I use a regular strap. I get the convenience of having both, as I like to use a strap now and again for a short duration, such as when I am going from my car to the house.  The way it is set up now is that the strap is one long length and can be pulled up through the the two metal rings on each side to create one long strap. You pull it back down when you want the back pack option. This is where the issue is for me. When I put one of the straps on my shoulder, the entire length is pulled to that side. Then I have to struggle to get some of that length to the other side. During this process the strap becomes tangled and I have to struggle to untangle it and then tug and pull so that I have an equal length on both sides. It's aggravating to the point where if I am in a hurry, I won't want to use this purse.There needs to be something to lock each strap in one in place, such as snaps or velcro, or something, or to unlock it when you just want to use a single strap. As it is, I am going to have to jerry-rig something so I can continue to use it.

.5 Years ago these were 5 Star Sandals. An adhesive reformulation makes them a 1 Star for me given the price and longevity. To put it simply, new pairs of these sandals are glued together using a new, non-toxic water based formula of adhesive and they simply do not last like they used to. My sole delaminated just after two seasons of use. Now, I'm tough on shoes, which is why I went with Keen again, because my original Keen sandals lasted years and I simply replaced them when the sole was worn out, not falling off.

The new sandals lasted 1/3 the life of the original before the adhesive change. Great for the workers in the factories, bad for the wearer of the shoe, unless you don't mind buying a new $90 pair more often. I know I don't.

Keen was kind enough to reply to my letter of dissatisfaction with the comments concerning the new glue formula, and they said it happens in only 1.5% of the product line, calling it delamination. Guess my last two pairs happened to fall in that 1.5%.

They are covered against delaminating for 1 year, which is not very helpful, since the failure occurs the following season of hikes and kayaking! Too bad their warranty wasn't better.

If you have a cobbler in your city, maybe there is hope for a fix. I'll probably buy some glue to try to repair mine since there is nothing else wrong with them other than delaminated soles.

Update 10/15 - I've worn the boots for an entire day of shopping and while they were comfortable in the footbed, I had a little trouble with my left foot, little toe touching the side of the boot.  Now, this is not the fault of the boot, it's my weird foot.  the left foot is slightly larger than the right, so sometimes it's a little bit of a problem.  I stretched out the left boot and it seems better.  These are comfortable boots with excellent arch support.  They are well made and sturdy.  The rocker outer sole is great for those who have foot problems.  I'm hoping the left foot will stretch out a bit over time like my Naot Primrose shoes did.  Overall, good comfortable shoes, at a decent price.

Ok, I'm giving these boots four stars because I love them but acknowledge that better boots exist. There is a caveat here: they are four star boots for GARRISON use, for field use I'd give them two or three stars. I've had them for over six months now, which I think is a reasonably fair amount of time to have them and do a review.

I bought these boots specifically for my garrison desk job, and I was looking for a boot that would be light and airy but also 100% 670-1 approved for use. These boots looked pretty good. I'd never bought boots off the internet but the price difference was about 40$ cheaper than MCSS prices so I took a chance. It worked out pretty well: these boots were everything I wanted for a garrison boot. Comfortable for long periods of time, they don't get crazy sweaty and stinky when you're at a desk, they keep a nice neat appearance without a lot of fuss, and a good fit and feel overall.

HOWEVER, I recently took the Air Assault 10 day class and wore these boots out in the field. My opinion of these boots is completely different in a field setting. First, these boots do not have a lot of arch support. My feet are pretty flat, which is irrelevant when you're at a desk but extremely relevant when you're on your feet 12+ hours straight during a day. The lack of support really killed my feet during the 10 day class. Long ruck marches are the same story, that lightness and comfort that is desirable at a desk translates into a lack of support during a high speed, high sweat three hour/12 mile ruck march. If you are going to be out in the field doing real soldier hooah stuff this probably isn't going to be the boot for you. Having said that, these boots are still better in the field than the standard army boot, which is heavy and uncomfortable (at least to me) even when broken in. I also took these boots up a nice hike up Guadalupe Mt in Texas. Same story there, I wish I had a boot with a little more support for that hike. All things considered though, the boot stood up to the hikes and rucks well and I've really inflicted a good hard fun summer on these boots. They've stood the test pretty well. Before these I had a pair of Bates that were the opposite, great field boots but uncomfortable when at a desk for long periods.

As for durability, I have had no issues with these boots. Even during hard ruck marches everything on the boot is solid and sturdy, not eyelets have fallen off and no leather seams and stitching has pulled out. I try to take care of my boots.

All in all a really good boot if you are in garrison and standing up in them less than two hours a day or so. Don't think this is a bad review, I love these boots and would recommend them to a friend/buy them again. Just not as a field boot, get something a little more field oriented.ke. These shoes barely miss the mark for 5 stars only because I had a pair of LunarGlide 5s that I absolutely loved and were more comfortable. I've also noticed some tearing along the toes after just about 50 miles of running.

First of all the good parts. These shoes do provide fantastic arch support for flat feet (mine are very flat). I run three 10Ks a week and I'm running some of best times yet (sub 55 minutes). Compare that to some "normal" running shoes that usually leave my feet absolutely numb and sidelined after about 1/2 hour. These shoes are also extremely light and air out quickly leaving very little moisture inside the shoe. I did not pay a lot of money for these at all. If I wear them outside, I can wear them all day and get more than 20K steps without blinking. Again, compare to a bad pair of shoes which basically guarantee I'll have to breaks or slow down to a crawl because of my flat feet.

The bad? As I mentioned, I had a pair of Nike LunarGlide 5s which I absolutely loved. I could run almost as fast in those shoes, they are almost as light and almost as cheap. What they did have more of is more cushioning. That means that the Asics are much harder on my foot after an outside run on pavement. I experienced heel bruising for the first time in these Asics. However, running on a treadmill, the Asics outperform my Nikes by far.

I wouldn't hesitate to recommend these shoes to runners with flat feet. Almost everything is perfect about these shoes except the cushioning, it's simply a very thinly cushioned shoe. However, if you run on a treadmill, track or path, you'll never notice the difference. These are my new go-to running pair, but the tiny rips in the fabric and my sore heels remind me there is room for improvement.
