Update first!

I brought these to Burning Man this year. Once I broke them out, I pretty much never wore anything else. They wipe clean, they held up beautifully in the alkaline dust, and they looked great. Everyone loved them.

I expected to need arch supports with them, but forgot to bring them. My feet held up all right, though they were sometimes very sore at the end of the day. I wouldn't want to wear these (or any other high-heeled shoe) on a daily basis year round, but for one week a year, they're fine.

On colder nights in the desert, I very much appreciated the extra width so I could wear extra-thick socks. Walking was no problem even in uneven footing or pockets of deep dust. Being 2" taller than usual didn't hurt, either! ;)

They also came in handy as part of the most ridiculous post-modern gladiator costume ever conceived, but that's neither here nor there.

I liked these so much that I think I'm going to order a second pair for clubbing. I left my original pair in our camp's year-round storage so I won't have to schlep them back and forth to the desert.

BTW, for travel, wrapping the buckles in plastic wrap did the job beautifully. I carried these shoes in my small carry-on bag along with a bunch of other random stuff, and they came through in perfect shape.

Back to the original review:

Full disclosure: I'm a guy, a dancer with the attendant high arches/flexible feet going on, and not a regular wearer of high-heeled shoes, chunky or otherwise. Thus, your mileage may vary significantly.

Onward! I bought these to wear with costumes and so forth, and I've never really owned anything similar, so I don't have much direct basis for comparison in terms of comfort and so forth. That said, I'll do my best.

Appearance and Materials:
These are simply really cute shoes. They look quite a bit better than I expected them to, in fact.

The color of the plastic stuff the shoes are made from is quite a bit darker than you might guess based on the picture, but as another reviewer mentioned, that's actually a good thing -- the shoes look great, and the sparkly stuff (which is safely contained inside the plastic) really shines.

The buckles do, as often mentioned, seem pretty cheesy. Considering that these shoes cost me fourteen bucks through Prime, I really can't complain about that. A previous reviewer posted an effective fix; I plan to employ that if the buckles give up the ghost. Also, if you're traveling with them packed, you might want to wrap some plastic wrap around the buckles to prevent them from snagging on things.

Be warned that the shoes might smell weird (mine did!) when they first arrive (ironically, mine are stamped "Natural Breeze" on the inside of the foot bed -- "I do not think that word means what you think that it means..."). Let them breathe for a couple of days, and the smell will dissipate.

Fit, Comfort, and Arch Support (or Complete Lack Thereof):
I wear a European size 40 - 41, so I ordered a US 10, and the fore-aft fit is spot on.

I was also pleased with the width, which is pretty good (in addition to being weird, my feet are narrow). I could use one more hole on the strap for barefoot wear or with really thin socks; with normal to thick socks, these would be about perfect.

I thought the plastic footbed would feel weird, but to be honest, I pretty much forgot about it after the first few minutes. I wore these around my house for several hours the day they arrived, then again the next day; they definitely behave as you might expect plastic shoes to behave when you accidentally dump water in them, but they're really basically pretty comfortable.

That said, unless you have really flat feet, do not expect these shoes to come anywhere near your arches. If you've got high arches, expectto feel contact at the heelbone and the balls of your feet and basically nowhere else. It may wind up looking a bit odd, but I'm definitely going to wear these with arch supports in them. I'd rather look a little weird than risk screwing up my feet.

As it stands, I can wear them fairly comfortably for a couple hours, then not terribly uncomfortably for a couple more, but eventually my feet start to hurt. I have pretty strong feet, so that's probably worth noting, but the closest thing I've worn in terms of heel-to-toe ratio has been a pair Iron Age work wellingtons with pretty substantial heels. That said, those were the most comfortable boots I ever owned, so that might also be worth noting.

Oh: walking in these is also no big deal. I expected to feel like I was going to fall over and kill myself, especially going down the stairs, but I didn't feel that way at all. Even if you tend, as I do, to a mid-foot stride, you'll probably be fine in these shoes. Performance may vary on uneven surfaces, though. I'll find out next week.

So there you have it. Overall, I'm quite pleased with these shoes -- they look nice, seem pretty well-made, and aren't horribly uncomfortable. Flimsy buckles and lack of arch support can be compensated for as needed.

I usually wear a size 12 in almost all shoes and sandals and since my feet are on the wide side, I usually order W whenever available.
But there was no WIDE option with these sandals, so I ordered 12 - and this is how it went:

LOOKS: good design, quality, material - just like in the photos.

FIT: My feet got it, but it was very narrow in a painful way, and it took long time (as in several weeks) to stretch and accommodate my foot. So if you have wide feet, you have be patient for a few weeks until it breaks in. If you have regular/narrow feet, then you're okay with this point.

SOLE: initially it was fantastic. The cushioning was amazing. However, it got compressed quickly and lost its elasticity. So after a few weeks, it was just an average OK sole just like any other unknown brand.

DURABILITY: the upper is just fine. A few threads flying here and there, but no biggie. The problem is with the sole, which is made of soft/weak rubber. It just wears out so quickly (in addition to losing its elasticity and compress-ability as mentioned before). This wearing out of the sole made it look less than what you'd like to wear in a decent outing. So I ended up wearing this for grocery shopping or for running errands on my own.

If these sandals had a different kind of sole, I would've bought many more. Everything else is just fine or perfect.

These are a great design idea, with a couple of flaws. I put over 1,000 miles on a set of regular Freeriders (XC, DH, Enduro), so I was pretty excited to try these because of the new toe protection. Unfortunately they don't fit like regular Freeriders - the toe box is quite a bit wider, and as a result my feet never really felt planted on the pedals while wearing them. Unlike the FRs, I felt really disconnected from the pedals the entire time. On top of that, the reinforced toe cover/protection makes the bend/flex point feel a bit strange - they don't flex like a normal sneaker, it's further up towards the laces. Not really a problem per se, but it's worth mentioning.

I unfortunately ended up returning them and going back to the regular Freerider. In addition to the toe box and odd disconnected feeling between my feet and my pedals, my feet literally fell asleep wearing these after an hour each time - I think it may be because the toe protection doesn't allow the area around the ball of your foot to flex/expand when you're moving around.

If your feet fit in them (or perhaps you have big toes?) they're certainly a quality shoe with the usual awesome 510 stealth rubber. They just weren't for me, and if you're used to the feel of Freeriders (which fit like a normal running shoe) you may not like these.

In fact, apparently some courses have banned these spikes because of how badly they can damage greens, ESPECIALLY if the greens are even slightly wet.

I almost to the point of taking the scissors to parts of the shoe... (and who wants to have to do that?) I have a wide foot and it is difficult to find shoes that fit without special ordering (and 6.5W is not readily available regardless).  These in a 7 (sized up for running shoes to account for swelling) fit beautifully, with plenty of room in the toe box for my wide feet.  I also have a very high arch and some knee problems, and these feel great when I run.  Doing the runner's box lace also gave plenty of room for my high instep, and eliminated the terrible pain I used to experience from running shoes laced tightly enough not to slip.  I've been able to really up my mileage this season without any of the lingering aches and pains, particularly in my feet and shins, that I had in the past.  I happened to be in my PT's office shortly after I got them and she reviewed my gait running at my current top speed; she said these shoes are worth every penny because they're doing a great job controlling my gait and therefore helping prevent injury.  One caveat that irks me... I've bought two pairs so far, because they really are the most ideal running shoes I've ever worn (for me, obviously YMMV). In the first pair, a slight flaw in the stitching of the left shoe at the top of the curved heel cutout created a lump just under the fabric that gave me a constant blister. I actually had to cut the fabric and snip out the little lump, which I was loathe to do in newer shoes that cost a small fortune.  When I bought the second pair, it had the same problem, but in the right shoe.  Considering these go for nearly $150 (depending on where you source them), I am annoyed that this is apparently a manufacturing issue and I can't trust that I can buy a pair that won't cause blisters.  I ran the Chicago Triathlon this weekend with an unhealed, uncomfortable blister because of it.  It makes me feel like the only options for buying these are to pay way more in a store so you can test run them on site and check for the stitching flaw, or order them more affordably online but know you may haveto return multiple times if the flaw is present. They work so well in every other regard that I'll probably continue to buy them. This brand has always been my savior in terms of width, I'll just hope they fix this issue in future iterations.  Experience level: Female in early 40s, 12 years back of the pack age group triathlete with 1 year focused on improving running, average 10-15 miles per week, longest runs 10K

I've long worn Nike Dunks as my go-to sneakers for almost 20 years now due to their solid durability, comfortable toe box, and understated simplicity. Unfortunately, this model is has none of the merits of it's ancestors. With the new Dunk design opting for a herringbone sole ala Vans and other skater shoes that is nowhere as flexible as the previous soles and creates pressure creases when curled. Curling your toes or pushing off the forefoot thus will cause unbalanced pressure on the rubber herringbone sole and will lead to cracks in the front sidings of the shoe leaving it's long term durability in serious question. Additionally the new sole is significantly narrower than the older models it's recommended to size up in width. The toe box shape has also changed and combined with a lack of flexibility in the upper material, people with a larger volume forefoot will find that their toes feeling strangled and cramped due to the lack of adjustment available at the lowest set of eyelets at the base of the tongue. Breath-ability is also a concern for this model with a combination of a full leather upper, a higher than a industry standard ankle cut, and lack of air holes which means your feet will get hot quick. Style-wise the snakeskin textured mid panels also are a horrid contrast to the otherwise plain and solid paneling as well.

The old Dunks were great because they were a basketball sneaker that can be comfortably worn all day without issues. They were versatile in that the toe box and breathable material did not constrict with any activity and the understated styling allowed it to be worn as as an athletic shoe or casual shoe. This new model can't do either, with a skater sole that is too rigid to be used for any traditional sports and, as far as casual wear is concerned, this model has a hefty volume and silhouette that can make it's wearer look like they they have an identity crisis like the shoe itself.

In time, these might be excellent Flip Flops, but out of the box there are a couple issues.  The primary problem is the strap.  While it does have a softer layer that sits on top of the foot, the strap is still quite uncomfortable.  At the front edge of the strap, the various layers that make up the strap are sewed together such that the lower front edge creates a "sharp" crease that cuts into my foot.  It seems it would have been easy to just round the softer layer of material up around that edge.  Also, the strap seems to sit at an angle such that the front edge is tight to the foot while the back edge has a little room.  The other thing I'm not thrilled with is how thick the sole is.  It's about like a conventional style athletic shoe, with a good three quarters to one inch of lift off the ground.  The reason I've still rated the flip flops 4 stars is that I can see that after I've worn them for a while and the footbed compresses down somewhat, some of these issues will get better.  In addition, the arch support and overall foot fit of the cork bed is exceptional.  I think it's worth it to put in the time to break these in and hopefully I'll be upgrading my rating.  In the meantime, please please redesign that strap and make the underside soft all the way around!

First I love Amazon and purchase a lot of products from them. But every once in awhile I get something that isn't correctly described. These replacement cleats are that way. The website describes them as multipurpose but this is not accurate. The product packaging states
* Superior Traction for Synthetic Surfaces.
* Designed specifically for synthetic turf, artificial grass, field turf, ever grass, evergreens and turf grass applications.
* Reduced profile allows cleat penetration into synthetic surfaces.
These facts were not listed in the product description so I purchased these cleats for replacements on my son's football cleats. He plays on really grass so they as inadequate. They're too short only 5/16".
Bottom line is - if you play on a synthetic field they should work well. But they are not for playing on real grass outdoors.

We received an email from the distributor asking if we would like to try out these sunglasses and post an honest review. Here it is-

These Sunglasses-
-are surprisingly good looking. The metal frames are almost delicate looking which doesn't compete with the lenses for attention.
-are extremely lightweight and therefore (for me anyway) much more comfortable.
-are polarized and also give UVB protection.
-come with a nice zippered pouch for storage.
-have comfortable nose pieces.
-have ear pieces that fit well and don't irritate the backs of my ears.

Overall, these are great sunglasses, especially for the price. The design is simple and attractive. They are made for men and therefore wider than some other unisex frames. I actually preferred them to most other aviator frames for that reason, but this is totally a matter of preference. They have stood up to wearing without a problem and look like they are going to last for a good long while. We keep extra sunglasses in all of our vehicles for the times when, for one reason or another, we end up out and about without our normal ones, so the case is especially appreciated.

These shoes were purchased for my 2nd Camino de Santiago (Camino Frances) that I just completed this summer.  The Camino de Santiago is an approximate 500 mile hike (790 km.) that starts in the Pyrenees in St. Jean Pied de Port and finishes in Santiago de Compostela Spain. The terrain varies widely from asphalt to boulderish steep mountain paths.  For my 1st Camino in 2012, I had used Keen Zion's that I had tried to buy again, but were discontinued. The Keen's that replaced them were not as reviewed as well so I decided to try something different.  After trying out a pair of Patagonia's that I returned because they didn't feel right after a couple of break-in uses, I came across these Hi-Tec at a local DSW.  I wore them a few times to work and they felt good and broke in nicely.  I decided these were it for Camino 2015.  In the time I used them, the shoes did well despite a couple of normal customary blisters.  They did even better after I improved on the insole, purchasing a much more cushiony insole 141 miles into the hike (228 km.)  After that the shoes felt even better.  I believe I may have gone on without any more blisters after the insole replacement.  Where the shoes became a HUGE disappointment is when I noted at the 211 mile part of the hike (340 kms.) that the shoes were becoming separated from the sole!!!  Needless to say, I was very worried (especially without duct tape!) and I knew that I would have to replace the shoes.  Replacing shoes mid-hike is every trekkers nightmare since they would need to be broken in and the potential for new foot problems becomes greater.  The next big city I was told that would have hiking shoes was Leon at 7 days away!  After 3 days, I arrived in a decent sized town that actually had some time type of selection and I was able to get new shoes.  I bought some type of European brand that I will not talk about since this review is for the Hi-Tec's I specifically bought for this trip.  BUT those shoes made it for the remaining 320 miles plus the extra 50 to get to Finesterre. (530 km total), AND they still look like they could handle another Camino!!  Based on my experience with this brand on my hike, I will never buy any of their products again and will stick to more well-known and respected brands when doing a long hike of any magnitude again. A shoe that is bought for a hike like this should last for at least as long as it was intended.  My 2012 Keen's are still in service.

If there were width options available I could've probably fit nicely into a 9-9.5 wide. For a shoe at this price point to limit itself in this fashion is pretty bad. They're great for easy hikes on beach cliffs, along rivers, and on moderate trails, and they are cute enough to wear to most restaurants. Okay - where to start. I understood going in that these were not going to be super, high-quality shoes - not at that price. So this is really just something I'm going to type up to give other buyers a heads-up. Depending on what you plan to use the shoes for, they may be perfect for you. They weren't for me, and here's why:

1) The Smell. I'm extremely scent-sensitive and I could smell these shoes as soon as I tore the tape off the box. Not sure how to describe it except that it reminded me of burning plastic. Granted, in time I imagine the smell would fade. However, I needed them for a costume just a few days down the road, and I did not need that smell following me around.

2) The Size. I typically wear between a 9/12 to a 10. I ordered the size 10 shoes, so I would have a little wiggle room in the toes. There was NO wiggle room. I could see the tips of my toes pressing against the fabric. They couldn't be worn comfortably, and that was before I even tried them with normal socks.

3) The (lack of) Support. Don't buy these shoes if your intention is to do a lot of standing or walking around in them. There is no support and no padding or cushioning of any kind. Fine for short term use, but nothing else.

All of that being said, depending on your needs, these may be exactly the shoes you need. Unfortunately, they weren't for me.

All of the Globe series based on the Chet Thomas IV and Vs have been, and will continue to be, my favorite shoes of all time. I absolutely LOVE the style of them, and the comfort I have found is second to none. Maybe if you need orthopedic shoes or have some kind of medical foot issues, then these wouldn't be on that level of comfort. But for those just looking for a nice and normal pair of kicks, these are the best you can find. The wrap around connected tongue is just... oh my god, so comfortable. Not to mention I don't like having to tie my shoes, and on top of that, my personal feel is that the normal bow tie laces left out look gross. So I love just leaving the excess laces on the tongue. The insides are wide just how I like them, but maybe you wouldn't like that. I know a lot of people don't like wide shoes when they skate, I preferred it immensely though. I don't really skate anymore, but for a while I was pretty good, and I always used these style of shoes or DVS's. Typically though, they don't last long on the grip tape, so keep that in mind. I definitely prefer to use these as walking shoes, because skating in them ruins them so fast, and I love them too much.

All in all, shoes are very subjective, so keep that in mind when using reviews to buy shoes. However, I would recommend these to anyone. In fact, I'm pretty sure everyone who knows me is annoyed because I'm always like "no really, just put your foot in my shoe. It's amazing." hahahaha

This is a small bag that's very lightweight.  It's mostly lightweight because the materials are extremely cheap.  It looks okay on the outside-- it's suede-- but the interior is a really junky material, a slippery rough plastic-y feeling fabric that makes a little rustling noise when you're looking for something.  I don't care about this, so I like the purse.  It's divided into 2 halves inside, with a zippered center pocket dividing them.  This makes for 3 compartments total.  I usually put my phone in the middle zippered one so it won't get scratched, then wallet on one side, and keys on the other side. These fit with room to spare.  It's a great size if you don't want to carry much more than that on a daily basis, and it will fit more on the days that you do.  It would fit a small 16.9oz water bottle if you needed it to, although that would take up all of one side.  UPDATE - 10 MONTHS LATER:  This is my daily purse.  As small as it is, I have a hard time finding things in it, due to the inside lining being black-- you can't see what you're looking for.  For my next purse, I'll look for one with a light-colored lining.  Also, the hardware for the center pocket zipper broke, about 4 months in.  It slid right off.  9 months in, the lining started to tear away from the wall of the purse.  The outside still looks great.   All that being said-- what do you expect for such a low price?  I still don't regret buying it, although I would have if I'd paid more.

BACKGROUND:  I know Skechers is capable of making good shoes.  My significant other absolutely loves her Skechers Go-Walks.  I used to buy Skechers for my son growing up.  Skechers is supposed to be Nike's latest main competition.  My beloved New Balance 475 shoes were wearing out.  The replacement New Balance did not have the color or price that I wanted.  I tried finding an equivalent, ordered these.    They run larger and half-step sizes are not offered at the top of the size range (normally a 13 works for me, these are oversized even for that) and I couldn't get a half-size in my size. ( Ideally what I needed from them, if they offered it, was Size 12.5.)   Worse is they seem to have no arch support.  Me adding inserts to take up slack and add additional support do not seem to help.  These shoes are extremely well padded on the heel but so much that it almost pushes my whole body posture into a lean forward type position - even if I'm just walking or standing still.  I have to compensate, it's awkward, not comfortable.     SUMMARY:   I hate to say this but for my purposes, these are sloppy shoes, lacking support and agility.   Cosmetically they look "OK" but don't seem to have the quality of construction I have gotten used to with the New Balance shoes.  I will probably grudgingly wear these or obtain some better fitting / looking /construction shoes from another brand.  These Skechers will probably be relegated to gardening / dump run / painting type shoes.  I certainly wanted to like them.     SAVING GRACE?  I could say that the only saving grace for these shoes is, IF you are a "heel striker" with wide feet and you have an extreme sensitivity to impact, these ** might ** be your ticket?  But as far as "steering" your feet and agility - forget it.  They are sloppy boats in that regard.   They are not mega expensive compared to what's out there in Nike, New Balance, etc.    I notice that lately the New Balance shoes that I would be interested in are around $80 - $85.00.    As usual, you get what you pay for.   It's possible there are other models of Skechers in a higher class of shoe design but this purchase has left me ambivalent about trying anything else from this manufacturer.

As others have noted, there are several fundamental issues with the shoe.  First, the sizing is way off - too large.  I first ordered these in a half size larger than my child's shoe size, and they were way too big.  Then I ordered it 1.5 sizes smaller than my child's regular shoe size and they were OK.  Second, the insole of the shoe is not glued in very well and  on one of the shoes, came out on the first day. Perhaps Shoe Goo is a viable solution for that issue.  Third, there are no drain holes in the sole, nor along the sides, so unless you turn these upside down or lay them in the sun to dry, water just sits in the bottom of the shoe.  Not only does that compound the poor glue issue, but they start to develop a mildew odor.  Lastly, are related to the poor insoles and lack of drainage holes, any sand that gets into the shoe is hard to get out because it goes under the insole and doesn't have a good way to drain out.  Otherwise, the shoe is ok; the rubber sole and mesh material seem durable.  The draw sting closure mechanism seems good enough.  I'm not throwing them out, but I would suggest looking elsewhere for a better designed and manufactured product.

I’m not one who likes huge purses, but I don’t like tiny ones either. This one is medium-sized and it's perfect for me. It's actually bigger than I thought it would be, but I'm fine with that. It’s spacious enough to fit all of my essentials, plus my gadgets (tablet, phone, power bank). Just to test it out, I put my 5lb Maltese into it and he fits perfectly! I mean, I know this is a purse, but it could actually be used as a dog carrier if you really needed one. Obviously, I won’t be using this as a dog carrier, but it was a fun way to see just how much can fit into it.

I love that I can carry it using the handles or the shoulder strap. For now, I’ll probably just use the handles since that’s more convenient in most situations. There are also two side pockets and a zip pocket on the inside of the purse. This is a great place for smartphones, MP3 players, power banks, keys, pills and vitamins, and other small odds and ends that would otherwise be hard to find.

There aren’t any dividers in the purse, it’s just one large space. However, I don’t mind this since I usually organize things in my purse - everything has its own little storage container of some sort. All-in-all I'm really happy with the style, quality and size. No complaints!

I won't recommend it to newbies but personally, I will keep trying it to learn to improve my stepping skills :)
Perhaps the shoes have been produced for a few years, so the rubber has already been deteriorating and the toe tip of my right shoe got slightly worn out after wearing it for a whole day in the first time. Provided the relatively cheap price, it is not bad to give it a try - also a good lesson to pick trail running shoes next time.

It really irritates me that Amazon lists trail running shoes in their running shoes section. There is a separate section specifically for trail running shoes. I was shopping in the running shoes section when I found these. This is the second time I've ordered a pair of what I thought were regular running shoes only to find out they were trail runners, which don't support my feet well when running on pavement or a treadmill. The title doesn't say they are for trails and neither does the description at the top of the page. You have to click on or scroll down to the additional description to see the first mention of the word trail. I didn't return them because I had already worn them several times before I noticed the title on Camp mor that says they are trail runners. I decided to keep them as everyday sneakers. But I could have paid a lot less for a cheap pair of everyday shoes.

As for sizing, I saw a lot of people had stated these run a little small. I ordered a half size larger than I normally do and they fit perfect. The neoprene liner is somewhat water resistant, more than nothing, but it's a little uncomfortable. It rubs on my ankle. There'd be no way to wear these without at least ankle length socks.

Edit: After having worn these shoes for a few weeks now I'm updating my review. The neoprene on the ankle must have stretched a little because I don't notice it anymore. But I have to say that these shoes have horrible traction on certain surfaces. The lugs offer a tiny bit of surface area actually touching the ground. Anything wet I find myself slipping on: wet grass, wet pavement, etc. I don't understand the concept of this lug design. When people are off-roading in trucks, they often air down tires so they flatten out to get more surface area and more traction. These have the opposite effect. And they certainly don't dig into the ground like cleats.

I bought this for my Study Abroad.  I had been warned about pickpockets in areas that I was traveling.  I was thrilled to find that the color actually matched that of the photo.  Too often I order items that are advertised as bright red, only to find that they are actually pink, or burgundy.  At first, this bag seemed too large.  I really like a bag that is more compact.  But it turned out to be very helpful.  On some long bus trips I was able to pack a lunch, sweater, and scarf, along with all the other usual purse items.  It conveniently holds a water bottle in the side pocket.  The strap is very easy to adjust, and it works great as a cross-body bag OR a shoulder bag.  The wallet was great, too.    The things I disliked were: * The outside zipper pocket was a huge pain.  Its lining was not sewn in so every time I tried to remove something from the pocket, the lining came out.  I had to fight the lining back inside as if it were a living thing trying to escape.  It was difficult to zip it closed without catching the lining fabric in the zipper. * The top zipper and the strap had features designed to thwart pickpockets, but they thwarted me, too.  It required two hands to fasten them and it took a bit of time, which was awkward when standing on queues or trying to leave a restaurant.  The idea was great, but the execution was lacking.  Now that I am home, I don't see myself using the bag on a daily basis.  It is really large, and it quickly looks soiled.  I am still using the wallet, however.  I found it very convenient.

Cons
- Arch placement: At first I thought this shoe didn't have any arch support. Then I pushed my foot forward and realized it was just in the wrong spot. So far so good with these boots.  I work in a factory on my feet all day and have been going through boots quite fast due to chemicals.  I picked these up since Irish rated these as 'best' chemical resistance.  I am about a month in on wearing these and they are just now breaking in and starting to get comfortable.  First things first is the shoes do feel a little bit on the large side.  This issue was resolved quickly however (I will elaborate later).  The boot seems very durable and I like the seeming lack of stitch points that could come apart.  Comfort and fit: 3 out of 5 (poor insoles and painful first week of break in probably a 4 out of 5 after break in period)  Fit and comfort are only average.  These boots unlike my last Timerlands do require some break in time I expected this and I hope this just lends to the toughness and durability of the leather.  While the boot is overall a little on the large side there is a point about where my toes start that it felt a little narrow.  This was slightly painful the first week of wearing the boots they have broken in I don't notice it at all anymore and I think it helps keep my foot from shifting in the boot.  The next thing about fit is the fact the boot does seem a little on the roomy side tallways (not so much longways though).  However, the supplied insoles that come with these are worthless.  You would be about as well off with a sheet of fabric in them.  Seriously the insoles are paper thin and provide no comfort whatsoever.  After wearing them for a couple days I purchased some thicker memory foam work insoles and the fit was MUCH MUCH better with the new insoles.  I highly recommend new insoles for comfort reasons alone and they also make the boot fit much better.  As far as the aluminum toe goes I haven't noticed any detriment to the day to day comfort from this feature being here.  The boots don't seem overly heavy, I don't notice the aluminum digging into my toes anywhere, etc.  I've dropped things that have probably landed on my feet though if they did the aluminum toe protected me.  I have yet to encounter a situation where the aluminum toe was called into serious action for the protection of my foot and will update about it's protection if at any point I do.  Waterproofing: 4 out of 5  While the part of this boot that IS waterproof is immaculately so these have one disadvantage to my old boots.  In day to day work I have yet to notice my feet get wet a single time.  The boots keep all the water out even if I happen to be standing with a flood of coolant pouring on top of them.  The only thing about these is unlike my last pair of boots, which were waterproof unless you sprayed straight down your leg into them, when I go to clean these boots off with a water hose and I spray up towards the laces my foot will get wet.  Not a big deal but I soaked myself the first night after being used to my old boots I could spray off in this area.  Durability: 2 out of 5  The look was very nice when they were brand new.  Mine changed colors about an hour after I wore them out on the floor (not the boots fault I had coolant pouring on them for an hour straight as I worked on something).  The look now isn't nearly as nice but it's a work boot so I don't really care about that.  The insoles are holding up very well so far.  They often get caked up with a black sludge, and when I clean them off the soles look as new and intact as the day I took them out of the box.  This has come as a very pleasant surprise as most other boots I've tried so far barely lasted a week before they started showing signs of wear from the chemicals and I was getting skeptical any boot no matter how chemical resistant would be able to hold up.  I will update to just how long the boots do end up lasting and hopefully it will be a while before I do so.  Conclusion: 4 out of 5 At the end of the day if these boots show the durability that I'm beginning to think they may have due to the lack of wear thus far IrishSetter will have earned themselves a customer for life.  You can always use a good strong durable pair of boots.  Even with the break in considered if they came with a better insole I would be hard pressed to find anything to knock a star off of these boots for.  Do yourself a favor, pick up these boots, and a pair of insoles to go with them.  UPDATE: 12/22/2015  Well I have to say I am dissapointed.  Here I am about 5 months in and I'm already shopping for new boots.  While the soles on the bottoms of these shoes still look absolutely phenomenal the leather on the top of the shoes is falling apart.  It has several gashes in both shoes and the leather on the toe of one shoe has essentially disintegrated.  I bought these because they were supposed to be resistant to chemicals but it seems they are anything but.  I'm going to have to try something different and find a way to protect leather from the coolant.

This is my first time purchasing Chacos. I wanted them for hiking and outdoor activities. I ordered a size 8 and that fit well. I am usually an 8-81/2.
At first, I disliked them a lot. It takes a while to adjust them to your feet well and sometimes it can be too tight in certain places. I recommend following the instructions that come with the sandals or watching a youtube video. Especially make sure that the toe strap portions of the sandal are loose enough to fit two fingers. Any tighter than that, and it can cause some bad circulation to your toes. If you dislike having your toe restricted, this is not the sandal for you, go for Chacos that do not go through the toe. Although the toe straps can feel restricting, I wanted them for hiking. In the case for hiking, this kept the sandal closer and more attached to my feet, even when going downhill.
As for the footbed, I had problems with it at first. When I first put them on, the arch support made my left foot uncomfortable immediately. My right foot did not seem to mind. I started off by wearing them for a few hours a day when I was life guarding. I thought that after having them for 1.5 weeks and doing that, I would be OK to wear them to a theme park all day. I was very wrong. My feet were in so much pain after wearing them for 8 hours straight, especially where my arch was. I was almost going to give up on them, but figured I would keep trying since I had worn them too much to return them.
FINALLY, after a month of having them, my feet have broken into my sandals. The sandals do not break in. They are very heavy duty and well made; your feet have to get used to them. Now, I can use them all day without discomfort and appreciate the arch support that they give me, especially when hiking. When hiking, sometimes the toe straps tighten a little, but not too much. They are sturdy and work well and, not to mention, are very cute looking; I often get compliments for them.
If you do not have arches, or your arches are low, these will hurt A LOT. The amount of arch support is surprising and took my foot a month to get accustomed. I have both Tevas and Birkenstocks as well. Comparatively speaking, my foot got used to Tevas the first day I wore them. Birkenstocks took my foot about 3 weeks to become comfortable (not pain really, more discomfort). This was a good call, because If I started a campfire in my closet my clothes would be less likely to smell like smoke than they would be if I left them in the presence of these shoes. So the first night after I opened the box I set them on the front porch overnight hoping they'd air out.  But the next day I took a whiff and was inundated with the stench of black pitch. I had to stop a concerned usher from pulling a fire alarm, and say, "sorry, what you're smelling is my shoes. They smell like smoke."  He asked my why, so I made up a story about them being the shoes I wore while saving a child from a burning building.  I've had them about a week and I'm currently leaving them in the hallway outside our room at night with the hope that sooner or later the acrid odor will die away and the shoes will be allowed back into our closet. I considered returning them for the non-smoking version, but I scuffed them the first time I wore them and didn't feel right about sending them back with a toe abrasion. The R4's are essentially a discontinued line so these bootlegs are the only way to get them now. If you go check any of the Chinese trading sites (like d****e.com - redacted) and search for R4's you will see merchants selling bootlegs for $60 in the exact same batch of colors and exact sizes (7-12) that the people on Ebay and Amazon are selling their R4's in. Coincidence? I will say this - it's obvious someone in China got their hands on the molds for these shoes and setup a factory with professional shoe equipment to pump these out without authorization from Nike. They might not be up to Nike's quality control standards, but these knockoffs are so good I bet the quality on these things would beat a lot of other real shoe companys' shoes.

As I said, the R4's are discontinued. Nike will re-release a couple colors now and then and places like Footlocker will carry them, but there's no rhyme or reason to it. If the knockoffs are as durable as the real thing, you have to ask yourself if it really matters that is a knockoff.

Fantastic looking shoe. Possibly the nicest looking black and white kick I have ever owned. The white laces complement the white sole and black canvas perfectly, and it looks great with dark jeans in particular. I really like how the sole itself in not very thick, because it holds true to the low profile style, and they are pretty light for skate kicks. I never skated in them, even though I do prefer skating in canvas despite the lesser durability in the long run.

The frame of the shoe (the plasticky material that holds the shoe's shape) began breaking apart quickly. I should also say I never rammed my heel in the shoe; I always undid and retied the laces to take care of them. But I'd notice small particles in my shoe, and after I would empty them on the ground, more crumbled crud would pop up the next day. This repeated until the whole heel area was flimsy because the material was not longer keeping the shoe rigid. This wasn't a problem; I could still wear them comfortably all day and I did. Grated, the shoe was not as firm, but this is worth noting because I had them for about a month at the time. Perhaps a month later the sole began to break down because as canvas shoe owners know, the glue holding the bridge to the canvas had come apart. Even so, I have never had a sole tear like that; that just doesn't happen at all. Soon after, the canvas just came off and I had a hole on the shoe of my shoe. When it rained, I was screwed. After maybe 3-4 months tops, I had to give them up, and each shoe was a complete mess.

I loved how they looked, but I have never had a canvas shoe last only 3 months despite me no skating in them, nor wearing them every day. The appearance saved the shoe from a 1-star; it was just too poorly made to get a 3 however, for all I wanted it to. I'm wondering if I may have gotten a defective pair, as Adio has a good sponsorship team, as well as a decent reputation. But I wuld just find another pair. The concept for these sandals was good, but the execution left a lot to be desired, and I returned them. The foot bed felt great and the gold and cork color was reasonably attractive. The problem was the poorly designed straps. All of the cross straps and the ankle strap were too long. The cross straps had so much velcro on them that even when they were adjusted as tightly as possible, there was still exposed velcro which rubbed against the top of my foot. The ankle strap was so long that it looped around and overlapped the top cross strap, making for a very bulky, unattractive look. If someone had a foot so large that it required straps this long, their foot would not fit on the foot bed. Finally, on one sandal the ankle strap was stitched to the inside supporting strap at the wrong angle, causing it to bulge outwards. Poor manufacturing. If Vionic could pair its superior footbed design with high quality uppers made from good leather, they would probably sell a lot more sandals. Combine the Vionic footbed with a Joseph Seibel upper, and you'd really have something.

I received these shoes on March 13th and have been wearing them as my primary shoe since receiving. I think they're great, other than the durability issue. In less than 4 months, I am already seeing an issue with the sole separating from the upper near the ball of my foot (right where the shoe creases when I walk). This is more prevalent on the inside edge of the shoes, but noticeable on the outside edge as well.

The separation on the left shoe is more pronounced - It looks like approximately half an inch, essentially separated down to the red "V" on the bottom of the shoe.

Since the sole is not stitched to the upper and there is no cutout in the sole to account for the natural roll of your foot when you walk, this appears to be a design flaw. This same sort of separation is also occurring on the very tip of the toe on both shoes, which appears to just be poor assembly since there should be minimal flexing there. Disappointing for $110, they're getting a bit too beat up to wear with nice jeans or something. I guess I'll relegate them to gym use.

Also, I noticed the tan leather darkens the more I wear them from my foot juice. Gross.

(As a side note, I think it's funny that the Amazon review input form wants to know if these shoes provide good arch support...)

The marketing pulled me in. Springs that will improve efficiency, making the run feel easier? Count me in! The wide toe box was an added bonus and I couldn't wait to run in these.

Upon first trying them on I could definitely feel those springs. The shoes have a bouncy feel and I thought I'd found a pair of winners. A bit of walking around and a short slow jog and I was completely sold.

Unfortunately, once I ran a bit faster everything went to crap. It's funny that many of the reviews here say that the shoes are too narrow; I have the opposite problem. The left one fits more or less perfectly, and the right one is way too wide. Shoddy workmanship, I guess? When I run a bit faster than a jog, I feel like my right foot is slipping and rolling around, even when I really lock down the laces. You might blame my feet or gait for this, except that none of my other five pairs of running shoes exhibit this problem. I've never had anything like it before, and I have to say that it's incredibly unpleasant.

Aside from the sliding/rolling issue, the ground feel and transition when attempting higher speeds is just really clunky. I just can't seem to get into a smooth rhythm when I'm wearing these shoes. I feel like I'm constantly fighting the ground and like I have to push a lot HARDER than usual to run fast. It's the exact opposite of what I hoped these shoes would do for me. After a run in these things my ankles burn in ways they never have before.

Finally, there's the issue of look and feel; the materials and construction just seem very cheap and plastic-y. These aren't cool looking shoes. I wouldn't care at all about their looks if they were performers, but it's worth mentioning given my other complaints. And based on the feel of the materials I can't imagine them lasting long.

All in all, I think if you want something for a comfortable long walk and/or light jogging these might work well for you IF you manage to get a matching pair. (Best of luck. Chinese manufacturing at its best.) If you're doing any kind of speed work, I'd look elsewhere.ching pair. (Best of luck. Chinese manufacturing at its best.) I ordered 4 different boots to compare fit and features and chose these boots over the other three.  Then I decided to go with these new boots on our annual 9 day 130 mile backpack trip into the Paysaten Wilderness in Northern Washington rather than my old pair - for fit reasons (my old boots seem to have become too small).  I'd only had these boots a week and hiked about 4 miles in them before the backpack trip.  So no break in was done.  Nevertheless - the fit was very good - no blisters at all - none - despite the long days in the boots.  The boots are light weight - yet the support was fine.  They seemed to wear well - but it is hard to be completely certain after only130 miles.  The soles have a  good rubber composition - it is a more "sticky" rubber that the other boots I tried or my old boots.  This was a great feature when scrambling several rock peaks along the trip.  The "stickiness" of the rubber did not seem to affect wear - the wear was pretty minimal after this trip - comparable to my other boots on previous trips of similar length. I stepped in the river to pull out a fellow hiker who had slipped off a log - one boot filled completely with water.  I drained the water and changed socks and by the end of the day, some 6 hours later, the boot was dry - I was surprised. I think these boots dry more quickly than several of my older pairs of Asolo boots.  The Gore Tex worked well - we had one day of light rain and it had rained heavily overnight and the vegetation was wet adjacent the trail.  Then the same day I slipped off a slippery rock while getting water and stepped into the shallow creek.  Nonetheless - my feet stayed dry.  I think these boots are better in this area than my last two Asolo pairs which are also Gore Tex.  (Not all Gore Tex is created equal-- it works better in some boots than others - for some reason).  However - this year's rain day was not as bad as the last three years have been on this Paysaten trip - so I can't sayfor sure that these boots are better as far as water resistance.  My only rather minor criticism is the lacing.  The lacing hooks are a little difficult to catch with the laces - one has to watch carefully or you will find that you've only partially seated the lace in the hook.  I can do my old Asolo boots while half asleep and the same with the Asolo and Lowa boots I tried as comparison when I ordered these boots.  So Scarpa could do better there - talk to your engineers....  But this is a mild annoyance.  Also - the laces are rather thin and probably will have to be replaced after a year or so - and often I can get 3+ years from a pair of laces.  Overall - I think these are a nice pair of boots - well worth the price - and very comfortable with no break in time - and I really like the sticky rubber of the soles.

Usually there's a trade-off between light and durable. These seem to find a happy medium with above average light-weight and above average durability!

Cons:

The second I took them out of the box to try them on, two of the eyelets found halfway up the boots popped off. These normally function as a "synching" point in the boot but are now worthless. Over the course of the next 2 DAYS, the remaining eyelets popped off. Talk about "durability". They popped off when I was in the middle of tying my boots so it's not as if they are under any extraordinary duress!

Summary:

While these boots do what they are meant to do (provide lightweight and durable support with breathability) I don't like the fact that they're obviously cheaply made. I will never buy 5-11 products again, or at least I will seriously look for an alternative. If these were competitively priced, it may be justifiable. It's been painfully clear to any ASICS fan that they have been doing some serious cost cutting with their shoes in the last many years. Literally painful. Less GEL, lower heels, way too narrow, way too short....whatever they can do to use less materials and bring down their cost.  The Nimbus 17 uses no sewn on overlays. Asics claims it's all for weight savings but lets face it, its an ingenious way to cut down on materials. What the savings DID allow them to do is to give you a generous toebox again and a shoe that is true to size. Add in more cushioning, and this should bring the Nimbus fans back, right? Well, maybe.  I have almost 100 miles on my NIMBUS 17 and I can tell you a few things. I loved the 15, disliked the 16, and I'm mixed on the 17. The short answer is that they are WAY too soft and squishy to my taste.  What felt great at the store has changed dramatically after some use. The white foam on the inner heels is just pathetically soft. You can crease this foam just looking at it hard enough. Mine have had it after roughly 100 miles. These uppers which did feel glove like are now just loose and sloppy. They feel terrible and offer absolutely no control or lock-in.  I'd recommend these to feather-light runners (woman) who are PERFECTLY neutral. That is it. At 175 pounds I've torn these up in no time. I cant imagine what a 200+ pounder would do to these shoes. I've worn ASICS since the 80's but its time for me to let go and try another brand.

This review is strictly directed to the fit of the Reebok Men's Rapid Response.  I purchased this boot sight unseen (my bad) due to the fact that I own a pair of these boots that were previously made by Converse...... and I LOVE THOSE BOOTS!!!  However, after Reebok purchased that division of Converse, they changed the design of the insert as well as the material of the shock absorbing system underneath the insert.  After receiving the boot, I promptly put them on and started trying them out. The knot underneath my heal was uncomfortable the second I stood up.  Much like standing on a not so squishy ball.  I took the boot off removed the insert and compared the old insert to the new insert.  The shock absorber built into the heel sticks up a good 1/8 of an inch above the rest of the shoe and on top of that is a Reebok insert that also has a raised pad on the heal.  I thought for sure that Reebok knew what they were doing so I put them on the next day and went to work expecting my feet to become accustomed to the raised padding.  That was a sad mistake.  My heels hurt for the following 4 days.  I have since removed the inserts and purchased Dr Scholls inserts to try and undo what Reebok has screwed up but it has only helped a little due to the raised shock absorber.  I've owed Reeboks before and have never had any complaints from their products...... but they really blew it with this one.  It feels as though you are walking on one of those palm sized hard red rubber bouncy balls.

Well, I'm surprised. I ordered the 49 mm pair before I ordered the 51 mm pair, and they were perfect, just too small. The 49 mm pair were definitely authentic, no problems there. I exchanged them, and when the 51 mm pair arrived, I immediately had my doubts if they were real or not. Everything that was supposed to be there was - each nose pad had a tiny "RB" on them, everything was spelled correctly, and the left lens had a very small engraved "RB" on it. However, the glasses didn't seem quite right. There were a lot of tiny things wrong that made me suspect they were fake. The label on the nose bridge was misaligned, the engraving on the lens was extremely faint (much more so than on the 49 mm pair), there was excess glue around one of the hinges and around a fixture, and they came with one of the nose-pad struts badly bent. The box was also missing the correct label and bar-code and felt very cheap. I eventually took them to an authorized Ray Ban dealer, and they were very unsure if they were authentic, initially outright calling them fake. Although they never gave me a concrete yes or no answer, they refused to call them real.

I am personally convinced that they are fake and I am returning them. I bought both pairs from Amazon itself, and I am very disappointed that Amazon would sell a fake item and claim that it is real. Although it is possible to get an authentic pair, just know that you are taking a gamble!

I really wanted to love these Crocs.  In fact I love most of my Crocs and live in them all spring and summer.  I got these in fuschia and the color is great.  I don't generally care for thong sandals but thought these would be fun to wear during the day and even for casual dinners on our upcoming cruise.  Now, I'm not sure I will even bring them along.  As other reviewers wrote, I too had some minor discomfort with the rear piece poking and rubbing my ankle.  It also does not sit on the middle of the back of the ankle and feels like it turns in towards the inside just off center and enough to feel weird.  Adjusting the strap does not seem to help with this problem.  If it doesn't rub at the ankle then it pulls on the inside of my toe from the thong.  Now, if I'm lucky and hit it just right, with my heel pulled slightly back to rest in the cradled portion of the rounded heel and my toe just right around the thong, I can actually go a few strides without incident.  But of course, they don't stay like that as you move and so after a few steps I am in pain and trying to grip and readjust my stride which is too much work to make a shoe feel comfortable.  It either is or it isn't.  I wear a 7.5 in regular shoes but have always been fine with a 7 Croc.  These seemed a hair large with the front just a tad longer than I'd like for a sandal so maybe the whole thing was just off to begin with.  I wore for about 3 days in a row to give it a fair chance and to break in as other suggested but it just isn't working for me.  I may continue to wear casually for very short periods but these will not be my go to Crocs.  Had no problems with the rivets so far and have been very careful to secure those areas when putting on and taking off.  Only time will tell.  Update- so I really couldn't believe I'd met a pair of crocs I didn't like.  Well, actually I'm sorry but I can't stand the original clog crocs!  All the sleek flats and my one winter pair with liner- love love love.  So I really couldn't believe how badly these were for me and I gave them another chance.  Wore them another couple of days and I am coming around.  I guess I've built up a callous on the back of my ankles and they no longer rub.  Every now and then the thong piece pulls the wrong way but for the most part these are now working for me.  Maybe they will go on vacation with me after all.  But I will be careful and wear a more tried and true pair on port days with lots of walking.  These will be great for sea days when I can run back to the cabin and change if needed.  Love the color!

These are comfortable, but very definitely not genuine shearling. The tag attached to the sole of the slippers says, "Genuine Leather Upper / Lining: Real Dyed Shearling from Lamb 70% / Real Dyed Knitted Wool from Lamb 30% / Shearling Fur Origin: Australia / Knitted Wool Origin: Australia / Rubber Sole / Made in China / ACV-2014". However, all of the fur parts have a synthetic backing, so they are definitely not "genuine shearling" (i.e. not made from sheepskin with the fur attached). It's very easy to part the fibers and look down to see what they're attached to, and it ain't sheepskin. They are comfortable, but they may not wear well due to not being genuine shearling.

I am really torn writing this review. I bought a pair November 2014 and I would give them 5 stars hands down. They were SUPER dark and just what I needed. The construction seemed a bit cheaper & flimsy compared to some of my other sunglasses, but they were still durable enough for everyday use and did exactly what I needed them to do. However, I cracked the lens recently--entirely my fault and opted to reorder a new pair (6 Aug 2015). Put them on today and was shocked to find them barely dark and not fitting the 'hardcore black dark lens' as described. I double-checked to make sure I ordered the right pair of replacement sunglasses; the brand and type matched exactly. The only difference I found was the supply vendor--Nov 14: OverStockToyz, Aug 15: palebluedot, both fulfilled by Amazon and shipped Prime.

I'm including 3 comparison pics. In the first, you can see them side by side--original on the left, replacement on the right--and the right side is clearly a lighter tinted lens than the pair on the left. The second photo shows an led flashlight shining through the replacement pair; the third photo uses the same led light on the original pair. The replacement pair allow through substantially more light than the original pair. Unless there were different batches and/or changes in the production process between my original order and the replacement order, I have no idea why they would be so different. I'm in the process of returning the replacement pair and dropping the review to three stars. So much for consistent product quality.

So I purchased a pair of these due to word of mouth on how this was the "Holy Grail" of OCR shoes. First I would like to say that the shoes definitely feel like they are well made and will last. The first thing I notice when I tried them on was that the shoes have a very narrow toe box and could not accommodate my "monkey toes" (as my friends would call them). Since I can’t exactly test run the shoes and return them if unsatisfied I decided to wear them around the house for a whole day. They were fine at first, then I started to notice the pressure of the arch supports after about 2 hours of wearing them. I run Spartan Races and this would be of a great concern if you are running long distances. The shoe definitely does provide better cushion compared to the Rebook All Terrains which I run with. I can’t say much for the grip of the shoes since I haven’t really ran in them. I also cannot speak about the water draining issues regarding these shoes that I hear about, since I did not really run in water with them. Over all the shoes feel very well built but could use some tweaking such as wider toe boxes and less prominent arches. At the end of the day everyone’s feet are different and it comes down to preference. These shoes on the other hand are not for my feet.

It has been years and years since I have purchased and worn a pair of Amalfi shoes. I can still remember the first pair I purchased with money I earned working for my father. I was a high school senior. I remember Amalfi shoes as being beautiful and having a wonderful fit, but unfortunately they are nearly impossible to find.
Now that we have been re-introduced, I must say that I have fallen “head-over-heels” in love again. My romance with the Rangoni shoe company seems to be even more intense this second time around. Undoubtedly, this is because the years have taken a toll and I can no longer step into and walk away in just any new pair of shoes. My feet will no longer allow me to ignore the discomfort of a poor fit and/or a poorly made shoe. Every pair of shoes in my closet prior to this purchase can be described as too wide for my feet, even my lace-up Josef Seibel shoes.
I was looking for something with a leather lining, a narrow width in a size 7.5, a comfortable fit, and something dressier than a common pair of sneakers. I found it all and more in these two different styles of Amalfi shoes: the grey Eric Oxford and the brown Egadi Monk Strap that I ordered from Amazon. Both pairs are fine examples of artisanship. These Amalfi shoes cradle my feet like a glove. The colors are gorgeous and the styling details are superb. I am retired and living on a limited budget, but I happily hand over the extra dollars to be able to wear this dream come true on my feet. Amazon’s prices on these shoes are a real bargain.
If you have narrow feet and struggle like me to find shoes that fit properly, please try Amalfi shoes. The Rangoni shoe company has my highest recommendation.

What is good about them:
Stylish - They are a cute shoe. The woven material is different and has a nice stretch
Pretty comfortable - When you first put them on they do have that, "ahhhhh" factor which lulls you into thinking your feet will have the same reaction after several hours but...not so for me :( At the end of the day I had slightly achy feet - not like the pain from, oh..4 inch spike heels, but discomfort
Decent quality - Pretty well made although I notice that the black wedge sides are made from that type of material that, after some wear, looks like peeling skin from a sunburn. So far not bad, but then I've only worn them a few times. We'll see how they wear
Pretty cushy insole - Not like thick, memory foam of higher end shoes but decent. I still always tend to add a medium weight comfort insole to all of my shoes for extra support.
Sizing is a bit on the large side - I always order a half size up to be able to fit an extra insole and for room in the toe box but these ran big. I ended up having to exchange them for the next size down which fit perfect
All in all, these are a cute shoe, reasonable price, reasonable comfort but still don't hit the mark for an all day, happy feet Sketchers sort of experience.

However, even though these felt wider than a medium shoe one of the stripes on the side rubbed against my pinky toe.  Had the entire upper been mesh it wouldn't have been an issue.  Since these are hiking shoes,  I know if I notice it right away when I put them on it will be a blister later.  As far as the length, they were longer than a typical 9.5 medium.  The heel and arch area are narrow, which I liked, so I don't think this would have been an issue for me.  Good padding, good arch support.  The size tag in the shoe says US 9.5 UK 8 EU 42. They do, mostly. because of the shape of the frame of the Cocoons and the shape of my face, I occasionally (about 5 times a day) get some flying grass/rocks/trimmer line between the lower right and left corner of the Cocoons and my face. Not a big deal, because before I bought these, I used an old pair of glasses (different prescription, thus poorer vision) that was scratched and pitted. Now, I can wear my daily glasses, and don't worry about scratching them up. In addition, these make trimming along bright white objects (concrete driveways, white siding, etc.) much easier, as I am not squinting. I usually straighten the temples and bend them in toward my headThey are also great for driving as they cut the sun's glare, etc.

This was the first pair of FitFlops I purchased on the recommendation of my chiropractor.  I have plantar fasciitis. I have had them now for 3 years and wear them all summer and more, so they are very durable. In fact, this past summer (their 3rd year) I took them on a two week vacation to Europe.  I wore them everyday (the only shoes I needed) and walked 6-12 miles a day in them.  As I said, they went with every outfit, which was mainly dresses and skirts.  I also have Fitflops clogs and mary jane style shoes. I was really excited for this book bag because it's so cute. It arrived quickly and was very lightweight. The outside material is a very soft and stretchy material. I had planned to use it for college but unfortunately, it just didn't last. I used it to carry 2 notebooks, my iPad, and pens so nothing too heavy that should cause it to wear quickly. However, the outside material started stretching out just after using it for one week. I continued using it because it didn't affect the bag's ability to hold my things. Then, the stripe material began ripping from the seams. The stitching was still intact, but the material just started to pull away from it. This was just your everyday use, walking to and from class, and opening to get out notebooks. After two weeks the snap completely ripped out of the material just from opening it everyday. If a sturdier striped fabric was used, I'm sure none of these problems would have occurred. It's just the wrong material for a book bag. It's more of an apparel fabric and it just didn't hold up to the tugging of the snap or the weight of notebooks. It's very disappointing and sadly after the snap ripped out, I was unable to fix it so I had to throw away to bag and purchase another sturdier book bag.

Ok, here is my issue with The Boot To New York as a company. I originally ordered their Panama Fisherman's Sandal, great sandal, but too narrow and returned it. The Barbados Fisherman Sandal appears to be wider, and it is, however I think it is a little longer/larger than some brands I buy (e.g. Cole Haan size 12 or 12 1/2 Ascis running shoes).  Based upon the sandal's I have received, The Boot To New York makes a high quality product and though a little over priced, I would buy their shoes, my problem is there is no effective channel for customer service. Before returning their size 12 for a size 11, I thought I would give them a call and find out in inches how much shorter the 11 would be.  As much as I appreciate Amazon and there vendor's return policy, it still involves some hassle, and frankly part of the reason we buy things is to avoid the hassle. So I thought a phone call would be efficient way to obtain information before engaging in the hassle of a exchange.  At $275.00 for a pair of sandals you would think The Boot To New York might actually have a Customer Service Department that could answer a question. They do offer a email Customer Service response, I sent an email  and it bounces back with the following error:  ----- The following addresses had permanent fatal errors -----(reason: 554 5.7.1 Mail appears to be unsolicited -554 5.0.0 Service unavailable So no telephone number and bad email link.  Called Amazon and they gleefully offer me an email as the only means of contacting The Boot to New York company  Good product, non-existent, or no way to contact customer service, considering their price point and their probable customer base, not sure if they will survive in the long run; really too bad they make a great product.

Very comfortable & supportive. This is more like wearing a sneaker than a typical hiking boot...but a SUPER SNEAKER, if you will. I am amazed that a boot with such a flexible stretchy upper can be so supportive in the footbed. My only problem is with the lacing. Because the upper is so flexible, I sometimes make the mistake of tying the laces too tight at first, and then have to readjust them several times to get that sweet spot where they're not too tight & not too loose....just tight enough. But, with a little practice, it hasn't been much of an issue.  The placement of the speed-lacing tabs make it possible to customize the lacing configuration. So, play around with it a bit. ALSO, I took the advice of other reviewers and ordered these 1/2 size larger than my usual size. GOOD THING!! Thanks to the reviewers who mentioned this...you saved me from having to do a return & reorder! This 1/2 sz larger is a PERFECT FIT. And it accepts my orthotics without diminishing the fit in the heel. I have really enjoyed my walks with the dog while wearing these. I take several long walks every day, over grassy, rocky, bumpy ground, and my foot feels secure, no matter what. No slipping around inside the shoe. The flexibility afforded by the slight stretchiness allows more natural movement and less stress on knees & hips. And yet, my ankles always feel just the right amount of support. I've gotten these boots wet in just-rained-on grass & puddles, and rinsed off debris by stepping into 3"- 4" of water, and my feet have remained dry. Towel the boots off and there's no need to remove them to step inside the house. For me, they're a "keeper" !!

I really LOVED these shoes, initially. They feel amazing and helped my get through a 10 hour work day on a hard concrete surface. They don't hurt my feet what-so-ever and they actually helped with my back problems quite a bit. My only issue with them was with the stitching of the two different materials near the baby-toe area. On BOTH of my shoes, there is now a nickel sized hole. This began 2 months after purchase. I've never ran in them like intended. These have merely been walking shoes for work while I'm on my feet all day. My toe nails are short, so that's not the cause. It's simply poor placement of the mating of the two materials. You've got the tougher toe strip that you see in the pictures and then you've got the lighter, breathable, web-like material beyond that. Where those two materials are stitched together, it doesn't hold. I've attached a picture of one of the two shoes. My finger is pressed up against the inside so you can see the size of the hole. Both shoes are identical as far as far as the hole goes. No pair of Nike's should start to fall apart after only 2 months. Maybe that's why they aren't priced like the typical $150 Nike's. Who knows. I contacted the seller (Heart & Sole), but they wouldn't help in the matter, nor would Amazon. I guess worn merchandise is worn merchandise and I'm simply out of luck. Like I said, I really wanted to like these shoes. I could wear them all day long, but now I have to consider buying something else. They've progressively gotten worse. Not before long, they won't be wearable. Luckily I wear black socks...

I just received these sunglasses after ordering directly from Luxottica (the company that owns Ray Ban). As someone who is a loyal Ray Ban customer, with many Ray Ban purchases over the years, I have to say, I'm very dissapointed in how the company has evolved these last few years. As you all know, Ray Ban is/was an Italian sunglasses company. In fact, if you look at the right side arm, it clearly says "Made in Italy" in all their advertisements. But it seems that this is false advertising and that more likely than not, if you look at your pair, it will say "Made in China." No hard feelings towards Chinese made products, but if I'm spending many hundreds of dollars on Italian sunglasses, I'd like for them to be made in Italy. If you call Luxottica and ask for an exchange, be prepared to get the run-around until you are worn out with no happy outcome for you (ask me how I know). For $150-250 these sunglasses are a total rip-off. If we assume you bought these for $50 and are okay with them being made in China, here are the details:  Pros:  - Stylish and more unique looking than the cookie-cutter Clubmasters everyone owns. - Metal should be more durable than the plastic version (although time will tell).  Cons:  - Arms are a bit short and stiff. - Black ear pieces feel very plasticy and much too stiff (can be uncomfortable is worn more than 2-3 hours). - My pair came a bit wobbly/crooked (again probably due to careless manufacturing) - The metal loops connecting the nose-pieces to the frame are very soft/malleable and change shape very easily with the lightest pressure (who knows how long they will last before snapping off)  This is my exhaustive review. Hope it helps with your decision. Again, this is for the "Made in China" version of these sunglasses. Not sure how the Italian version fairs as far as quality. Unfortunately, this will be my last pair of Ray Bans. I salute the original Ray Ban company for making excellent products in the past, but it's time to move on. If you are still in the market, Maui Jim makes excellent lenses and I hear their customer service is impeccable. It's worth a look-sy!

Both boots are marked with the correct size, but cannot possibly be close.   Since my husband expected them to stretch as all his previous pairs have, he added mink oil to waterproof and soften the leather.  Therefore likely making them non-returnable.  At this point it seems that we have simply wasted $200, since he will have to go buy another pair somewhere else if we cannot get them exchanged.   ADVICE TO YOU if you purchase from this seller is to return them immediately if both boots do not fit exactly the same.  There is apparently zero quality control prior to shipping.  I recommend buying your Ariat boots elsewhere.  UPDATE: Amazon was very quick to send a replacement pair.  Although the new boots are still a bit tight, they definitely fit differently.  There is still some issues with quality control as I compared these with Ariat boots I bought prior.  I also noticed that even though the style/model number of the boots were exactly what I ordered, the first pair were made in Vietnam, the replacement pair was made in China.  I raised my review to 2 stars only because Amazon was very quick to send replacement.

Using this product in an unusual fashion..... After ankle shattered and main bones that comprise the joint were splintered (talus, sub-talus, tibia, fibula), the end result is a total ankle fusion and a 1 inch reduction in leg length. I now walk flat footed on the right side with short steps. The physical therapist (Dr. Eugene) encouraged me to buy these sneakers. He thought the rocker bottom could simulate the work previously done by the ankle; allowing me to walk rather than stutter step.
After a week I still had a difficult time moving while wearing both rocker bottom sneakers. We decided to use the rocker shoe on the challenged foot only and wear a standard sneaker on the "good" foot. It seems to be working. I am having success learning to walk and building the mechanics into muscle memory.
Also important for some to know, the rocker bottom sneaker has an insole that is higher from the ground than a standard sneaker. For me, it sorta works because I have the leg length difference.

Great minimalist shoe. Only problem is, no half sizes for people with over size 8 feet. I was caught in the middle; 28 was far too small and 29 was too big, floppy and insecure. So, I returned mine... Good to remember that these fit like gloves, so it's important to use their size chart and select a size close to your own foot measurement. Otherwise great shoe, sole is so flexible that if I hold the shoe with the sole parallel to the ground it will droop towards the floor. If you're a minimalist runner/enthusiast you know this is a very good thing. The sole has a very high percentage of rubber and traction is extremely good, no excessive wear but, because of the composition of the sole I avoid too much use on pavement for the pair I kept(29). Putting the shoe on is not complicated or difficult; you start from the bottom and hook the metal tabs(kohaze) to whichever line of string is the most comfortable for you. It's a good idea to flex your foot up while hooking the kohaze as it makes it easier. I recommend getting injinji or tabi socks(non-kohaze) to go with these so you can avoid dirtying the white linen inside. The shoes are not waterproof so keep that in mind, the canvas  upper is tough though. All in all great shoe, if they had half sizes they would be perfect and would get my repeat business. At their best they are nimble, light durable and cool looking minimalist shoes, try them, I recommend it!!
