This product changed my life! I have a lot of shallow scars, a few boxcar scars, and a lot of hyperpigmentation from old scars. I have tried dermaneedling for two years and didn't see much change and was going try laser resurfacing it but sounded too risky and expensive (since I didn't want to damage my the good parts of my skin). I didn't think chemical peels would make a huge difference so I never thought much of it until I stumbled upon reading about different peels online. I bought and used the glycolic acid 40% two weeks earlier and that didn't do anything but make my face more smooth the next day. I decided to try purchase the tca 20% and and see if it would make a difference. I was hesitant after reading stories of people having bad experiences with tca peels but I finally got up the nerve to try it. I have asian skin and read I should be more cautious which is why I stuck with 20% and nothing higher. It wasn't bad at all compared to the burn with the glycolic acid 40% for some reason (maybe it prepped my skin)!

I applied it after meticulously cleaning my face with diluted rubbing alcohol (to make the alcohol fumes more tolerable). I then applied this product for about 3 minutes and only got to really light frosting and didn't continue with another layer since for my first time I wanted to be on the safe side. My skin got really tight feeling but wasn't red. The next morning it didn't really look at all different than before I did the peel. Since I only had one week before work started I didn't have much time to wait it out a week or so and see the results which I felt weren't going to be dramatic because I didn't really get a good frost. I decided to apply the peel again the next afternoon (I researched and was convinced it was ok since I know my skin well and knew I could handle it--not everyone can handle this so this is not suggested!!) I left it on for the full 5 minutes and it burned more than the previous night. I also frosted morethan the previous night (but not completely white) and could see my scars turning a little red so I neutralized and rinsed with water. Surprisingly the second time it did not feel as tight. I applied aquaphor (kept it moist for at least 8 hours at time) for a week while it peeled and didn't have any discomfort. My skin turned darker during the healing process but looked fine otherwise. The fun part was to see it peel and see the fresh skin underneath.

The edges of my shallow scars have softened and the hyperpigmentation is still there but has lightened in some areas. My skin looks so much more refreshed and softer. This is the first time in the past fifteen years that I feel confident not wearing makeup. I'm only using some tinted sunscreen as a moisturizer and concealer in two or three spots. I plan to do this peel in another two months. Cannot wait to the see the results! The scars haven't completely disappeared but it gave me a second chance and most of all taught me to not pick at my face so I don't ruin my results! So happy with the results so far. Life changer!

I had been seriously shopping for a pair of folding glasses for some time to toss in my pocket to use at restaurants and the like. When I saw a news segment about these glasses I immediately came on to Amazon and, Lo!, there they were. Mostly, I think these things are great. I bought the "universal case" and simply carry it in my pocket for the times when I'm without my reading glasses (restaurants, in a meeting, on a plane, etc.). I've never gotten the impression they are to be considered replacements for ones regular reading glasses and they're not. With that said, they sit comfortably and firmly on my nose and I never feel like they are going to slip off and, at the same time, they are light enough to be comfortable to wear for longer periods if need be.

With that said, my one complaint about them, and this is why I only rated them 3 stars, is that the lenses have scratched quite noticeably. I've been using these glasses for about a month now and most of that time they are in the case in my pocket and, still, they are pretty scratched up. I'm not sure if there is some lint/dirt from my pocket making its way into the case and causing the scratching or what the issue is. When I read the product description, I read "shatter-proof lenses" as "scratch resistant" as well - apparently that isn't the case. As another reviewer mentioned, maybe lining the case with felt or some other material would mitigate the issue.

Overall, I would, and still do, recommend these glasses to people, but now caveat my recommendation with the warning about scratching. If they get a handle on the scratched lens issue, this would be a 5 star review, no questions asked.

I had read the numerous reviews regarding the black ink on the feet. I thought they were exaggerating and making it out to be a bigger deal than it was. Ummm, nope, not an exaggeration. These sandals will turn the bottoms of your feet black as night. I will say that using a damp microfiber cloth will wipe the black dye off very quickly, all of it. So I figured, no big deal, the sandals should stop transferring the dye after a few wears or so.

Ummm, nope. I have worn these sandals 3-4 times a week since I purchased them. I have had them since July 11th. They are still transferring quite a bit of dye. Not as much as when I first got them, but still more than I like to see. It's a bit of an annoyance to keep cleaning the dye off before venturing to let my feet touch anything in my house.

Other than the dye issue, the sandals are phenomenal. I have them in the Crockery and Brown colors as well. This is the first time I've ever purchased every color of a sandal. These are the most comfortable sandals I've ever worn. They are wonderful right out of the box. I can wear them all day without feeling any foot pain or fatigue. I have flat arches and plantar fasciitis. Because the strap starts at the arch, I am able to wear it snug to give my arch support. The low heel cushions the heal nicely.

That being said, I have a narrow foot. The strap across the toes is way loose. However, the straps that go around the foot and ankle are easy enough to adjust that it's not a deal breaker for me. I keep meaning to put some of those silicone jobbies on the strap across the toes to make it fit more to my foot, I just haven't got around to it.

Also, because my feet are narrow, the ankle strap does stick out past the back of the shoe. I thought about taking it to a shoe repair shop and having them trim the excess and re-sew the edge, but it would probably cut through the "Teva" across the strap and I'm not sure I wantto do that. So I just wear them as is.

If I decide to have the straps cropped, I'll update my review.

In my search for a new handbag, the Scarleton brand kept popping up. They seemed to offer handbags in a variety of styles at reasonable prices.

When I saw this one, I fell in love. It looked like everything I wanted:

-A practical crossbody bag roomy enough to hold all of my junk

-A simple, classic design

(I'm pretty sure my mom had a bag in the eighties similar to this one.)

-A bag with great reviews

This bag met all criteria, and best of all, the price was right. I placed my order, and two days later, the bag arrived on my doorstep. I was so excited.

That excitement soon turned to disappointment.

I did not have extraordinarily high expectations for this faux leather, no-name bag, but I've bought plenty of satisfactory faux leather, no-name bags at similar prices in the past 20 years. This bag was not a keeper.

The bag was nicely packaged in a plastic Scarleton bag. The bag had an "S" on it in an elaborate font, and it also said Los Angeles. Ooh, fancy! The handles were individually wrapped for protection.

Maybe I'm misunderstanding something, but the bag comes with what appears to be a luggage tag. I've never had a luggage tag on a purse. Maybe it's for a photo? Regardless, mine was slightly different from the one in the photo. That's no big deal. I'm just pointing it out. If you don't want it, it can be easily removed.

At first glance, the bag looked pretty decent. It has two main interior compartments that are separated by a zipper compartment. The interior fabric is brown, which would not have been my first color choice. However, compared to a black interior, the brown interior likely would make it easier for you to find your belongings.

Unfortunately, the bag seemed very cheaply made. The exterior material felt like cheap plastic. You wouldn't be fooling anyone there. I don't see how anyone could ever mistake it for leather. The interior lining was even worse. It had a rough texture and felt--well--cheap.

The bag itself is pretty photogenic, but in reality, it looked like they had cut every possible corner in making it. Maybe one star is harsh, but it's not a bag I would ever describe as nice. If I had seen this bag in a store, I would not have bought it at any price., but in reality, it looked like they had cut every possible corner in making it. Maybe one star is harsh, but it's not a bag I would ever describe as nice. If I had seen this bag in a store, I would not have bought it at any price.

We (I bought them for my spouse) have owned 2 pair of these MJ Makaha 405-10, the first pair lasted about 24 months before the lens cracked at the screws at the nose bridge. The second pair cracked in the same place within 18 months, despite handling them with extreme care (she only uses them for beach walks and driving, no sports). She says these are the most comfortable glasses she's ever owned, so for that they get 2 stars (her previous pair of Maui Jim's were Cyclone 136 which were heavy and uncomfortable). But when you pay this much for sunglasses they should last longer or be repaired without a runaround. When she bought the first pair at our local MJ retailer here in Hilton Head, I assumed the lenses were replaceable when I saw the screw mounts, which I found out was incorrect. After they broke, the seller offered the send them back to MJ for repair but the cost was prohibitive, and in my opinion should have been free anyway. But since they were so comfortable, I went ahead and got her another pair. But now that the second pair have the same 'defect', I will not waste another penny on Maui Jim's. Which is too bad because I know they are a quality brand, but I refuse to support a company that won't stand behind their product- especially after I gave them a second chance. And if you peruse the reviews here and elsewhere, you'll see this is not an isolated incident or due to counterfeit products. I'll probably try the sunglassfix replacement lens since we now have 2 perfectly good frames, and hopefully they'll last longer than the original lens. If not, here we come Tifosi.

Firstly, this is my fault for buying something with such a vague description. The good: -color is spot on -quality is higher than expected, the handle/edging trim is not cheap-looking at all, which I was prepared for -soft, flexible canvas  The bad: -MUCH smaller than expected - it's about the size of a small/medium handbag. Again, it doesn't really say much in the actual description, but when you're choosing your style/color, it gives dimensions there - they are not accurate. "Oversize" for a child's bag, perhaps, but not for a grown woman. This couldn't even be a diaper bag. The few dimensions that do line up as stated are misleading because of all the cinching/ornamental detailing that makes some of those inches unusable.  -it was supposed to be a zip-top bag, which is the whole reason I bought it, and it's got only a magnetic button closure  The neutral: -It comes with an additional bag inside (aside from the large coin purse pictured) which is about the size of an oversize clutch, that snaps in and is removable. It's nice in theory, but it doesn't fit or sit well once snapped in, and is more of an annoyance than anything - but if you like multiple areas to organize/dig through, it's probably fine. This smaller clutch/pocket also has loops to use with the shoulder strap if you want to use it solo and have a strap. -the buckles (like a belt) on the side are "functional" as in they do unbuckle, but there is only one hole so it's not adjustable, and where the hole is placed, it cinches the sides and you lose about 1"-2" of interior room. It seems like it might be fairly easy to punch other holes to your liking, but having to alter a purse is fairly absurd. -the short handles have a mind of their own and twist every which way, which is only annoying when you're trying to dig around for something and they keep flopping in on you until you untwist them.  Approx. measurements of the item received: top, across opening: 10" (would be about 12" if you could stretch out the material, but the grommet prevent that) top to bottom: 9" when buckled, 11" unbuckled bottom width: 13" width (with room for expansion when it's full): 3"  If the description had been more accurate/honest, I wouldn't be so displeased, but it was a blatant misrepresentation. I'll use it only because it's canvas and SHOULD BE very durable - and I'm hard on my bags so durability's a must - but this isn't remotely what was shown/described. I'll update again to attest to quality/durability once I've used it for awhile.

I first bought the black Montrail Enduro insoles,but the arch was too high, so I returned them and bought these yellow ones. I have a really low arch on my right foot, and I tried about 7-8 different pair of insoles, but these were the only ones I found that supported my arch without rubbing against it. I've been wearing them for a few weeks, and they are slowly taking the shape of my foot. I did not heat them in the oven, and I do not believe this is necessary. I love the heel cup, which acts like a shock absorber, and these insoles are very comfortable without being too bulky.
If you have a high arch, I would get the black ones. If you have a low arch, then get the yellow ones. If you don't know, you can guess based on age. Arches tend to fall over time, so the younger you are, the better the odds you have a high arch. Everything goes downhill after 40.
It also depends on how much room you have in your shoe or boot. You will need more room in your shoe for the black insoles than for the yellow ones. If you are replacing a low insole with a higher one, your shoe might need to be a half size larger than what you normally wear. I was able to use these yellow insoles with shoes my normal size. I have these in my Ahnu hiking shoes, and will buy another pair for my backpacking boots soon.

SA106 Tempered Real Glass Lens Mobster Flat Top Mens Rubberized Matte Sunglasses:  These arrived on time in a small box and the sunglasses were in a plastic bag inside - sparse packaging but sufficiently protected and I suppose economical to ship.  I have a rather large 7 3/4 hat size head and these fit and felt pretty nice, especially with the rubberized coating.  I have to note that in typical chinese manufacturing tradition the rubberized frames featured a contextually inappropriate "hand polished frame" label printed on one of the arms.  If there is in fact an employee somewhere in Southeast Asia polishing matte rubberized surfaces by hand I extend my apologies.  In any event the finish was what I expected and the lens size was exactly what I wanted, tall and wide.  The tint was even and the pictures on the site listing are representative of the actual color and darkness. The lenses are not what I would call good optical quality and there is some distortion but nothing unbearable at this price point.  What surprised me most, to the point of some concern, was how light they were.  I was expecting the "real glass lenses" to have a little more weight to them, weight I was willing to accept for the inherent hardness and scratch resistance of glass.  They are not as substantial as I had hoped.  The lenses do not fit particularly snugly in the frame, are a little creaky when handling the frame and to me they are indistinguishable from plastic.  None of these shortcomings should be entirely unexpected in a $10 pair of chinese sunglasses - particularly if they indeed proved to be decently scratch resistant.  Unfortunately the pair I received had an additional and ultimately critical problem.  The left lens had 3 subtle but very distracting vertical parallel creases or impressions running from top to bottom through the very center of the lens.  The exterior surface of the lens was smooth but inside were these lines.  At some angles they were difficult tosee, but when held up to a light source they became very apparent and were too stright and too uniform to be anything other than a feature of manufacturing.  The right lens did not have these lines so it's obviously not unavoidably inherent in the manufacturing of them - just a matter of poor quality control.  An email to the seller resulted in a prompt apology and a first class tracking number for a replacement pair.  This was a very pleasant surprise.  I will update this review when they arrive - hopefully the lens issue was just an anomaly and I can put a pair through a bit of wear and tear.  UPDATE August 5, 2015:  The second pair arrived today and had the exact same issue as the first - vertical impressions or creases inside the glass.  It's pretty baffling that they would send me another pair and not verify that the lenses don't suffer from the same problem that necessitated a replacement.  Quality control at the manufacturer and at distribution just isn't good enough to buy from this seller again despite what seems to be decent customer service.  Would I be thrilled with these $10 sunglasses if there weren't lines running through the lens? Probably not thrilled, but given I like the style, they fit nicely and they're comfortable, I would be quietly accepting.  At $10 they would be a solid 3 stars.  I think the whole "real tempered glass" aspect of these can be largely disregarded as a buying point, though time will tell if they hold up better under normal use.  Customer service regarding my issue was good but ultimately not enough to overcome a bad product.  I guess I have 2 pairs of $5 glasses to hopefully deflect debris while I mow and weedeat the lawn.

Altra has a great advantage with the 0 DROP sole, it takes a lot of pressure off the body, it makes you stand straighter and makes you're hip alignment improve dramatically. I have previously used the NEW BALANCE 847, ASICS, KAYANO 19, SAS TIME OUT for which I have changed the inserts to custom insoles, but all of them have a HEEL which makes you're body shift forward in an NON-Natural Alignment. This puts pressure on you're feet and hips and increases pain. I have flat feet and an injury on my FHL tendon, which left me with issues in the past, 0 drop reduces much of the stress on the foot.

The Altra Provision Walker is a similar shoe to the NEW BALANCE 847, a normal leather walker, but it has a great advantage being 0 Drop. I slipped out the insoles, since the factory insoles are very cheap and put in a Powerstep Pinnacle which does the trick. The Altras have good cushion and good sole.

A couple of years ago I bought a pair of Inov-8 Roclite trail runners. After a couple of hundred miles, they were still holding strong even though they didn't quite grip like they used to.

Based on my previous experience, I picked up these boots. Sadly, that was a mistake for a couple of reasons.

First the good.

The Grip - The grip on these boots is second to none. These boots even provide a decent amount of grip on wet rock. I haven't found anything that beats Roclite when it comes to grip.

Lightweight - The boots are about the size of a normal pair of boots, but they weight about 1/2 as much.

The Bad

Size - These are boots are insanely small. Normally I buy my normal size and have plenty of room to spare. I can barely get my feet into these boots. Length wise they are fine. It's the width and height that is out of line. Once you get these on, they do stretch out a little. The sizing issues lead to another big problem.

Cushion - These boots have the least amount of cushion of any boots I have ever owned. These are going to wreck your feet. Normally gel inserts are nice to have. In this case, gel inserts are a MUST HAVE. They will be they only cushion you have. That leads to a big issue. There is ZERO room for gel inserts.

Build - Looking at the boots makes me hesitate. I do not trust the build. They look glued together. Nothing about these boots gives me the impression that they are going to last as long as my trail runners have. I'll test them on a few 10 mile hikes and see how they hold up. I just hope I don't get stuck five miles from the trail head with a busted boot.

Value - Not much. Not many places carry these so it's hard to price hunt. If you pick these up for $150 you will not get value out of them. Go buy some nice boots and avoid these. If you can get these for under $100, you might get some value out of them.

Pro: Lightweight, moccasin-like feel, look sharp, sturdy laces, odor-control seems to work.  Were excellent to wear on paved and smooth/soft surfaces. Con: Flexible sole means you easily feel rocks/pebbles/rough edges.  I bought these a couple weeks ago, and wore them on a nine day vacation to Hawaii.  I've worn them nearly daily since I bought them.  Overall I am very pleased with them -- I was looking for a lightweight casual shoe with leather tops to replace some athletic shoes I had been wearing as casuals, and these were a perfect replacement.  I have wide feet, so ordered the 9EEEs.  The length was perfect, and the horizontal width is also good, but the shoe was ever so slightly tight across the top of my foot.  Since the uppers are thin leather, I decided to keep them and give them a chance to stretch a bit, which they did.  The result is the shoe fits exactly to my foot, no extra space, but no cramping either.  Altho advertised as a "chukka boot", they are very moccasin-like in their feel.  The moccasin-feel effect is furthered by the fact that the soles are very flexible.  This feels great on flat or soft surfaces, such as pavement or sand. This also means that  on Hawaii's trail where the surface is uneven volcanic rock with pebbles and rocks you can easily feel them through the sole.  I would not wear these to hike in unless I knew the trail was beaten smooth earth or sand or paved.  If you're used to going barefoot or with thin soles anyway, this would not be a big deal, but if you are used to the more sturdy soles of hiking or work boots/shoes, you might not want to cross-country in these.  Rockport advertises these shoes have DEWIX anti-microbial lining to reduce odor and wick away sweat.  I gave this a pretty good test, because unfortunately Hawaii was beastly humid and hot while we were there.  Everyone was dripping sweat from the humidity, and I could feel my feet sweating inside the shoes.  However between the shoe lining and the Wigwam socks that were also supposed to be wicking and anti-microbial, at the end of the day the shoe and my socks were actually hardly damp at all, and the shoes have no odor whatsoever, except maybe a residual "new" smell.  I bought these specifically because they were higher-topped "chukka" style,  a little taller than low-quarter/oxford style.  I think some reviewers have complained that the tops rubbed their ankles, but in my case this was not a problem.  The padded tops fit very well.  The laces resemble paracord, and I like them very much -- they seem very strong, unlike a lot of laces that seem to come with "fashion" shoes. I bought the tan color (IIRC they were the only ones available in 9EEE) and was worried they might mark and stain easily, but in two weeks so far so good. The good: To say these boots are durable is to redefine the word "durable" to more correctly mean "armored". I love the thick rubber toe guard that prevents me from shredding the toe leather completely off while performing my job on concrete and jagged metal grates. Anyone who has worn steel toes know that OSHA does not want to see that shiny steel under the thin leather found on ever work boot I have ever worn. I work as an industrial mechanic and am kneeling all day on very rough surfaces, which is no problem for these armored toe boots. As the leather disappears from the toe on normal boots I have had to buy new boots every 3rd or 4th month simply because the steel toe begins to show - not these! Make no mistake, these boots feel like a working man's boot should feel and each time your foot makes contact with a surface while walking - the walking surface shudders a bit. The short of it is these are heavy although this is actually a positive selling point for me as I prefer sturdy boots. The boot is more square toed than every other boot I have ever worn as either a Marine or as a Civilian, which is great as my toes have always been squeezed in every previous boot with pointed or rounded toe areas. In regards to the insulation: these boots are warm. I wear these with regular socks in temperatures well below zero and have never suffered form cold feet. They are a bit hot in the summer when temperatures stretch to 104 degrees but I got used to this because I need a rugged wide toe boot.

I still polish my boots just as I did when I wore the uniform (this dates me as Marines no longer shine their boots) to maintain both the look and the water protection of the boots but that sadly does not keep the water out. While I absolutely love these boots for not making excuses on how manly they are in a world full of "men's" footwear that sings Kum-by-yah while apologizing for their boot-like appearance, I do have a major reason on why these awesome boots are being awarded just two stars.

The truly bad: They are not waterproof in any stretch of the imagination. The first pair of waterproof boots leaked in under 90 days. The replacement (free of charge from another online shoe retailer) lasted little more than a year. If something is waterproof they should be able to keep my feet dry as long as they are not punctured or deeply cut, which would of course compromise the internal waterproof membrane. I do not make the insinuation that manufacturers should make boots that cannot be punctured, but as mine are leaking from a manufacturing defect, I cannot call them waterproof. In fact, BOTH pair of Wenatchee 8" boots I have owned leaked at the exactly the same spot which means these suffer from a build quality issue. They both leaked where the rubber toe guard, the side leather, and the sole meet near the toe. Now a slight walk through damp grass soaks my socks so badly that I must change my socks or suffer form wet feet. I can withstand nearly any environment (and I have) but I never could get used to wet feet. I have sent a warranty claim into Keen as of this morning but since this 2nd pair leaked after just one year of use the warranty might not cover it as the waterproof warranty only covers 12 months of ownership according to an email I received from Keen last week. I have had this latest pair for about 18 months and this pair started leaking around the 14th month. I will update accordingly depending on the response I get from Keen.

I work in raw sewage and of course cannot stress the need for true waterproofness, which these boots do not come close to providing. It pains me to give these such a low rating as I do LOVE these boots. If I was just looking for a non-waterproof boot these would easily command all 5 stars possible. I cannot wear full rubber boots because they never fit well and I will not climb scaffolding and the sides of buildings wearing rubber mud boots because mylife is literally on the line. Rubber boots no matter how waterproof they are (and they really are deserving of the term waterproof) can fit snuggly enough to give me the grip and surefootedness I need on the job site.

I have had and used this bag for a while now and I can safely say that it is really well made and durable. There is plenty of room in the inside lined pockets that have both a zipped pocket and two smaller pockets as well as a larger area. The outside pocket is ok except that it lays flat against the main bag; there is no additional width extension on the outside pocket so, if the main enclosure were completely filled, the outside pocket would be essentially useless. There is also a small zippered pocket on the backside of the canvas bag and it also has no width extension. While the canvas material of the main bag will stand up to a great deal of wear, the lining material feels a bit on the cheap side and I do not know just how long both the material and the stitching will last.

This review requires couple of qualifications. First, I have been using 0 drop/minimalist shoes for 2 years or so (Brooks, which I love) and have incorporated a more efficient, higher frequency stride into my running; second, I am no longer a high-mileage runner - just relaxed medium to long (5 - 10 miles) runs with my wife. I wore these shoes yesterday for the first time; five miles/9:30, and even walked a few times - about 100 meters or so - during the run. The shoes were fine; the fit was exactly one thumb's width between my longest toe and the tip of the shoe (I am a slight Morton's Foot runner, though I have not had any problems/discomfort), and a "pleasant' snugness across the metatarsal head. 8.5 in Brooks is perfect; the Newtons were also 8.5 and were a good fit as well.

Feedback while running: The Newtons felt a bit more "dead" compared to my other shoes. I do not mean this in a pejorative way; there simply was slightly but noticeably less "life" to the shoe. Forefoot flexibility was fine and the heel felt very secure. My feet may have been a bit warmer than usual when I finished (I usually wear - believe it or not - very thin, synthetic cycling socks in all but the coldest weather), and I attributed this in part to the inner sole which to me seemed ever so slightly "rough".

Today, I have no 'unusual' calf soreness to speak of (in all fairness I'm 64 and there is frequently some transient stiffness and soreness somewhere in this body). I can probably run 20 miles without too much difficulty, but based solely on the one run in the Newtons, I would prefer my Brooks Flow or Connect, despite the fact that they have a LOT of miles on them

Perhaps the essence of my review is this: As I was running in these shoes, I noted that they certainly do encourage a fore/midfoot strike, but are they necessary, given the plethora of fore/midfoot-oriented shoes? Clearly the Newtons can function quite well as a "transition" shoe, but is their proprietary construction far and away better at eliminating heel strike than other less technical shoes? I realize that I am but one small voice and running is so subjective....Can I have a decent run in the Newtons? Of course. But, given my impression of somewhat more cushion and "life" in my other shoes - and an admittedly short run in the Newtons - I am not inclined to change my shoes just yet."transition" shoe, but is their proprietary construction far and away better at eliminating heel strike than other less technical shoes? This, my friends, is a marketing scam at best to make you believe you are really getting a great deal. Problem is, even at $69.95, these shoes are still far from worth it!! I wore this model for a year and loved them. I finally said it was was time to purchase a new pair. I could have gone to the NB store down the street, but with a busy schedule and limited time. I ordered from Amazon. Shipping from Amazon was great, just as normal. I have no complaints with Amazon. I do however have an issue with New Balance. The Quality Control seems to be a little lacking on this pair. Something is not correct with the construction of the left shoe. I purchased these shoes back in June. I understand that I can not return them, they are shoes, once you wear them they are yours.What was strange was when I first put the shoes on and walked around the house I felt as if I had just come home from a long trip. I was happy to be at home again in a pair of 990's. I only wore them for a couple weeks and started to get a pain in my heel and arch. It felt as if something was in my shoe, like a high point in the middle of the heel and a second high point in close to the arch. This caused me to put more weight on the ball of my foot and in turned caused pain in the calf.  I had to do something. I knew I was stuck with the shoes after wearing them for a couple days. I bought a pair of forty-five dollar NB in-certs. The in-certs seemed to help, but that too faded. An thus is why I am writing this review as I sit at my desk with my shoes off for some relief of the pain. I have now noticed that the sole is coming apart on from the left shoe. The sole coming apart after only a few weeks of usage. The soles on my 1.5 year 990's have not  come apart. The old 990's sole is almost worn through, but never separated. I really feel that the day my shoes hit the Quality Control something happened and the person must have been distracted to let this left shoe off the line. I am just shocked how badly the left shoe feels. I will gladly pay for that MADE IN THE USA badge, but it really hurts when I am let down.Hurts my foot more than my wallet. I don't know if I will have muchfaith in NB for the next pair of shoes, which will have to be soon, since my soles on the original pair of 990's are almost worn through. Just an FYI, wear this model around the house for a couple days. Make sure there is not something wrong with either shoe.

I thought long and hard about taking a chance on these shoes. Was looking for some slip-on's I could wear in the office and be able to quickly get in and out of them to use the padded mat at my stand-up desk. I've had several good pairs of Merrell shoes and liked them all, but when recently looking to replace my worn out Chameleons, the one's I had were no longer available and have been replaced by what many reviewers said was an inferior quality product. Having then seen some in a local store, I was not impressed with the "new/ improved" Chameleons and immediately saw what people didn't like. Didn't feel or even look much like the old design and made noise when I walked in them.
Same issue with my hiking boots. was going to replace my waterproof Moab mid-hikers and found that again there was a "quality" change, and not for the better. Boots falling apart, failing waterproofing, etc, etc. Still look the same, but evidently not. Still haven't replaced mine.
As for the Encore Gust, I couldn't find them locally, and though most reviews were really good, there were a few very unhappy campers who had the same quality issues and pointing out that the current model is not the same as the previous shoes (differences not being enhancements). Despite the negative reviews, I decided that since Amazon offered free returns, I could take a chance.
It's only been a few days, but so far, so good. Though they were a bit snug at first, they are loosened and comfortable so far. And so far, no visible quality issues. I really want to like these shoes. They suit the purpose I bought them for perfectly. Jury is out on how well they hold up. I will post updates.

I have run about 180 miles in my pair in about 3 weeks and have a few detractors to list. First, the sole is coming unglued from the foam. Second, the lugs seem to not be very sturdy as I am missing parts of a few and most show more wear than I feel like they should at less than 200 miles. Third, the mountain laminated picture on the outside of the shoe is peeling off. Fourth, this shoe is sized larger than previous models, so you would need to size a half size down. Fifth, because it is wide, turning sharp corners at speed causes my foot to tip off of the edge of the shoe because there isn't much lateral stiffness in the upper.

Now some good: Much lighter and faster feeling then the previous models. Cushioning is very good and smooths out rocky trails very well. Traction is great (until the lugs come off). Overall the fit is nice and having a soft upper really lets my foot expand as needed. No blisters or hot spots with these shoes.

Final thoughts: Again, durability and sizing seem to elude Altra. If it wasn't for the wide toe box and solid trail features, I would look at different brands. Their customer service is poor, and there isn't any help with the "warranty" unless you purchase shoes from them directly, which in most cases cost you an extra 20% over what you would pay elsewhere. It would be nice to see them stand up for their product and make it right by an unsatisfied customer.

I have owned a pair of the original Newport sandal that had a leather foot bed for about 10 years.  They are wonderful, comfortable to stand, walk, play in. They are without a doubt the most comfortable shoe I own.  I wear them daily summer and winter(with socks).  In January of this year I was concerned they would not last forever so I embarked on a quest to replace them.  I found what appeared to be the exact replica on Amazon.  There was much discussion in the reviews about sizing being a little small so I ordered 1/2 size bigger.  Turns out they were not a good fit.  I returned and got correct size of 10 which the original was.  First off I was disappointed the leather insole had been replaced with the Micro-fiber foot bed.  This was not anywhere as comfortable as the leather.  The sandal is tight on my foot as the foot bed takes up additional space and does not settle out to conform to your foot..  I have loosened the draw string as far as I can, but the shoe, after 7 months, still feels like they need to be broken in. There is little room in the toe box area, they squeeze my feet to the point they ache at night. I can hardly wait until the end of the day when I can change them out for my originals. There is no way I will be able to wear a thick sock with them during the Fall and Winter. On a positive note they are extremely well built. Sturdy, good craftsmanship, fairly priced and provide good arch support. I am now looking elsewhere for something comfortable.  I contacted Keen directly and they confirmed the originals did have the leather, but now all but one style has the new microfiber inner sole. What a shame that I can only wear them for short periods of time before changing out to my old Originals.  I hope my originals continue to perform.  KEEN, if you are listening, I suspect you did away with the leather insole to save money, but you gave up the quality and short changed the customer.

Around week two I noticed that the structure of the shoe was starting to weaken around the ankles and the toe area. I thought that I would try a new brand besides my pair of trusty New Balance stalwarts, so after reading the reviews I opted for the ASICS Gel Contend 2 model.

Pros:

VERY light. No surprise as it is a running shoe but I use it primarily for kicking around and, in particular, I bought it for use at work. Unfortunately, that didn't work out. (See below.)

OUTSTANDING heel control. Nice and tight with no slippage which is just the way that I like it.

Nicely padded around the top of the shoe and quite breathable.

Heel padding is excellent and I am lovin' it.

Cons:

Too narrow a fit. I bought the 11.5 4E model. Length-wise, it's fine but it is too narrow a fit for me. I wore them around the house and thought that if I took them for a nice walk they would start to break in. Unfortunately after several outings, they're not breaking in whatsoever. Strange. They're not God-awful tight but they are annoying enough that I don't want to wear them for very long. Of course, it's now too late to return them so I'll have to figure out a way to use them for short periods of time and (hopefully) they'll eventually break in. Keep your fingers crossed...

Poor padding in the front part of the shoe underneath the foot. Granted, one would expect a running shoe to have extra padding in the heel area (and again, it is superb in the heel) but I expected more in the front part. It is way too thin for my comfort. I will have to seek third party insoles for light duty work which is not what I anticipated having to do.

Poor arch support. I don't think that I have any unusually high arches but this is another area of the shoe that bothers me. The arch support is way too shallow for my comfort. Again, I will probably have to seek a third party solution for this.

I don't expect a shoe that I buy online to be perfect out of the box but I also think that, at minimum, it should be comfortable enough to wear for extended periods of time. In that respect, these ASICS don't really make the cut. Then again, maybe it just has to do with my fat feet.

As far as comfort goes, they aren't bad. But they aren't fantastic either. They are quite a bit heavier than any other pair of flip-flops and at first I found them clunky, but after wearing them for an hour or so I got used to them. The part between the toe is quite stiff and I found it a little annoying but not painful. They are not completely flat but if you need a shoe with good arch support, these are not what you're looking for. After wearing them for about 12 hours, my feet felt fine except the part between my toes was a little sore.

The worst part for me was that the colour rubbed off all over the bottom of my feet. The groundals site says that this is to be expected when the shoes are new if you tend to sweat a lot or wear lotion on your feet. I did neither of those things, yet the soles of my feet looked like they were covered in ink. Even after scrubbing them in the shower I could not remove the stains entirely. I included a picture of my foot before showering.

I'm giving these a 3 because I love the concept of a grounding shoe, but this design needs to be tweaked. I will keep wearing these until I find an alternative.

Doc Mart pair number seven for me, and I must say that despite the excellent look of these boots. . . .well they kind of just plain suck.

Reasons they suck:

Break in: I understand that docs take a long time to break in, but wow. These were about the most horrific and painful boot I ever owned for about three months. I did all the classic things we used to do to break in combat boots when I was in the army, (oil, shower in them, beat them to a pulp) and nothing but time and pain seemed to do the job. Before you go off on how they probably didn't fit proper. . . .no. No they definitely fit very well.
To emphasize how hard the leather was on these boots, understand that after 4 months of owning them, I still didn't want to wear them on a cross country motorcycle trip.
Needless to say, eventually they got pretty comfy.

Looks: they look sharp, however, it is very easy to tell that they were assembled out of patchwork leather. My toes are two completely different colours. COMPLETELY. Like night and day.
Pretty cool, Doc.

Quality quality quality:

This is where things get nice; I was in my driveway destroying something ransom and discovered something under my bum that I was sitting on. What was it you ask? Oh, nothing more than the heel of my boot! Just decided to spontaneously fall off.
They went for some sort of stacked leather idea on the soles, but went the air cushion route they always do, yet in the process sewed the front of the boot on (good idea, thank you, common practice and sense) but glued the back portion on, using some sort of quality of glue you used to eat as a child.
So yeah. . .that happened.

They've been gluing together under 5 C Clamps in my garage for the last 24 hours.

If this is a reflection of your quality, I feel as though you should drop the doctorate portion of your name. For shame.

I'll update this review after receiving the smaller size.  Update:  One-half size down is perfect, so I wear a 10.5D in the California and an 11D in the U81.  Any thoughts of sizing down with the U81 are now gone, because they would certainly be too small.  Other then size and appearance, the biggest differences with the California are that it has more cushioning all around and probably a big more lift.  It's more typical of later running models in these ways, and since it was introduced at a later date (I think), I don't find that surprising.  So far, it's really comfortable and I think I'll like them a lot.  Although it's heavier then the U81, it's still quite light compared to most running shoes.  I'll also note that these have a lot of arch support, which I like.  They probably have more arch support then any shoe I've owned in a while.

Purchased the Dansko Paven Clog/Mule in the Full Grain Navy, not here on Amazon but at a local discount retailer. After doing some very extensive research, first with intentions of finding my husband, a severe over-pronator, some suitable shoes for his office job, I then found myself in need of some reliable, comfortable shoes for a newly acquired job where I will be standing and walking on MY feet majority of the day. With numerous issues affecting my feet and ankles including, plantar fasciitis, swelling in one or both ankles due to poor circulation from years as a runner, athlete and kidney disease, in addition to lupus which has contributed to arthritis of the joints, especially those already affected by other elements, good shoes are not negotiable!
Armed with all the knowledge from research, these were the first and only option I actively sought out, and OH MY GOODNESS, they are AMAZING! While I did have an opportunity to physically try out some other Dansko options, such as the Dansko Professional Clog and another couple varieties, none compared to these in comfort, mobility, support! True to size, my typical size is 9-9.5 med, and they fit like a
glove in size 39! Roomy toe bed, anti-fatigue rocker-bottom sole, breathable leather insole, anti-shock absorption in elevated heel which also assists circulation for energizing hard-working feet what more could you ask for?
The reviewer who mentioned there is a difference in sizing between Pavan and the Professional is correct, the Professional model seemed to fit up to 1/2 a size larger compared to these. While some of the other options ran smaller than these, so I think one would be wise to find a nearby retailer and try these on for your self. I love that while these are a clog, they feel snug as you slip them on, yet still allow supportive movement of your heel, movement, but not complete slippage. I'm a school teacher and mother of 2 young children, and can say through bending, fast walking,slight jogging, stretching, etc., these have held up and remain in place (don't fall off). The only negative, which is not one for me anyways, but for some may be that while the description claims the anti-microbial leather foot bed is breathable so feet remain cool, don't over-heat, I found my feet get very warm, to the point I have had to remove them at times, for a few minutes to cool off, which is really saying alot, since most of my days are spent with freezing cold feet. Like I said, not a bad thing for me, but for some this could be an issue, Otherwise, this is the perfect shoe, so much so that after purchasing my first pair and wearing for approx. 1 day, I found another pair in caramel, and ordered promptly! Favorite shoe ever!!!

I purchased these shoes for ultralight backpacking trips and hiking. I broke them in yesterday on a 14 mile hike carrying a 20lbs pack through dirt, rocks, mud and rain. Here is what I found.

Pros:
-Snug comfortable fit (I didn't have the issue others reported about the shoe being too narrow).
-Great traction on the following surfaces: soft dirt and mud (I did not test on snow).
-Great lacing system
-Light weight
-Looks great
-Breathable material
-Well constructed body

Cons:
-The cleats are the only area offering traction and are made of a weak flexible material.
-You get zero traction on the following surfaces: wet rocks, wood, concrete and slick surfaces.
-When walking through rocky terrain they offer little sole support. You can feel the rocks poking beneath your feet (at times painful)
-Some of the cleats show signs of wear and I don't foresee this shoe lasting more than 6 months.

If your terrain consists mainly of soft dirt, mud or possibly snow, these shoes are great. They will offer little to no traction on the following (specially if wet): rocks, concrete and wood.

I can't expect for conditions on the trail to always be ideal. A shoe that offers zero grip on wet surfaces is very dangerous.

I will update my post in a few months but my initial assessment is that this shoe would be perfect with a better sole made of a sturdier material with better grip on slick surfaces.

The zipper extends too far inside a seam along the underneath the purse.  This causes the zipper head to become stuck inside a place that even her little fingers could not reach.  Still we tried to pull the zipper back out and the zipper head came off - too easily.  If not this time, it would have broken off soon.  Meanwhile, the zipper (without a zipper head to guide it) is still too far inside the seam of the purse to retriever it.  It is unusable.  Do not buy this purse no matter how pretty it is.  I felt sad that my other grandchildren had pretty coin purses (different styles and brands from this one so that each child had a unique purse) but that this granddaughter had something altogether unusable.

* Aesthetics: Looks great. I love the multi-color scheme. It is not bright to give it a garish look, but more subdued and earth-toned to make it subtle, yet still unique.
* Material/Craftsmanship: Very nice high quality canvas material - very thick and sturdy, it seems like it can take a beating and carries on and last you a long time. The inside lining is cloth, and I wish it was a bit thicker. The stitching is strong and in good alignment. The zippers are high quality and easy to operate - VERY important for me.
* Dimensions: The bag is approximately 16 inches long, 13 inches tall at its tallest point, and 6 inches wide stretched to its widest point.
* Capacity:
- There are no outside compartments.
- There is one main compartment.
- On one side on the lining, there are three stacked compartments, the outer most and inner most which are zippered, and the middle one is an open slot. They are 6-8 inches wide, and up to 7 inches deep.
- On the other lining are two small compartments for cards, documents, and small items.

Overall, this is a good shoulder bag, made more valuable by its good price of under $30. I always rate the product with the price in mind, because nowadays that is a key factor in deciding what you buy and whether you buy that particular product, or the competition. Taking into consideration its quality and functionality, I feel this is a 5-star product at up to $35, because the outer material is excellent, and this bag should last you a long time, and looking great while doing it.

Durability. I have been wearing these shoes for just over two months now. I noticed within the first 3-4 weeks that the sole was already beginning to wear down. It is especially noticeable under the ball of the foot where the tread is completely gone. (see picture) Also, the pink color between the sole and navy material is pealing or wearing off. I don't do alot of walking or hard labor while wearing these shoes. the only real outside work I've done wearing them is mowing the lawn a couple of times. I occasionally exercise inside by walking laps in a large room with low pile carpeted. I tried to do this wearing these shoes and found that after just 15-20 minutes, the balls of my feet hurt so bad that I had to remove the shoes and continue walking in my socks. Not only did the memory foam fail to provide any cushioning for my feet, but these shoes actually caused extreme discomfort for this type of use.

To sum it up, the shoes are nice looking and comfortable as long as you only wear them for minimal activity. If you are looking for a shoe that will be comfortable for spending alot of time on your feet or for exorcizing, I would recommend that you find another option.

- sole: Indy has much better and more durable neo-cork sole (Walter is leather soled)
- uppers: Horween Chromexcel on Indy, but Walter uses quality leather too
- Indy`s back of the heel area is anatomically better shaped

They are very narrow, although the box size says "W" (and the description here on Amazon says "M"). If they were a bit wider, I could've worked with the constricting straps, but alas, they are not. Otherwise, the footbed is very comfortable, the platform height is fine (I'm 5'9" and still don't feel too tall in them), and they can even look slightly dressy with the right combo outfit. UGH! This shoe would have been PERFECT had it not been for Naturalizer's funky measurements! I had previously purchased the Carlita sandal, 12M, but the sandal was a bit too big (I am an 11) so I gave them to my sister which fit her perfectly. So, I ended up ordering a size 11W - same sandal thinking that - like Goldilocks, I would find the perfect fit given that the 12M was too big but fearing that the 11M would be too small (I have wide feet). The shoes arrived and with bated breathe, I ripped open the box and had a "Cinderella Stepsister" moment as the shoe DID NOT FIT AT ALL. I checked the label multiple times thinking that the store had mistakenly sent me 11N or an 11M but NOPE, there clearly printed was an "11W". I have ordered PLENTY of Naturalizer shoes in the past and have NEVER had this issue before! Either my foot had grown ever wider or Naturalizers sizing changed.

Determined to get these sandals, I came on Amazon and found a comparable Capricorn sandal that also came in an 11WW. SCORE, right? WRONG. While the color is lovely and the shoe so comfortable, the shoe is STILL TOO BIG (my perpetual dilemma)! The width is perfect but the strap is WAY TOO BIG. Unlike a fellow customer, I guess I have the opposite dilemma of having big, wide feet bu with small ankles thus it feels as if I am one wrong step away from leaving my shoe on a DC metro platform - literally, I can slip in and out of my shoe without ever unlatching the strap.

*SIGH* Alas, I am keeping the shoes as I can't part from the comfort and am weary of ordering again. Just know that the sizing is funky and pray that Naturalizer standardizes their sizing.

I purchased these glasses after losing a prescription version of them, so this is my second pair, which should tell you that I really love these glasses.  I originally bought them at the recommendation of my Optometrist since I am involved in boating, sailing, fishing, and snow skiing, all which reflect a great amount of sunlight.  These glasses are designed to block out sunlight not only through the lenses, but the light that typically enters around the frames, so when you are wearing them, you get superior protection from the sun.  My first pair had plastic 400-series lenses, while my second pair has the glass 580-series lenses.  The plastic lenses are needed if you are getting a "progressive" prescription, which is what I had, and the plastics are supposedly lighter.  I really don't notice any difference in weight with the glass lenses (they don't feel heavy), but they are noticeably clearer and supposedly more scratch resistant than the plastic (per the Costa del Mar website).  There is a definite difference in the wavelength of light that gets through the 400 and 580 series lenses and according to the Costa del Mar website, the 580's block blue and yellow light to cut haze.  To me, the 580 lenses definitely seem clearer than the 400 lenses, but I also went from plastic (400P) to glass (580G) lenses, so it's hard to tell if it was the change from 400 to 580 or from plastic to glass.  In any case, the Tuna Alley glasses with the 580G lenses are awesome.  They are comfortable (I have forgotten that I am wearing them and started to look for them!) and provide incredible sun protection.  I personally think that the crystal frames with the blue finished lenses are super cool looking and I get lots of comments on them, but they come un a number of colors.  While they don't really need a retainer to hold them in place, I would recommend one if you are fishing or boating.  I lost a pair by putting them up on my baseball cap after sundown while cleaning the deck- not a good idea.  I bought the Chums retainer with the large ends which work perfectly.

I was looking for a walking/hiking shoe that was lightweight, attractive and comfy right out of the box. These fit the bill. I ordered a half size larger, as other reviewers had suggested, and I'm glad I did. I have a fairly wide foot, high arches and instep. These shoes do not have any arch support. The very thin insole is removable, so I put in some "over the counter" fairly thin full foot arch support and heel padding, and there was enough room to slip the original insoles back in over them. I wore them with a thin athletic sock and they fit fine. I couldn't find any information on whether they were water resistant, so I sprayed them with waterproofer, as I'm using them for a trip to Iceland in early September. I tried them out for an all-day outing, and they were very comfortable. I walked on varied terrain including up hills on road base trails and they were very stable - no sliding, like athletic shoes do. No rubbing, no blisters on first wearing. My daughter said they looked sort of nerdy, "mom shoe" like, but better looking than some I've seen.

I'm a neutral runner who luckily can wear a wide variety of shoes with no problems. These are a nice zero-drop shoe. It does have a rockplate in the forefoot in the form of Mizuno's classic wave plate. Cushioning is very adequate for mid-strikers, at least for mid-distance runs. I just got them and ran a 6-miler on roads today. They felt great and fit like snug slippers. They have a very breathable upper. Too early to tell how they will work on trails, but they're great road shoes because the lugs are pretty shallow. I'll update when I've put a few trail miles on them.

One concern for people considering these shoes is the fit. I've run in several Mizunos over the years from classic trainers to their new zero-drop lines. These do seem to run a little big. Where I would run in a 12.5 in traditional shoes, I have to go down 1/2 size in the zero-drop. I got both a 12 and 12.5 because of the excellent price. The 12's fit the best. I'll be able to run in the 12.5s, but they feel big. I have to use lacing strategies so the heel doesn't rub up and down while walking in them.

I do like the looks of the bright colors and the style. They do look a little different with the square toe you don't normally see in running shoes, but I've gotten compliments every time I wear them (not sure if people are just being nice or they really think they look cool). I bought a pair of Wave Inspire 10's earlier this year, and the Ferus fits my foot a lot better and feels better walking/running (partially because the Inspire is a stability shoe and I'm a neutral runner).

I recommend them highly if you get the right size. Getting the right size is the only reason I rate them a 4 instead of a 5.

I bought these as a replacement for my flak jackets when they got scratched in the wave pool at Holiday World, Indiana. I figured for less than $20 I couldn't go wrong, eh? Oakley OEM replacements ($60 regular / $90 polarized) can be exorbitant and I just wanted something that would get me through. Needless to say, you get what you pay for. The quality is subpar. The first thing you notice is they are thinner. Quite a bit thinner. I'm sure they lack the ANSI certification for impact resistance but for the money it's no surprise there. The second thing is is that they are DARK. I got the equivalent to what I had, which was the black iridium polarized. They are indeed polarized. They also have a much more mirror finish to them, where the Oakley ones are more subtle. The darkness was a bit hard to live with but the deal breaker were the reflections they introduced while wearing them. It seems that the knock offs have a ever so slightly different curvature to their lenses where outside light can come in and be reflected inside the lenses. This is what happens when you reverse engineer something and don't get it right. If you can imagine 12 o'clock being straight ahead and 9 o'clock straight to your left and 3 o'clock straight to your right, then the glare / reflections would be at the 11:30 and 12:30 positions. Basically between your eyes where it's most distracting. I couldn't live with that defect and am sending them back for a refund.

On a positive note, and I say positive because I got a good result, a better result than I was expecting, I went on the Oakley website and shopped for different lenses. Their website is hard to navigate as far as explaining what all the different color tones were best suited for, but I called customer service and they were helpful in answering a lot of my questions. Apparently I didn't know much about sunglass lenses or all the technology Oakley invests into it but there is an "optimum activity" fordifferent shade colors, polarized and unpolarized. I schooled myself and there are lenses for baseball, golf, snow skiing, shallow and deep water fishing, cycling, trails, etc. I thought colors were up to indivdual preferences. I'm sure some of it is marketing but there is an amazing amount of science that goes into what they do. I visited the Oakley store at the mall near me and tried on all their different styles and lenses. Wow! What a difference compared to this crap! In the store it was literally night and day (these knock offs being way too dark). Their lenses are clearly superior. In the end I went with their newest latest and greatest hi definition optic "Prizm" line which the sales staff said was superior (of course). It has a rose like tint to it and supposedly increases contrast and viewability for everyday use. I like them. I compared them side by side with a pair of Maui Jims I have. I have always considered Maui Jims to have an excellent picture, and toe to toe, I think I prefer the daily Prizm polarized better. Of course, the lens replacements lightened my pocket by $110 but let's face it, we buy and wear Oakleys not just for their style, but for their functionality and comfort as well as superior optics. At least I am reasonably sure with genuine lenses that my eyes are getting the advertised UV and impact protection versus taking a chance among all these various knock offs. Yes, spending a hundred bucks sucks but you get what you pay for, and in the future I am going to insure that I take more precautions to protecting my lenses. Don't waste your time with these cheap inferior knock offs.

I used these shoes for the first time during a full day at Xplor in Mexico that included walking on flat and inclined wet and dry concrete, swimming, and driving ATVs.

Durability - 2/5 stars - The heel of the shoes is already starting to wear apart where the collar surrounds your foot. I have concerns over the pull cord eventually breaking and wonder if the shoes will become unusable if it breaks.
Fit - 4/5 stars - Comfortable all day long with no blistering or chafing. Adjustable pull cord works well to secure shoes to your feet, but can get annoying since it swings around and occasionally goes under feet when walking.
Traction - 1/5 stars - On wet surfaces these shoes make you feel like you're walking on ice. They're fine on dry land, but avoid these if you plan to be walking on anything smooth and wet outside of water.

Overall I'd probably be inclined to look to Speedo or another brand without the pull cord and with better grip. As others have mentioned, these are definitely not shoes I'd wear hiking, surfing, or running.

This is the 5th pair of Cobb Hill women's dress shoes I have purchased. They usually hit all the right places for my oddly shaped feet and help me cope with back and knee injuries. While there have been some issues with certain Cobb Hill shoes running a tad narrow in the foot bed (even differences within same model but different colors) these wedges were a standard B width and fit as expect. They are VERY light weight and this does concern me some as other Cobb Hill shoes feel more durable and better made. Definitely a different sole. But after only 2 wears, it is too early to tell if their weight is a reflection of how long they will last. I know that they aren't great for all day comfort. Maybe 4-5 hours max. I will give them a proper all day test this fall when they are back in season. Overall, it was a great deal and I am happy with my purchase. Glad I didn't pay full retail price for them tho as craftsmanship may be a little compromised on this particular model. Some sloppy glue and a semi cheesy fashion fastener. But overall, CH manufactures well made leather therapeutic shoes and these aren't a total exception.

Note, these are made in China like their other styles so best consumer value when purchased on sale... (you generally get what you pay for with this brand). When I spend $80-100+ on a pair of dress shoes, I like them to last about 5 years or seasons if possible so I was happy to find these at 60% off. My oldest pair of regularly worn CH leather Mary Jane pumps are about 4 years old now and aside from the Velcro buckle getting weak, they have held up nicely... But they do have a different sole and thicker leather upper compared to these.

I have mixed feelings about the New Balance 759 shoes, hence the 3-star review.  I should note that this is the second paid that I have purchased; I wore my first pair for over a year.  On the plus side, they are quite comfortable.  I do a lot of walking, and because the balls of my feet are susceptible to pain, I have typically had to use inserts with my walking shoes to provide a sufficient cushion.  I have not had to use inserts with the 759, which speaks well to their cushioning.  On the minus side, they do not seem quite as well-made as walking shoes that I have purchased from New Balance in the past, such as the 645.  The sole seems to wear out more readily.  After a half-year of wear, the outsole lining the perimeter of the shoe completely separated from the midsole, and I was able to squeeze out additional use only by re-gluing the separated soles on my own.  Hopefully New Balance can improve its manufacturing process to address problems of this nature.  Because of their cushioning and their fit with my narrow feet, I still prefer these to other walking shoes, despite the problem I have highlighted.

Ordered these with great excitement. I was thrilled to have found a flip flop that would support my problem feet. I have learned over the years the power and effectiveness of good solid support in shoes. However, my excitement turned slowly remorse. Right out of the box, I noticed the straps seemed way too loose. The flip flops were the absolute correct size and even the correct width. For whatever reason, the straps were way too loose. I'm not talking about a personal preference here...as in, perhaps I just like the straps to fit really snugly. No, these straps were so loose as to render the flops almost, but not quite unwearable. Oh how I wish I had not worn them. I shrugged it off and tried to wear them anyway, as I was on vacation. I wore them for the better part of two days before I noticed serious pain. I have problem feet and am no stranger to experiencing foot pain. However, this pain was located in a foot and a spot (ball of foot) where I don't normally experience pain. For this reason, I attribute the flip flops and the likely culprit. This was actually so bad (my toe and ball of foot were very swollen) that I could not wear shoes of any kind for several days. I don't want to completely slam the shoes or Vionic, because obviously, for whatever reason, these did not fit me correctly. I must say though, that having gotten the correct size and width, it seems to me this is a design or manufacturing problem. I've seen other reviewers say the straps on these are way too loose, as well. So, heed the reviewer warning! The straps on these particular flip flops are indeed, extremely loose. I returned them through amazon without any problems and am now searching for another brand of flip flop. I really wanted to like these. They seem very well made in every way, save the length of the straps. Unfortunately, when it comes to flip flops, the straps are an essential part of the fit.

They were so packed out and smashed that I had to stop running in them from leg fatigue and pain. I am not a heavy person, 165lbs, so I shouldn't be able to destroy a shoe that fast. I called to have them considered a warranty issue since Altra says you should get 300-500 miles out of them. I was told that I first had to send them back to the place I purchased them. Shouldn't it be the manufacturers responsibility to fix a problem with their product, not the store selling them? I purchased them from a brick and mortar store 500 miles from where I live and it isn't that stores responsibility to fix Altra's problems. Second, they said if it was after 30 days (Now, I actually put 200 miles on a pair of shoes in 30 days, but I would guess most people don't.) Altra could only offer you 25% off of a new pair purchased directly from them. Anybody paying full retail price from the manufacturer is overpaying because with the internet you should be able to find a reduced price somewhere, so offering me a coupon for 25% off only good at their website doesn't save me money, and on top of that doesn't get me a warranty. I was told to purchase them from a store that offered returns on items after Altra's 30 day policy expired. I would love to keep running in them, but there is no way I can afford $110 or even $82.50 for as many pairs of shoes I need for my training.

I own two pair of Dawgs now and love the prints. I have the multi-colored-floral ones and the red, white, and blue ones. People who see them for the first time always comment positively about them. My findings are that I wear a size 7 1/2 Medium, and have ordered shoes online for years and never had to return a pair. Having read on several sites that they run a bit large, I ordered size 7, and length-wise they fit perfectly. However, the Z-straps are somewhat loose, and there's no real arch support. I expected the width of the straps would run smaller, since I was ordering a half size shorter than what I normally wear, but this is not the case. They fit me somewhat loose, so I can't wear them over a couple of hours or they start rubbing my feet. However, I read here that some people think they run small, so that means there is poor quality control at the factory in China. This is a real downer, and no doubt costs Dawgs some revenue by people who don't want to deal with returns, as they aren't free, like they are on most shoe sites. I, myself, went on this site to order another pair in a solid color this time, but I won't, as I'm afraid I might get a pair that is too large, too small, or too short. All of these have been listed as complaints here. My opinion is that, if you take a 1/2 size shoe, then order a size down (as I did), and if you have a wide foot or high instep, they will probably fit you very comfortably. But if you normally take a medium or narrow width shoe, then you probably will be unhappy with them. Medium will be loose and narrow won't do at all. If you want to take a 'Dawgs Roulette' shot at fit, then by all means order them. They're cute and reasonably comfortable, but wish I could buy the Canadian version, as I've read here that the footbed is smooth and more comfortable than the 'pebbly' USA ones.

I have been comparing these Teva's against Chaco sandals for about a month before deciding on these, mainly because they are half the price.

I ordered a size 10.5, which has been my shoe size for a decade without issue. When they arrived, they were way too small. There is a lip on the back end of the sandal and at first I was stepping on that lip which was uncomfortable. I pushed my foot all the way forward in the sandal and tightened the back strap first to keep my foot forward and off that lip. This worked better, but left my toes hanging over the front by a little bit, enough to painfully kick a rock or stump if I wore these hiking as I had originally planned.

There are three straps to adjust the sandal. The back and top straps are fine, but the one that goes over the toes is horrible. I could get the back and top straps snug, but the one over the toes always remained fairly loose. If I tightened it enough to make it snug, it would squeeze down uncomfortably on my pinky toe. No happy medium.

I did try these on with hiking socks and it seemed to resolve the issues I was having with the front strap and made the sandals pretty comfortable. I could see them being nice with socks if I replaced them with a half size up, but I don't plan on always wearing them with socks.

The quality of the sandal seemed to be pretty good. The top foam is very soft and might get torn up over time, but the tread is great and sturdy.

I will be returning these and trying out the Chaco's next.

Unless you have a super power that prevents you from feeling pain in your feet, forget wearing these sandals for more than 4 hours at a time. Even if you have flat feet, these things are horrible due to the cute little pattern in the leather part of the heel. The circular pattern will wear into your feet and give you either blisters or calluses from how stiff it is. There is no cushioning in this shoe whatsoever.

These shoes are good for wearing for short periods of time, such as going out to dinner. If you're looking for shoes to wear to work, to a wedding, or to another event where you'll be on your feet for long periods of time, consider more comfortable shoes before settling on these.

Loved these shoes when I first put them on.  They look really nice on the feet and were quite comfortable at first.  However, after about an hour or so of walking around the house in them, they started to feel very uncomfortable, like something was rubbing on the side of my feet.  After a couple of hours, they became downright painful.  I took them off and inspected the inside and I believe the culprit is the stitching on the inside.  If you run your fingers along the inside edge you can really feel how hard and rough the stitching feels.  None of my other shoes have this problem.  They should put the stitching somewhere else where it doesn't contact your foot or at least put some soft lining on the inside of the shoe.  The other thing I noticed is that my feet sweat more than usual in these shoes.  I blame this mostly on the interior lining of the tongue and around the ankle (collar).  It's made of what appears to be a synthetic leather.  My Adidas have a soft, cloth lining that either absorbs the sweat or is much more breathable that my feet don't heat up as much causing less sweat.  I really wanted to like and keep these shoes, but the obvious design issues caused too much discomfort.  I hope PUMA reads these reviews and makes improvements to this really good looking shoe.

There are so many things I like about these shoes, but there are a couple important aspects that are really bad.

The good:
The rubber on the outsole is great for walking around, and the closure system is secure, although a little goofy with the backwards strap. They vent well, too. I have only had them for a couple months, but they seem well made.

The bad:
These shoes are NOT STIFF. I've had trouble with toes going numb from my pedals creating a "hot spot" over the cleat. I've tried 2 different kinds of Crank Bros cleats on candy pedals and egg beaters, and I've tried SPD cleats on some shimano pedals. I also added the crank bros shoe shields in an attempt to add a little stiffness to the cleat area. I think these shoes should work ok on a large platform clipless like a Crank Bros Mallet, but on a mini-platform like the Candy, the shoe simply doesn't offer enough support.

Fit... a 48 regular isn't long enough, and the 49W is too wide. Does shimano make a 49R? Yes, but they don't sell it in the US market. I tried the 49W, and it has too much volume for my foot. In troubleshooting the numb toes, I tried volume reducers and 3 different insoles in an effort to make them feel better. I've settled on a volume reducer and the factory insole, but there is very little arch support and the heel of the shoe doesn't have a deep enough cup to really lock the back of the foot to the shoe.

In the end, I'm going to sell these shoes locally and get something stiffer. I really wanted to like them, and I wish I could make them work, but the lack of a stiff sole is what is sending them down the road.

I wanted a pair of sandals that I could wear in spring, summer, and occasionally in the fall. I wanted pair that was neutral but stylish, and I wanted something that would last me for at least two years. The Lauren sandal seemed like a perfect pick, but these shoes suck.

There are both design and implementation issues with these shoes. They would be appropriate for a weekend getaway where you wanted to throw them away afterward providing you were walking only short distances.

Design
- The sole is satisfactory and should protect from rocks, including side brushes
- The enclosure does not tighten the overall shoe like laces or velcro would, instead it tightens the top around your ankle. That keeps the shoe from coming off but if you tighten it for significant walking you'd better expect lines on the ankle and pain later
- The tightening ball does not really keep the string tight when wet
- The ball bounces against the back of the ankle when the string is wet

Implementation
- Sole is good in implementation as well as design. No real issues with the top netting
- The glue attaching the very thin foam to the inside of the shoe was faulty. The foam completely detached after a day and let the foam slide which it did. Removing the foam exposes your feet to the inside stitching and eliminates all cushion.

Overall - get something else. Better options are available at similarly low cost.
