This is my 6th pair of Fryes (and my last, I promise), and they are all American-made, classic styles. Most similar to them would be my Campus 14l in banana. I am a solid 9 in the harness and campus styles. Imagine my shock when I find myself between 9-9.5 in this boot! In the 9, my toes felt crowded. There was the normal heel slip, but then crowded toes. I really don't fancy crowded toes. Maybe this would diminish as the boots stretch with wear, but then maybe not. I would rather have more room, so I sized up. I have rarely read reviews where people size up in Frye, but there you have it. The new pair arrived today, and the fit does seem better. The right boot has more room than the left, width-wise. I suppose this is to be expected since these are hand-made and no two pair are alike. I do wish it was a bit more snug in the width, but I think it will be fine. The leather is unlike my other boots. "Stonewashed," they call it, and it is buttery soft and variegated in color. The shaft is roomier than my other Campus boots. The rubber lugged sole is wonderful; I so prefer the comfort of a rubber sole.

The walnut was so dark that the stitch detail and variegation were lost, but the saddle is LOVELY. These boots are so unique; I've never seen anything like them. I really wanted a pair of Fryes in stonewash since I find them to look like a modern take on a classic boot. Also, I think the stonewash holds its beauty when scuffed and abused better than smooth leather. There is another version of this boot in Dakota leather with a leather sole, but I think it looks outdated. This one is more beautiful and could only be improved if the thread used for the stitching was a different color. The Camous stitch of old had a banana boot with green stitching. Those were head-turners, for sure.

Why haven't more people bought this boot? Mine was deeply discounted and there are almost no reviews of this boot online, which suggests they didn't sell. I hope you find my review insightful, should you be considering these boots.

******Update**** I decided the right boot was just too large, and it was noticeably so, even just visually. I exchanged for the same color/size and the new pair was perfect. Ok first let me say that I have a beloved pair of TBNY dress shoes which I purchased around 2003. They are the best fitting, most comfortable, highest quality shoes I have ever had, hands down. The leather was top notch and so was the 'fit and finish'. However, at 12 years old they are finally showing cracks in the leather. This is a testament to the quality of that shoe and how incredibly comfortable they were for me.

Now, fast forward to today when I have been trying to find a new pair. I am 6'0", 165 lbs, and I was 6'0", 165 lbs 12 years ago. Therefore I believed I should be able to use the same shoe size from TBNY. My 2003 TBNY dress shoes were a 9.5M (my normal size with other brands ranges from 9.5M to 10.5M US). I have recently purchased three TBNY Oxford styles from Amazon, starting with 9.5M. The first pair were far, far too big. They were very much too long, and especially too roomy/wide in the heel. I sent them back. I then purchased a 9.0M in a slightly different TBNY Oxford style, thinking that perhaps the style contributed to the size problem. But no, they were closer to the right size but still off; they were exactly right in the toe and ball/arch, but again were quite a bit too wide/roomy in the heel. In desperation (I really, really liked the shoes), I sent these back and ordered another pair in an 8.5M in the TBNY Duke Oxford. Alas, these were now far too tight in the toe/ball, and, incredibly, still slightly too roomy/wide in the heel. I had to return them, too.

My conclusion: TBNY has clearly changed the SHAPE of their shoes in all three pairs I purchased. The 'last' (the mold that is used during the construction of a shoe to give it its shape) is now different, with a narrower toe and a wider heel. This simply does not fit my feet. I am disappointed because I loved my old TBNYs. My recommendation for potential buyers: if you have a relatively wide heel and relatively narrow toes, this shoe is likely to fit. If you have previously purchased TBNY shoes from a decade or more ago, bear in mind that they are not likely to fit the same way since they have apparently changed their overall fit.

One other note: my old TBNY dress shoes were higher quality shoes than all three pairs of TBNYs I tried recently. The older pair were made with more supple, higher quality leather which will tend to be more comfortable. The recent pairs were stiffer, thicker leather and the edges were rougher. The manufacturer clearly did not spend as much time on the shoe as they did 12 years ago. I would not recommend TBNY like I used to based on the decrease in quality. On the other hand, these shoes look SHARP; styling is not the problem.

If you consider yourself a serious hiker, do NOT buy these boots.  After reading so many wonderful reviews, I decided to buy these boots for a summer of hiking through different national parks.  I broke them in by hiking 3-5 miles every other day through my neighborhood park for about 2 months.  They felt fine and I was excited to wear them over the summer.  As we hiked our first park, I wore them for 10+ miles on the first day and 10+ miles on the second day.  On the third day, I started to feel intense soreness through my achilles tendons.  My husband thought they just weren't broken in enough so I continued to wear them for a few more days.  The pain just kept getting worse and worse, to the point where it was unbearable to hike in them.  I switched to my Chacos and was able to hike many miles in them without any pain.  I took a two week break from the Danner boots during the trip, thinking that my tendons just needed some time to heel and strengthen.  The second I started walking in the boots again the pain flared up.  I went to a nearby REI to get other boots to finish my trip in.  I spoke with two different employees about the Danner boots and both said how horrible they were.  People were constantly returning the shoes because they made the same mistake I did.  While these boots look adorable, the technology is archaic, the soles are flat, and they are super heavy.  They are NOT good boots if you plan to do any actual hiking!

These were my first real running shoe. I've got about 250 miles on the pair now, so I feel I can give an experienced review overall. These are dedicated running shoes for me, no other usage aside from warm up walks and street running - asphalt, concrete, very rarely grass when I have to skirt around puddles or slippery pavement. I only ran in the rain a couple of times.

First, quickly, these are very comfortable shoes, lightweight, and stylish. I trained up to a 5k (3.1 miles) without any issues aside from 1 little section of mesh on the left shoe spontaneously disappearing/breaking. Not sure how that happened, but it did. It has not gotten worse over 100 miles or so, which speaks highly of their mesh quality I suppose. Could have snagged something I suppose.

When I got past 3.1 miles consistently, that's when I started to get a case of plantar fasciitis in my right foot, and the right side of my foot (outer edge) started to bug me. Not sure if I'm just dealing with a shoe that is 1/2 size too small or something (my foot feels great in it, before running, during and after). But, it's interesting to note that as my distance increased (very gradually) and these shoes are aging, something has changed.

I also noticed a tear above the left big toe, in the fabric layer under the mesh. It's about 1/2 inch now, but I expect that will grow. And gradually my toe will probably poke through the mesh - before that happens, I intend to retire this pair for a new pair shortly and use these for walking.

So, I expect to get about 250-300 miles out of this pair of shoes. I've read you can usually get around 400 miles out of a shoe, but that's probably a general guideline and lots of factor come into play - your personal stride/gait/wear patterns, surfaces you run on, etc.

Aside from the unexpected wear above the toe, the random mesh fraying, and plantar fasciitis in my right foot (which honestly I can't attribute to the shoe necessarily, but it's worth noting), I do enjoy how these shoes feel on my feet and while running. I may get another pair (perhaps a little bigger) or I might try another brand...haven't decided.

These shoes were designed especially for Zumba, which includes lots of twists, turns, and sliding. The big selling point of these shoes is that the area on the pivot point of the sole is supposed to have less grip to the floor, thereby making the twists, turns, and slides that are a big part of Zumba easier to perform and easier on the wearer's knees. Unfortunately, this is not the case--this area on the pivot point of the soles grips just as tightly to the floor as the rest of the sole. I was so excited to try get these shoes and try them out because my knees have really been hurting due to these twists and turns and my previous shoes not moving smoothly enough and gripping the floor during these moves. My knees hurt even worse after wearing these shoes, but that's probably because I really went all out in that class because I thought the shoes would do what they are advertised to do. Additionally, the insole of this shoe is 1/8" thick. This is less support and thickness than many dress shoes! Zumba is a high-impact exercise--there should be 2-3 times as much support in the insoles of these shoes. I gave them the one star for lightness and flexibility as well as their wide toe box, however. So, if you modify these shoes by removing the insoles and replacing them with something more cushioned and supportive and get yourself a pair of dancesox (they're available out here on Amazon) and slip them over the front of the shoes, you can make these shoes work for you.

My husband ordered these boots for me out of my Amazon wish list and surprised me for my birthday this year. These are my first real pair of boots (other than some ones my mom got me from the Goodwill when I was a kid) and I'm totally surprised at how comfortable they are right out of the box! I love them! The color of the distressed leather is gorgeous, and I love the turquoise highlights and stitching, too. I normally need a wide shoe to be comfortable because I have a fat foot - these are B in width and are absolutely perfect. The cushioning and support on the inside of the boot is fantastic - the tag calls it ATS Technology, which stands for "Advanced Torque Stability." The ATS system: wicks moisture away from the foot, has a gel-cushioned footbed with heel stabilizer for shock absorption and control, and boasts a lightweight, composite forked shank that provides advanced stability. I played football in them the first time I wore them and they were very comfortable.

The boot outsole is made of carbon rubber Duratread, said to "last longer than traditional rubber outsoles" while being "highly resistant to manure and acidic waste." It also offers superior traction and maximum energy absorption for increased comfort.

That's from the tag, by the way.

I like these, and they're good Toms quality, as always. Positives are that the design on the top is vivid, more so than it appears in the photo here (but it's not glaring). It's eye-grabbing, but not in a weird way. The burlap tones down the design and makes it easy to match with everyday clothes. It's also breathable, which is a real plus in the summer months.

Amazon has a lot of auto-questions about fit, and they're hard to answer for this item. I rated these somewhat small and somewhat narrow, even though I got the size I always wear in Toms. The reason for that is that the burlap fabric is less forgiving and stretch-friendly than canvas Classics: the latter are a lot easier to break in and stretch to fit your foot a lot more quickly. At first, it's hard to wedge your foot into these, and I definitely didn't go out on long walks with them on. They did start to stretch, but it was definitely a process: if you don't want to mess with that or have bothersome foot issues, maybe consider canvas Toms instead (that's what I'm planning to stick with in the future). I answered that these do have good arch support, but I'm going to add another rider on that one: I have odd arches, and almost any shoe with "normal" arch support is extremely uncomfortable. I'm not entirely sure how to word this clearly, but if shoes with standard arch support aren't ideal for you-- and you prefer a shoe with minimal or no built-in support instead-- this is one alternative.

In short: These are cute, fashionable, quirky but not downright weird, and a good wardrobe piece. However, they're not for all feet.

I ran in these shoes for one season and did several races in them (trail runs and Spartans).  I purchased them looking for a trail shoe alternative to Inov8 because inov8's are notoriously difficult to size correctly and i have not been impressed with their durability thus far.  Altar's description is pretty accurate.  I almost returned them for a half size smaller because the wider toes box made them feel a bit on the loose side however, after a handful of runs I decided the fit was right it was simply a width I was not used to so my advice is to trust the sizing guide.  Pros:  Very comfortable and stable.  For 'barefoot' type shoes they have plenty of padding and never made my feet or knees sore.  I cannot recall ever rolling an ankle while wearing these which I attribute to the wide sole.  The extended heel is an excellent feature and saved me from several falls.  Cons: The tread is not very aggressive.... they work well for dirt roads and moderate trails but don't have quite enough bite on loose or wet terrain.  They are not a great option for OCR races.....a rope burned all the way through the side walls of mine after just one ascent/decent of a 15ft rope and I had to throw them away.  I would recommend these strongly for someone wanting a shoe for runs and races with mixed terrain.  The zero drop construction combined with a wide padded sole makes them ideal for long, moderate trail runs.  I would not recommend them to anyone wanting a shoe for OCR's, steep trails or off trail running.

Why does Merrell keep messing with a good thing? My first pair of Merrel's was a pair of the Chameleon 3's and they were an incredible fit right out of the box and lasted for years...I still use them for yard work.

Then I got pair of C4's and overall they were a step back. The durability has been pretty good, especially since they felt cheaper than than the C3's they replace, but they have held up nicely. But, the fit has never been right and even after a long time of wearing, they are less than comfortable.

So, when it came time to buy a new pair, I was nervous. The new Primes looked more like the C3 and the garish colors were gone, so I thought I would give them a try and just like the C4's it is mixed bag.

One of the things I liked about the C4s were the Vibram soles, they were durable and gave good traction without tracking too much of the outdoors...indoors and that is gone. The new soles look more like the C3's and they weren't bad, so I can live with it.

The toe and heel guards on higher than the C4's, which is a good thing and the overall construction seems a little more durable, but the problem is once again fit.

Once, you get these one, they are actually pretty comfortable...definitely much better than the C4's...but someone decided to make the back of the shoe higher, which leads to the foot opening being much smaller and incredibly challenging to put. I could slip my foot into my C3's with no assistance and the C4's usually need a finger to straighten out the edge of the sock, but the Prime's require both hands and quite a bit of jiggering to get on. Once you get past this, the fit is pretty good. Not sure what they changed about the sock, but these shoes are definitely hotter than the C4's and a lot hotter than the C3's. Not sure I could wear these all day on a Summer day.

Finally, that extra height at the back of the shoe changes the appearance and it is hard to notice in a picture on Amazon, but the C4's stop about an inch below the ankle and give plenty of wiggle room, but the Primes run right up against the ankle and could lead to rubbing when walking on uneven surfaces. I can see where the extra height would be beneficial when walking in wet environments, but it just doesn't work for me.

I am pretty sure these shoes will hold up for quite some time, but I am not excited about spending a couple of years with a pair of shoes that are uncomfortable like the C4's were.

Other than the color, the size, and late delivery, I can speak highly of these shoes, when compared to others. I purchased my first pair of this same shoe in November 2013 and really liked them. These, that I just purchased, must be an updated model since my first pair weren't labeled "2." They are the only minimalist shoe that is actually a shoe, but only a few millimeters under your feet. Most other minimalist shoes have much more sole, "support," or a drop--I did a lot of searching before I found these. The only other shoes that come close are Vibram 5-fingers, which are not practical for me and aren't very aesthetically pleasing or xero shoes, which are great sometimes, but they are only made in roped sandals.

There are a few downfalls. My last pair only lasted 1.5years before they had large holes where the mesh met the sole....under a year if you count from when the holes started. This is not ideal since the shoes are quite expensive. I paid $85 for a pair of shoes that started getting holes in under a year, and they weren't the only shoes I wore. I have a beef with the price of minimalist shoes in general since they are just a vibram sole, which I can purchase for about $20 retail and then some mesh with laces. Other than the price/durability ratio, I'd really like it if these shoes had elastic mesh like the 5-finger so that it would mold even better with the shape of my foot. I've contacted Vibram 5-fingers, and a 1-toe shoe isn't likely.

Were these shoes $40-50 they would be just fine. But for twice this you should expect a better and more reliable shoe.

This is a quality insole. But, for someone looking for good arch support and an insole that isn't too thick/bulky in your shoe, my absolute favorite among all insoles I've tried is the regular Powerstep Pinnacle (blue color). I've bought and worn both Powerstep versions, because I wanted to see which would work best for me. And, IMO, the regular Pinnacle is a thinner insole than the Maxx, not surprisingly, but also feels like it has a somewhat higher and more supportive arch support element.

In other words, my feet feel OK when I put the Pinnacle Maxx in my shoes. But my feet feel really great when I put the regular Pinnacle blue version in my shoes. And, I should add, I'm a guy who's 6-8 tall and about 275 lbs. So, if I'm getting good support from the regular Pinnacle, it's hard for me to imagine who's going to need more support than me with the Maxx -- unless for some reason, you just want a thicker insole in your shoe. As far as cushioning and comfort is concerned, I didn't find the Maxx to be superior to the regular Pinnacle at all.

The Cole Haan dress shoes arrived yesterday, and I very excited/anxious to be receiving them. I ordered them for a close friend's wedding, since I was invited to be an usher. I figured it was time to update my shoes, since my last ones were on the verge of retirement. Easier said than done for a poor college student. It took a good chunk out of my paycheck, but I was able to order the shoes just in time for the wedding with 3 days to spare. Well, I can honestly say when the shoes arrived they were, I sure was surprised (both in a good and bad way.) The shoes themselves are of really good quality. I've worn many dress shoes throughout my life (my family is religious.), and there are some things that I would like to point out about these shoes. Some dress shoes the leather is softer, more pliable, than others; well, not this shoe. These are as stiff as a board, with very little give. That can be a good or bad thing depending on one's opinion. I personally like dress shoes that way. With the shoe being so stiff, it does mean they'll be taking some breaking in. Now I bet your wondering why if I liked the shoe, that I gave them one star. Here's why. The pair of shoes I received, well, it was obvious that they were used. To be honest, I expected shoes that had been tried on like you would expect in a shoe stores (it's hard to find a pair of shoes that haven't at least been tried on once by someone else.) The issue I have, it that the pair I received was obviously used/abused for a couple days, then returned. There are scuffs around the shoe, but scuffs aren't hard to polish out. The heal is worn, by outside use if I could guess (concrete/pavement) it's harder to wear down the heel of a shoe on carper or tiles. The shoes also have permanent creases already from excessive use (still livable, since I was only going to do this to the shoes myself.) But the biggest issue was the gash taken out of the side of one of the shoes. Everything else could be seen as normal use or polished out. Holes in leather shoes are harder to cover, and all you really can do is try to make them less noticeable. However, this was the breaking point for me. If I wanted a pair of used shoes, I would have bought used shoes. I would love to return them, but I need them for my friend's wedding. And I'm not one of the people that would use the shoe for a day and then return them (as you can see already happened to these shoes already.) So for a recap:

Point:
---Comfortable fit, seem well-made (duh, they're Merrells)
---Breathe marginally better than shoes with full-leather-uppers
Counterpoint:
---"Mesh" descriptions imply the mesh is solid straight through to the inside of the shoe, but it is not. This might have been okay, but
---Inner lining of shoe doesn't breathe well
Conclusion:
---Great shoes for Summer in upper Catskills, avoid if you live south of Pennsylvania, and if you live south of Virginia, there's a good chance nothing much will help you stay cool outside anyway...
-------
If you live anywhere with temperatures regularly above 85 Fahrenheit, don't buy these. The "mesh" uppers on these are mostly aesthetic, and rest atop a solid layer of cloth. At the time of buying these shoes last November, I thought my 2-year search for affordable, versatile leather nude-for-me flats was over. Alas, it was winter and I didn't get a chance to wear them outside. Then I forgot I had them until June. These shoes turned out to be a major disappointment and I will be donating mine to charity as they are unwearable.  I encountered 2 problems: 1. The leather is really hard and rough inside the toe box. I have worn my share of bad shoes, but these are the only ones that drew blood on 4 toes after just a leisurely 30 min walk. I was wearing nylon stockings. I actually got these shoes in 2 sizes, picked the one that was slightly loose and returned the smaller pair, so sizing was not the issue.  2. The leather discolored extremely easily. On my first day of wearing these shoes, a single drop of water splashed onto one shoe. It left a dark spot that did not go away after the water had dried.  I tried blotting but it was really completely dry. Then I tried leather cleaner that I have used on other light colored leather products. To my surprise, after the leather cleaner dried, the shoes are now badly mottled with a lighter color...except for the dark spot where the water drop used to be. This is absolutely ridiculous! I didn't soak them in water. It was just a single drop splashed from a faucet!  So yeah, unless you don't walk at all in your shoes and don't ever go near any liquids, save your money and stay away from these shoes.

Finally I've found a relatively speaking "cute" shoe since I was recently relegated to full orthopedic inserts.  My unusually large inserts fit these shoes very well without showing much in the back and sides.  What does show is quite unnoticeable.  I am happily surprised since I thought I might have to give up on "dressier" sandals.  I have a fused ankle and rod in tibia and usually require a rocker shoe (which this is not but it still works for me).  The footbed is removable and is very deep.  I have "dress" orthotics as well which have a lower profile and also fit perfectly.  If I need to add a lift at toe and/or heel, these also fit.  If I want to wear them with the provided footbed only, they are VERY comfortable.  I found them true to size.  I can wear 5.5 or 6, and I bought 5.5 and they fit very well.  I also think I could wear the 6 since I bought a 6 in another similar shoe made by same manufacturer.  One thing to be aware of is that the Beige Multi Python Print (which is greyish/tan/blue/beige) -- the printed part/design -- may not be exactly the same on the top of each shoe.  I might order one more pair just to see if I can get a little better match on the design.  One of mine has quite a bit more blue on the top of the straps while the other one is more gray/beige which I prefer since it looks more neutral - this is the only reason I gave it a 4 vs. 5.  Arch support is good - I have high arches.  I would not say the arch support is superior, though. One more thing - even with my deep orthotics and high arches, the velcro straps are plenty long enough.  The inside of the shoes and straps are very smooth so while I normally have to wear a protective band around my foot due to thin skin grafts, I don't even have to wear it with these since they do not rub at all.  These shoes are very, very, very, very comfortable!  I will be buying another pair in a different color.

The basic Army boot, size 9W, has been my mainstay for 19 years. They have delivered many miles of support across hardball, shifting sands and mountainous terrain. Now I'm looking for a civilian boot to take over my non-work related hiking and outdoor activities.

After several months of reviews and trying on different pairs, including a purchase-return of Merrill Energys, I finally settled on the Keen Targhee II. I like the roomy toe box and grippy soles. The first two weeks included work around the home and minor walking. They were hot, much hotter than Army boots and stiff. I thought they just needed some break-in love. Then we took a family day hike off the Blue Ridge Parkway (everyone should do this!) and several long walks back home. At six hours I was sore, eight was crippling me and by ten hours I was repeatedly taking them off and on. I tried tying the laces tight, leaving them loose and several combinations in between. Nothing was helpful.

I feel like the shoe pushes my foot into the toe box and continuously smashes my toes at the tip. My heel never feels secured, leaving some unpredictability to my foot response on uneven terrain. These are a size 10D.

Maybe I don't know how to lace a boot properly... whatever the case, it's just not working. My initial rating was four in the store, two around the house and finally settling on a three star rating.

The Soles are confidence inspiring, especially on wet Appalachian rocks and muddy mountainous trails. They will grip anything, much superior to the Army's choice of sole. These sunglasses are made well. They have polarized lenses which add so much clarity to things, especially around water. They have springy arms which means that they won't stretch or break on larger faces and will spring back to fit smaller ones. I have the smoke color and the protections is good. They aren't too dark but they block the sun well while allowing me to clearly see everything. I originally got these for my husband and they really are a tad wide on me but I liked the clarity so I kept them. He loses. Ha!

I have some sunglasses that actually feel like they are prescription glasses - and not MY prescription. I don't know why that is but they make me feel a bit wobbly and there is a bit of distortion that bugs me. These glasses are crystal clear as far as distortion which is the main reason I kept them. That and the polarized lenses which many fashion sunglasses do not have.

They are, though, a bit wide as I mentioned. I think they are better for larger faces. But they don't slip down or cause any issues and they look fine on me. They're a big change from my usual oversize glasses or my mirrored wayfarers. I like them and feel they are high quality. They are pricier than many cheap fashion glasses but they're worth it because they are well made and have such good clarity. I am going with 4 stars. I wish they were a bit narrower but that's just because of my small face, not the glasses. These are a great choice for people who want sunglasses for hiking, fishing, and almost any activity. Really cheap sunglasses are fine for lounging by the pool but when you need clarity, you need to look beyond style to functionality.

I am very disappointed in the comfort and fit of these turfs. I have wide feet and immediately noticed how narrow the sole of these shoes feels, especially when cutting or turning sharply--it feels like I am about to turn an ankle every time I change directions. Despite feeling too tight width-wise, I noticed my feet sliding forward to the toe when stopping quickly; I am wearing the correct size, and they feel snug putting them on, but that doesn't carry over to the field.

Undoubtedly the worst part of these shoes is the tongue. It is made of a cheap plastic material which has an unfinished edge that is simply sewn together. See those two humps on the tongue--just so happens that these slide back and forth against my skin, wearing a bloody wound into the front of my ankles. I thought this would get better with use--it hasn't. I tried putting bandaids over the wounds, they fell off; I tried wearing higher, thicker socks, which kind of helped, but now the socks have a worn-out patch in them wear the tongue rubs them.

Unfortunately, I bought these on Amazon and cannot return them. I will order from Zappos in the future--much better return policy. Not sure if I will be wearing Adidas turfs in the future.

TL;DR: If you hate your feet and enjoy pain, get these shoes!

The problem is that the back of the shoe is quite rigid.  I dislike returning things, so will try these once more with double socks; if that removes the attrition I will keep them, for I do like the other features of this shoe and Teva generally.  I need a little more ankle support than most, so go for something in between a low back fit and very high fit (the latter limiting foot pivot mobility).  This shoe is in that in between, but is so rigid in the back to cause the bleeding.

This purse was perfect for the first four-or-so months. Really great looking for work, nicely sturdy, with a smooth and convenient carry strap. It felt really well made. I liked that it had an open area plus at least one zippered pouch.

Then one day, one of the zippers split open while it was supposed to be closed. I could force-correct the zipper to close and work for awhile, but it kept happening. After a while, the splitting occurred more frequently to the point that one side pouch it really doesn't stay closed and the other opens at inopportune times. In full disclosure, I carry some lumpy stuff - a big key ring, a bi-fold wallet, big sunglasses, a cellphone, and small tablet (sometimes) and various other bits and bobs. I think the lumpiness of my purse's contents maybe caused the zipper(s) to bend awkwardly since they're along the outside edges of the purse. In any case, if you like a medium sized satchel with pockets to carry a lot of stuff, you might be better with one that has a zipper pouch through the middle and a magnetic clasp across the top.

Also, I purchased my purse at Macy's though it's this exact style.

I've been an Amazon customer for years, and this product compelled me to leave my very first review! Yes, the fabric is soft and cushy, but the design is seriously flawed, and the quality seems more fitting of a $10 slipper from Payless.

But in order to get the front part of the strap tight enough so that your foot doesn't slide through, the back part of the strap is too tight and pinches your foot. When I spent 20 minutes adjusting the strap to something that could potentially work, the velcro started scratching my foot when I walked.

Even if I didn't struggle with the fit (which was definitely not a sizing problem), having a "flip-flop" style sandal is not the best thing for your foot, if you're home and trying to rehabilitate it (in my case, I just have high arches, wooden floors, and incredibly sore feet at the end of the day). You are still engaging foot muscles you normally wouldn't have to engage with a heeled slipper.

And even if I didn't struggle with ALL of the above, I still wouldn't recommend this slipper. It's severely overpriced. I'm up for paying a little more than I normally would for a product that I love, but this just left me with a feeling of being ripped off (kind of a first for me here on Amazon, hence the first-time review).

As far as their usefulness as described (see to read, see your computer, see across the desk) there is not much rhyme or reason as to where the sweet spots are placed. I have a normal size face but the lenses are not symmetrical. The sweet spot for the right lens is within the inside one quarter of the lens (you almost have to look at your nose to use this area) while the left lens doesn't seem to have a spot where my eye can focus; certainly there are not areas in both lenses where my eyes can both use the magnification at the same time. Lastly, the most powerful area of both lenses is right along the bottom border within about a 1/4 inch area meaning that I have to tip my head uncomfortably back in order to focus, plus there is the issue of not having an alignment between my eyes while doing this so I pretty much have to move my head left and right until I decide that it's close enough. I bought these to try and end the headaches from using a computer screen at work for several hours while I interview clients but they are way over-rated. I'd return them if my son didn't toss out the packaging, and I think I'll see if they will take them back regardless! I also want to note that I wore progressive lenses for several years before I had the lenses in my eyes replaced and never had a problem finding the focal point for the distance I had to deal with at the time.

I purchased these as an alternative to wearing flip-flops or sandals during warm weather. The idea was to keep my feet cool and let them breathe, but with the added benefit of sneaker traction and styling. Also, I wanted a little more stablilty and control that wearing sport slides doesn't provide. I wear a size 12.5 and my feet are a little wider than normal. I ordered these in size 13. The styling and appearance of these shoes was impressive right out of the box. Initially, these shoes were a bit uncomfortable to my feet. I took my time to break them in. A few days around the house, then some short jaunts out of the house. Like other reviewers noted, these shoes fit a bit small and narrow, specifically across the top of the foot and in the toebox. After wearing them for a couple of months, they have broken in and are more comfortable now. I wear them with the laces very loose and the tongues tucked up over the ledge of the upper lace bracket. All I need to do to secure the shoes is pull on the laces to tighten them quickly if the mission requires it ! The entire shoe is very breathable, except for the tounge and toebox, which are made of solid neoprene. Amazon had these priced about $30.00 lower than retail, and I purchased them with an Amazon gift card (thanks Dad)! I would not recommend these to people with large feet, but folks with average or smaller-than-average feet should be fine with these. I don't use these for water sports, so I can't report on that aspect of performance.

The faux leather material is nice but it did have a bit of a funky smell, I don't notice it as much after a few days so hopefully it is wearing off. The pocket on the outside is functional but I'm not sure you could put much in it without it looking bulgy as it is pretty small. These boots seem well-made and sturdy with good waterproofing, so it's too bad they didn't work for me. First of all I usually wear 7.5-8 women's, so based on the reviews here, I ordered a size 8 to be safe. But even with thick socks and plastic orthotics, the boots were too big -- my heel kept moving around when I walked.
That would have been tolerable if not for the fact that the boots were WAY too hot. Ontario summers are hot, and these were uncomfortably hot even when worn indoors in June with thin socks, before the temperature really rises. They are not going to work for me through the summer.
Far worse was the fact that the soles were actually slippery on wet surfaces. That was the clincher. Sucks because the big treads in the photo made them look really safe.
Additionally, these boots add a lot of height -- they're like platform shoes, I don't know why the soles are so thick -- which felt weird. It was like I couldn't feel the ground with my feet when I walked, so I felt a little unstable walking in them.
Had to return them, which means I lost a stupid amount of money in unrefunded import fees and the shipping cost of sending them back. I'll never order shoes through Amazon again -- I just have to be able to try them on and return them without penalty.

Since it's not clear from the product title that these shoes are for girls only, and we took the M and W in the sizing choices to signify men's or women's (boys' or girls') rather than medium and wide sizes, my new bride and I purchased a pair for her young son/my stepson to wear in our wedding when we couldn't find similar saddle shoes to match mine in local department stores. We were profoundly disappointed (understatement) to discover far from home and with the big day at hand that he couldn't wear them due to the mistake. He wore hiking shoes, since it was that or sneakers. It was all we could do to drag him out of the room without dress shoes, he was so mortified. After the wedding, when we looked up the product page and discovered how this had happened, he told me that he wanted to burn the shoes, he was so disgusted. We left them behind in our room, and I hope they end up with a girl who can wear and enjoy them.

Yes, the detailed product description posted far down the product page (off-screen beneath other info and rows of related products) indicates that the shoes are for girls. So one could say this was our mistake. But we never saw the details, nor felt the need to go hunting for them, since all the info we thought we needed appeared at the top of the page and on the sizing and order screens. I hope the good folks at School Issue Footwear, who presumably didn't intend to mislead anyone, will revise the product title to make it clear that these shoes are intended and sized for girls only, so that other parents aren't similarly disappointed. When they do, I'll be glad to revise this review.

I grew up without foot binding so my toes are straight and fan out wide. Thanks to that I have never had foot issues of any kind but I cannot find shoes that fit. I used to run in Instincts, but the latest version 3 has much narrower toe boxes with uncomfortable hard plastic toe cap that restrict toe-splay. When I was about to give up on Altra, this new version of One came out and it seems to work well. The One2.5 has a curved last with very wide toes with narrow heels, completely different from the Instinct's straight last with narrow toes and wide heels. The One2 had extremely shallow toe boxes that make the shoes effectively smaller even when the sole patterns are the same, but apparently Altra addressed that issue with the One2.5. When you compare the profiles of One2 and One2.5 you will clearly see that One2.5 toe boxes are taller almost by a half inch and thus more give to allow for better toe splay, but the fit of heels are snug so they do not swim inside like in Instinct 3. One of Altra's weakness has been durability so I will see how it goes (it does not feel any more durable though).  For me finding shoes that fit is so hard that I have to be content with just that, but Altra's inability to find the sweet spot and stay there is pretty frustrating. The great concepts (zero-drop, wide toe box...) have been ruined by some weird extreme changes between versions, and quality controls. At this point I have limited confidence with them and I will stockpile on One2.5 so I can weather another swing to the other extremes in the near future.

Altra shoes basically healed me. Seriously! I had suspected PF for almost a year. We went head to head on the best shoe for me, he wanted support and I do best with zero drop minimalist however I'm not your typical light weight good form minimalist runner. I tried everything, however, including the hated "support" shoes. As we kept trying to treat whatever was going on and not getting better, he theorized it might be nerve entrapment. Sure enough, that is what it was! It wasn't a common one. PT suggested Altra, I had never heard of the brand.

From the minute I put them on, it did not hurt to run. It didn't hurt to walk, my form improved, and it was absolute perfection. I started in the Torin and have gone through different models, the latest being the Provision.

The Provision (not Provisioness, as someone else mentioned) is billed as a support shoe but I see it as more of a suggestion to your foot instead of wearing concrete blocks. It was comfortable from the onset. I got less miles on them than in the Torin but maybe it was the support component that started to go.

Size up. I can't emphasize that enough. I wear size 11 in Brooks, I wear size 12 in Altra. The shoes are wide, at first they might seem too wide. That is intended. There are alternative lacing options on their website, it's a good thing to look at. They're more for running than walking but if you want to walk in them and they work for you, that great!

A few words of caution. If you haven't ever been fit in them before or worn them, get fitted or try on a pair before ordering online. These shoes are different and it'll take you a bit to get used to them. It helps to have someone good verify your size that way you're not second guessing when you get them and end up sending them back. That's not fair to Amazon and you're spending too much time on trial and error. Best thing? Maybe purchase a pair "in person" somewhere and once you learn what you like, THEN order online that way you're not taking up a salespersons time then not giving them a sale. I purchased my Torins at a store -- I order online now mainly because I know the shoe better and I am womens size 12, it is rare to find a store that carries both the brand and the exact shoe I want in the size I need.

Break into them slowly if you aren't used to zero drop. Go easy on the hills until your calves are used to it.

Give them time. They feel SO wide at first. After a while your foot and toes will spread out and it'll seem normal.

Lastly, realize as awesome as the shoes are, they aren't all magical and stuff. So many shoes promise so much -- these won't make you faster or stronger or less tired at the end of a run, etc. They WILL allow you to do it yourself :) There will be times I'm out there thinking "why don't the shoes feel cushiony-er or why don't I feel like I'm floating on air" and I realize what I need to do is turn over my stride a bit more and improve my form. These shoes make it super easy to help you help yourself.

Once I started with this brand I have not looked back nor have I been tempted to. When I went to Altra, I was a brand ambassador for another brand. By going to Altra, I actually had to start buying all my own shoes and not getting some of the perks I did before. I have no regrets on my decision. (The other brand is incredible and work for other people -- just not me.)

I must admit, I was quite impressed with this bag. Mine looked a tad bit different from the pictures in the listing. My zipper was not all black. It was gold. And there is a logo name on one side. See pics.

Perfect sized bag for my 13" macbook and files. The bag does not have feet so beware of putting it on the ground or "dragging" it. The straps are a nice length. It is long enough for me to wear on my shoulder and keep the bag tight against my body. Yet, short enough for me to hold it by the handles and walk with my arms down without dragging it on the floor. I'm 5'2".

The outer zipper pocket is big enough to hold my iphone 6 plus with wallet case (standing up). It's a bit of a tight squeeze if I try to lay it down completely inside the pocket. Any other smaller phone would fit much easier.

The interior has a nice lining that does not feel flimsy at all. There are multiple slip/open top pockets on both sides and one zippered pocket. It also has a nice long strap with lobster clip for holding your keys. I love this feature because I no longer have to dig for my keys as I walk to my car.

The bag material is synthetic leather and you can tell at first sight. It has a grainy texture and even smells like plastic. This bag has is well finished. Meaning, the straps, the stitching, etc is well done for a non name brand purse. There are a few stray strands of brown strings that I could see on the inside from the lining, but other than that, the straps did not have fraying. The stitching was nice and tight and the pockets were well sewn.

My favorite thing about this purse is its weight. It's VERY VERY light. I can't stand bags that weigh a lot when its empty. Add your stuff to it and you may as well skip the gym. I added pictures and everything you see in the one picture all fit inside the purse and I could zip it shut. Capacity is pretty good. The base/gusset is nice and wide.

Personally, I would pay about $25 tops for this purse just because it is not real leather. But as far as usability, practicality, and quality goes, this is a decent purse for those who don't care about name brands or the smell of leather.

My suggestions on how they can improve this purse:
Use a better zipper for the main compartment. The current zipper is a little sticky when opening and closing.
Add feet to the bottom of the bag.

I purchased this shoe in both 3-6 months (for my niece) and 12-18 months (for my nephew). I was looking for a shoe with a soft and flexible sole because research has found that hard soles are not good for babies' development. These little shoes are so adorable, good quality and they are super easy to slip on baby's foot.

The outside of the shoe is a leather-like material and the inside of the shoe (the insert and toe box) are terry cloth (similar to an infant wash cloth). The insert is soft (for the bottom of baby's foot) and has a good cushion. The sole is a flexible "suede-like" material, allowing for proper growth and foot formation for baby.

An elastic band around the "ankle" of the shoe expands and contracts with ease, making it a breeze to slide the shoe on and keeping the shoe on baby's foot. My 13 month old nephew wore the shoes and walked around (even on carpet a linoleum) with no issues. He seemed comfortable and the shoes seemed to support his balance. However, after wearing the shoe for some time and removing the shoe, I noticed a slightly red imprint on the top his foot from the elastic band. I do not think the elastic band hurt him and it did not cut off any circulation. He was wearing the 12-18 month shoe. I will update this review once I am able to try the 3-6 month old shoe on my infant niece (she's currently too small).

I coach a high school baseball team and had my last pair of turf shoes for two years. While the shoe fits and looks great, I found that the sole started to peel off shortly after my fist time using them. I used some super glue to repair, however as the weather heated up, it seamed as though the sole of the shoe simply could not handle the heat of the turf. For those who aren't familiar, the temperature of synthetic turf surfaces are often much warmer than the temperature of the air. the black rubber pellets in turf attract the heat and insulate it, making for a very hot surface. In about a month, I had large pieces of the sole missing and just went back to using my old Mizuno shoes. It was very unfortunate because I loved the look and feel of the shoe. It just did not have the durability needed to endure baseball exercises on a synthetic turf surface.

If you're looking for a minimalist trail shoe...keep looking.  I had high hopes for these based on some other good reviews on the Internet, but honestly, I was disappointed with the product.  For one, they're very narrow and obviously not built along an anatomical last, so any long-term running (e.g., over about five miles at a time) will result in discomfort due to the inability of the shoe to let the foot splay naturally.  I tried running in my house wearing the NB XC900 on one foot and my old shoes (Inov-8s) on the other, and in minutes, the foot with the NB shoe started to hurt in the arch from the foot being unable to spread out. Not only were the laces annoyingly short, but the tongue tended to stab me in the upper foot no matter what I did, and even though I wore socks, it protruded over the top edge of the sock to stab me anyway.  Although the soles gripped on tile, they slipped on other surfaces, and I'd be genuinely leery of trying them on wet rocks or asphalt.  In short, I am really not sure what kind of running New Balance expects people to do in these shoes?

I got two pairs of these from Macy's. I got a black and a brown pair. The black pair is absolutely terrific. The brown pair, however, has a couple major problems.

As I had hoped, the black pair creases in the area of the pleats as I walk. A couple months later and there are hardly any creases in this area at all, because it seems that most of the strain is absorbed by the pleats.

But the brown pair...creases exactly where I had hoped they wouldn't, right in front of the pleats. in fact no flex at all seems to occur on the pleats, and so there is even more strain than usual in one particular spot. Literally within one week, deep cracks and creases began to form in front of the pleats. This might not be so bad if not for the second major problem...the dye job.

The dye on the brown pair is terrible. Every little bit of wear to the shoe, from the creases when walking, to accidentally bumping your shoe against your office chair, rubs the dye clean off of the shoe. Yet somehow, no color is absorbed into these areas during a polish (except slightly in the creases in front of the pleats), so every little rub results in a permanent and obvious color change to the shoe (pictures included of both the black and brown pairs...freshly polished).

I even brought the brown pair into a professional to ask about polishing techniques, and immediately after looking at them he said the dye job "could have been better." I hadn't even mentioned the dye to him or any of the wear that I was concerned about. I'm thinking of sending these pictures to Stacy Adams and seeing what they think. But this is going to stay a 2 star in the meantime.

I would recommend the black pair, but the brown I'm sure won't even be wearable in another couple months of regular use around the office.

First let's have the good news. I like the color (white & light gray), which has not been available in this brand of running shoes at our local super store for several months. Unfortunately, most of the rest of what I have to tell you is not so good. I' ve been buying Dr. Scholl's running shoes at our local super store for a couple of years now. Being retired and fairly active, these are the shoes I tend to wear daily. I have no issues what so ever with the quality of Dr. Scholl's running shoes. All of my running shoes are ten and one-half, including the pair being reviewed.

The problem is in the fit. The local super store sells wide width as opposed to medium width (width of the Amazon purchase). That being said, the main problems looks and feels like the length, not the width. I've included a picture of the new and old shoes, although the relative tightness associated with the new shoes is demonstrably more noticeable than the picture would suggest. The new shoes feel a bit tight, although not to the point of being substantially uncomfortable. They do become uncomfortably tighter when I had an additional Dr. Scholl's heal gel pad. My older pair has both a second full length gel pad and heal pad without feeling the least bit tight. I like the additional padding because I sometimes walk several miles a day.

My solution is avoid buying these from Amazon again. Another solution might have been to have ordered these shoes in at least a half size larger. Since I don't want to make a career out of buying shoes, I'll settle for a less than desirable color in a pair of Dr. Scholl's running shoes at our local super store. By the way, the automated feedback from Amazon suggested that a fair number of folks found their shoes to be somewhat small as well. I bought these boots after reviewing many different styles and am satisfied with the fit, comfortably and support they provide.  One of the main reasons I picked these boots is because they have a side zip.  The reason I gave a Three star rating versus a Four/Five is because of the side zip.  I work at a location that requires pat searches to enter, this includes removing footwear.  My expectation of having a side zip boot was so I could easily remove and put on my boots without having to retie them.  If this was the sole mission of these boots I have to say they fail.  Removing them using the side zip is no problem, however trying to put them back on is next to impossible.  They have a piece of material that expands but connects each side of the zipper, restricting how far you can separate each side of the zipper when unzipped.  Unfortunately, this piece of material prevents one from putting your foot back into the boot without untying the laces.  I have thought about cutting the material out or at the least down the middle to allow the boot to expand enough and allow the boots to be put on without untying.  I have not as of yet, and feel I should not have to alter a product in order to make it work properly.  On the positive side, I work on my feet for a 13 hour shift and the boots are comfortable.

A really comfortable fitting boot in the shop turned into a mini-nightmare when put to the test of a five day walk. Across the granular environment of the Fish River Canyon sand filtered into the mesh covered tongue and got between the inner lining and upper where more and more became become trapped. After two days this caused increasingly painful pressure on the toes. Initially I assumed my feet were swelling. They weren't: the shoes had bulged with trapped sand.  When I tried to dislodge the sand it just spread around between the rest of the lining. On probing between tongue and lining my finger slipped through.  (picture of just some of the sand that came out of the shoes' lining)  That it happened to both shoes suggests it is not just a faulty item, but a design flaw. It probably means the same thing happens with water; this site has a number of complaints about waterproofing issues on these shoes.  What it also means is that this model of shoe does not appear to have been properly tested. Or if they have, then the company has ignored the results.  The company care and maintenance literature was of no help. Contact with the company proved to be a drawn out process with no results.

I love Adidas, just about everything they put their name on.  I think they've got some serious work to do though to get their running shoes up to their standards.  On the plus side: they're sturdy, the sole is thick, and there's a decent amount of padding.  Overall they're a decent shoe.  But that's the problem: they're just decent, and Adidas shoes should be the best.  On the minus side, the biggest challenge I have with these is ergonomics.  There is some form to these, but it's not enough, especially in key places.  As a result the high pressure areas of the sole don't have enough support and the places that don't need much get more than they need...it's like an even level across the board.  For ex. the sole is thick, but it feels like a uniform thickness in all areas.  Side support is the same, and it mirrors the lack of form to the lateral shape of the sole.  No matter how tight I tie these, I continuously tempt callouses on both my toes and front pad because there's not enough form-fit support to provide the right amount of traction between foot and sole.  That should never happen.  This shoe runs fit-wise about 1/2 size larger than it should also (I fit 9.5 US and these run about 1/2cm too long).  Width feels fine though, and I have wide feet.  The last issue I have is with moisture: the outside material is porous, which would be fine if the insides provided breathe-ability, but they don't.  As a result, 10' of running through grass with moisture soaks through running socks, and there's no air circulation to boot.  Overall it's a decent shoe, but just decent.

After literally hours of research between 8-9 shoe brands, I narrowed it down to these, the Salamons or the Hokas.  All of the representatives were knowledgeable, asked good questions and gave good feedback for my particular needs, which were a good cross-trainer, as I walk and run in every outing, as I grow to more running than walking. I also needed a shoe that could easily adapt to changing terrain, as I run on concrete, paved roads, gravel roads and dirt trails all in the same outing. And finally, I did NOT want a show with a drawstring lace. This may be the new fad, but I see it as something that will just wear out in less than a year and replacement 'laces' are expensive.  So, with all of those requirements in mind, that is how I shopped for my new pair of running shoes. I also wanted decent cushioning, not perhaps as much as the Hokas brand, but a decent amount without adding weight or that clunky feel with thick bottomed athletic shoes. The cushioning on these is perfect.  As an aside: as a former Nike customer, I can say with full confidence now that Nike shoes are garbage. (Sorry, Nike fans). This Merrell All out Charge is the lightest, most comfortable running shoe I have ever owned. It effortlessly adapts to changing surfaces without a hitch. And as an added bonus the tongue is sewn to the shoe on the inside right, so it never slips to the left or right. Very nice. I can't say enough good things about this shoe.

First pair ordered from the Prime sale were not authentic. These WERE BOUGHT FROM AMAZON and not a third party seller. The first red flag regarding the authenticity of the glasses was the inferior "RB" etching on the right lens. It was done in such a manner that not only could you feel it, but you could also see it from 5-10 feet away as it looked like the lens was damaged (scratch, etc.). Authentic "RB" etchings are nearly imperceptible and not something that can be easily seen from several feet away. The second, even larger red flag was the presence of a plastic seam on the top of the frame that was easily felt running across the entire length of the front of the sunglasses as well as down the top side of the arms. Authentic Ray-Ban's are cut from a single piece of acetate, so there should be no seam on the frames (presence of seam suggests injection molding was used for creation). Everything else regarding the glasses seemed legitimate; eg, the case, cleaning cloth, and other features.

I submitted for a replacement, will see what I get in the next couple days.

I'll preface this rating by saying that I've been purchasing Cole Haan shoes for many years.  Nike sold the company to a private equity group and since the sale I've noticed a significant decrease in quality. I've had several of the Cole Haan drivers and this new pair received is disappointing. The shoes are made in China and the quality and suppleness of the leather is very poor.  While they are very attractive, it appears that the new owners are more interested in cost savings than continuing to produce a quality shoe. This new pair lacks substance and no longer feature the Nike Air insole, one of Cole Haan's greatest attributes. I'm reluctantly going to hang on to them and see how long they last. I'm mot optimistic. Should this trend continue, I'll be venturing out to other brands like Johnston & Murphy, Bally, Ferragamo, etc. If you're looking for a driver moc, take a pass on this style and try something else.  If you're a discerning Cole Haan shoe wearer, you'd be disappointed. This shoe is a miss in my book and I'm hopeful that the company will focus on quality as they move forward.  Otherwise they will lose loyal customers.

To make these usable,
1. Put on 72 inch laces so you can let the seam in or out as needed without unlacing the boot each time you take it on or off.
2. Put in some jell soles in them and on top of the jell soles a standard insert or arch support.
3. Cover the leather in oil or saddle soap so that the leather becomes flexible.
4. BREAK THEM IN by wearing them awhile each day until they conform to your feet.
Overall they cut some corners in building these, but for the price they work ok.

The DESERTWOLF VINTAGE CANVAS TOTE BAG is marketed as being a laptop tote bag that is suitable for both men and women. That marketing is a bit misleading. The bag is extremely well made and it has a lot more room than one would imagine upon first glance. It has been constructed for durability. There are three zippered pockets (two on the outside and one on the inside). In addition, there are a few other open pockets on the inside. There is a zipper on top to secure the articles inside. However, this top zipper leaves a small opening on both sides, so if you have any small articles, they can fall out of the bag.

The biggest issues I have with the bag are that it will NOT hold a laptop computer and it is definitely a bag designed for women, not men. The bag will hold a tablet, but it will not hold a laptop computer, so don't be fooled by the title or advertising. In addition, the DESERTWOLF VINTAGE CANVAS TOTE BAG is a very feminine looking bag. For instance, there is a faux leather belt in the front with some Chinese writing on it and there is a label in the very center of the front of the bag. These are both designs that are typical of female purses and totes. In short, it's something I would think about getting for my girlfriend, but not something I would ever purchase myself.

Overall, the DESERTWOLF VINTAGE CANVAS TOTE BAG is a tote bag that has been designed for durability and longevity. However, it will not fully carry a normal laptop computer and has been designed with some feminine features making it not something that most men would probably use.

I love both pairs of the Dansko shoes that I own which is why I’m disappointed in my purchase of the "Jessie” sandal. I went with this sandal since the heel and platform height measurements are the same as Dansko's “Sophie" but with a different style to the leather uppers.

However, I did not pay close attention to the material of the footbed. The “Sophie” description states it’s a DRI-LEX wrapped footbed where as the “Jessie” has a leather-lined footbed. So what's the issue - DRI-LEX absorbs any foot perspiration while the leather causes an annoying “sucking” sound during every step taken. This “audio issue” may not bother everyone but if you currently own a pair of Dansko “Sophie” sandals you’ll quickly notice the difference. More than likely I’m going to return these shoes.

On a side note, I do like the feel of a leather-wrapped footbed but for shoes that have some type of back heel support, i.e. an adjustable slingback strap. That would suppress the heel from popping off the shoe, subsequently preventing that “sucking” sound.

I purchased this boot in Slate in my usual size 8. I knew that they would be a little too narrow since I have one foot that is a little wider than the other. The rest of the fit is great, and I can see these being extremely comfortable once broken in.
The color is beautiful: a cool-toned mottled taupe-gray, the leather is supple, and I have no doubt that these are the genuine article. That being said, I don't think they're the pick of the litter, either. The right boot has a sloppy overcut edge on the inside of the sole; it's barely noticeable if you're looking at the boot from farther away than eye-level. Also, the front sole of my pair is most definitely hard leather, not rubber like the description says and like the pictures SEEM to show. The back of the heel is indeed rubber, and it slips and slides all over the place! While test-driving these around the house I nearly went down twice on the hardwood floor. These are definitely going to the cobbler for some grip-ums, and for a protective coating/sole so I don't ruin the bottoms during the impending New England Winter.

I normally fit a 10.5, so I went with the size 11 G4 (it's annoying that there aren't half sizes, btw), and the fit does not feel secure enough for barefoot wear (you mean I need a sock inside my barely-more-than-a-sock 'shoe' thingy?), as they fit slightly loose, letting the foot slide around inside. Ruling out any possibility of a better fit with the next size down: the rubber sole cups around the foot and tends to press in on my little toe, which is very irritating, if not a tragic design flaw considering that a proper barefoot-like feel requires allowance for toe splay.

As for materials? The smothering neoprene/TPU construction makes the feet grow sweaty quickly (which only worsens the issue of slipping). And then there's the fact that the sole is held to the upper with glue... and upon receiving them I immediately noticed it was either peeling away already or had simply not been properly glued on in a couple spots. Either way, it reflects poorly on craftsmanship.

On top of all that, the specific shape of the sole, and how it connects to the upper, causes a hideous buckling to occur right around the center of the interior side of the foot. And it's not just on my foot; I see this in every photo. This causes what might otherwise appear to be a simple sock to take on the appearance of a sock worn through mud, taken off and allowed to dry, then put back on once the mud had dried and deformed.

Despite the issues, I briefly considered keeping them for winter house slippers. But they're simply nowhere near being worth the money, so I returned them for a refund.

For now I will be sticking with Vibram FiveFingers for all athletic needs despite the small issue of having to individually align the toes when putting them on. I may try the Soft Star Moc3 next.

I was so looking forward to getting these sandals because my friend has a different model of Merrell sandals she bought in Europe and wears them all the time while walking all day, going everywhere and they are amazing. I wasn't able to find the model she has here in the US so I decided to give these ones a try.

I have to say I have pretty mixed feelings about these sandals and Merrel brand in general. First of all, based on all the reviews I've read and also my first experience with a different model I ordered from DSW (and returned), I went with a smaller size than mine. I'm a true 6.5 when it comes to most shoes, except for winter boots. Those I prefer in 7-7.5 so I can chose what thickness socks to wear. But for most sandals and flip flops and pretty much anything "open toe", anything in 6-6.5 works well. Typically. Well, not Merrell's apparently. The DSW pair I got in 7 was huge and left tons of space in front of my toes and didn't look as cute in reality so I returned it to the store. Found these ones and ordered them in size 6 to avoid the same situation I had with the other pair. Wrong again. The sole wasn't small. It was ok. No toes hanging over because my foot wouldn't even fit that far into the sandal lol

The very first strap (non adjustable and closest to your ankle that goes over the "instep") would not allow for my foot to go much further. Fine! I sent them back and exchanged for yet again, size 7. Size 7 of this style fits a bit better and the sole isn't too long like the other ones. Little room in front of my toes but nothing crazy. Straps are slightly wider but I'm still uncomfortable with the tightness of that instep strap :-( And the other strap you can adjust on these in the front doesn't really do anything. It's pretty much there for looks lol The front strap is surprisingly comfy for me but only because I have wide "duck" feet with all toes of the same length. so for anyone who has normal more pointy feet, it'll most likely be too wide :-(
I'm hoping that it'll stretch with time because it's leather and the sole is comfy. I can't say it gives amazing arch support. It seems to me that in order for that to happen, it would need to be more firm instead of soft but they do feel nice to walk in. I have yet to test them on a really long walk (5 miles +), but I'm keeping them simply because I need a pair of comfy walking sandals and I"m tired of exchanging them. Not sure I will buy Merrell's sandals again though. The whole "no half sizes" thing is pretty disappointing. All of the adjustment features they offer do not make up for weird sole sizes for all of us half size people and sometimes, the straps that need to be adjustable the most are not. Besides, they aren't exactly $39.99. I guess I expected more for the price :-( Time will tell if at least the quality makes up for fitment difficulties :-)

Sorry for the low rating, but with almost 2000 reviews, it was unlikely that folks would read anything but the 1 star and the 5 star reviews.

I actually like the shoe a lot (a bought 2 pairs, one for myself, and one for my son). The key problem is that the insert comes loose and jams in the toe area during an obstacle race (i.e. Spartan). This happened to both my son and I, and occurred after the water obstacles. This "defect" was pointed out in numerous 4 star reviews. Which is what I would have rated this shoe: 4 Stars! But if you are like me, you don't tend to read the 4 Star reviews. Hence I'm hoping that I'm providing a public service to folks that will buy this shoe in the future, and that can possible fix the shoe prior to their big race. Several of my 4 Star colleagues recommended using Shoe Goo or some other type of glue. I will try to experiment, and will update my review in the future. But whatever the glue ... make sure its water proof. Final comment: the insoles only came out, came loose when wet. I had run in the shoes for several days on the street with no problem.

Recap of the Pro's and Con's

Con's
- The insert comes loose (both shoes), and jams in the toe area
- and unfortunately, without the insert, the shoe was a bit too loose for me
- perhaps a bit too long for me. Felt my foot moving forward when heading down a steep slope

Pro's

I have been wearing this style for years, but the quality has really gone downhill in the last few years. 2 pairs ago, they lasted until the soles wore down after several years - perfect. 1 pair ago, the soles fell apart within a few months - the top and bottom of the sole seem to be stiffer material, but there's empty space in between, with just a narrow band of material around the edges to fool you into thinking they're the same as the old type. The most recent pair had problems from day 1 - the hooks at the top swivel around, so the shoes come untied. I ended up needing to re-tie them repeatedly during the day. Perhaps due to this, after a few months the lace sleeve (the 3rd row from the top) popped out of the leather on one of the shoes. The right shoe also becomes very uncomfortable after a few hours and starts digging into my heel enough to cause blisters. None of this used to be a problem with this style.

Perhaps this is another example of "quality fade" and Timberland simply doesn't care (they certainly didn't seem to be motivated to do anything about the pair where the soles fell off when I called them). I have a pair of Tourmaster Solution 1.0 boots that have traveled the world with me without a problem. After many tens of thousands of miles, it was time to retire them. I replaced them with Tourmaster Solution 2.0 boots and boy, what a mistake.

First the boots arrived and looked to be okay but made of much cheaper materials and with much less support than the originals. They are just not the as well made as the originals in materials or in quality. After trying them on, the left boot felt fine but the right boot felt an entire size too large. I bought some aftermarket foot beds and heel support and they then felt minimally okay but still not what they should. The heel cup is not formed well, the foot form is wide and they are just flimsy in terms of construction. Overall, they are just not made of quality materials and so the more they're worn the looser and less supportive they become.

I wore them around my office and my home for bit to break them in and last week finally had a chance to use them on some longer 500 mile rides. After the first ride, I looked at the soles and the rubber had actually torn in the middle of the boot. Incredibly, the rubber on the sole seems to be just a covering of some type and the foot pegs actually tore through the rubber making holes in the center of the sole after just the FIRST ride of about 500 miles. The sole also began losing chunks of rubber on the ball of the foot.

I have posted pictures below. One picture is of the sole of the left boot of the original Tourmaster Solution 1.0 after about 100,000 miles and 5 years of wear on several different bikes but with at least 30,000 miles on my BMW R1200GS Adventure.The second is the Tourmaster Solution 2.0 after one 500 mile ride on my BMW R1200GS Adventure.

These boots are not like the originals and should be considered to be even minimally adequate for any type of serious motorcycling.

All outdoor terrain was a breeze- slick rock, groundcover/dirt, sand, rocks, you name it. The only surface that I found slippery with the Garmonts was those smooth tile floors.

UPDATE2 after a year of use:  I am not an intense skateboarder. I use them as loafers, and they are not the only shoes I wear. After a year, the shoes are showing some wear and tearing beside the little toe, on both shoes.  But they're still going.  The back part tore at the top when I didn't untie my laces properly to remove or put them on.  Most shoes are forgiving of this, not these.  So they are having a beginning stage of falling apart that is taking a long time, and I still like to wear them because of their light weight.  I don't want to replace them, because I'm stubborn and want to get my money's worth, determined to wear them out till they fall apart before I might buy another pair - only in leather next time.   UPDATE1:  I am reducing my rating by one star. shortly after I bought them, the loop at the back, that you grasp to help put them on, came off. Testament to fragile construction. Not happy about that.  Before buying these, I went to a local skate shop in my city to try several brands on. (The clerk at Emp!re was so lazy at first, just chatting with other staff, and then so impolite, that I have absolutely no regrets buying here instead of paying him full retail price).  What I learned, is that Vans are the narrowest, but all brands are extremely narrow and uncomfortable, and while you have to generally go a half size larger, with DC you have to go a full size larger.  To help you better chose the right size, let me give you some background on myself: I wear a size 10 on average. I do have one pair of shoes, for playing soccer, that is 9.5, so I have it snug, as no extra space in front of the toes is desirable. But generally, I buy 10.5 to get a little bit of extra width. I tried these on in the store, and 10.5 fit well, felt light, and it was like you were walking on air. Those were the ones with the large mesh upper.  The ones I ordered are a finer mesh, and are not as comfortable as the ones in the store.  My little toes stick out to the side slightly, as the shoe stretches easily to accomodate your foot's width. In retrospect, I wonder if I shouldn't have ordered a 10, instead of a 10.5, in the case of this model, but I'm thinking that maybe my little toe would be sticking out too far from the side, causing premature wear at that point.  I am generally not impressed with skate shoes. But my well-padded running shoes just don't cut it for skateboarding, and a fall wearing my five-fingers left too much of a gauge on my foot to want to go without skate shoes again.  When I was little, skate shoes, like Converse for example, sold at KMart for $5 a pair. It was what poor parents bought their kids when they couldn't afford better shoes, and us kids hated the experience.  By some stroke of marketing genius, these companies have turned the budget product into a high-priced fasion product with a cult following.  My advice is this (it's what I did), your preferred color might not the the cheapest one there, but your second or third-favorite might be a bargain.  These shoes were about 40 in the size-color combination that I settled on, which is far more reasonable than the 120 they asked in the store for this model. Some of them are under $30, close to 20... but in my size, they were just too ugly. Given they are more comfortable than all other skate shoe models, I think paying about 40 is an OK deal.  But don't go spending 120 on these just because your kid asks for it - none of these skate shoe models are worth that. These are $20 shoes that you accept to pay a little bit extra for on account that they are more comfortable.

This bag has plenty of internal pockets so my bag is decently organized. There are two outer slip pockets on the side that are probably intended for baby bottles, but fits a water bottle easily. No one I work with can believe that this bag is supposed to be used for a diaper bag - it comes off as a professional bag when used in the right setting i.e. I'm not carrying a baby with me so no one thinks my giant purse is really intended to be a diaper bag.

- Good stability vs weight (very stable/not heavy)

The bad:
- Insoles are bad and need to be replaced
- Straps are way too short, which makes it impossible to wear additional ankle support or even an extra pair of socks
