The one star is for the (lack of) service. I left a message on the customer service message on the day after receiving my shoes. A few weeks go by, no return phone call. Fair enough - perhaps my phone number wasn't heard (despite always repeating it slowly twice). So, 1.5 weeks ago I call the customer service line and leave another message. I wait a week. No call back. I called back again yesterday and spoke with Janice. I felt like she didn't believe that I had left messages and found her service very unhelpful. She stated at the end of the conversation she would send me an email with some links. 1.5 days later, nothing received. No issues resolved.

As for the shoes. I would rate them a 3. Mind you, I've been in minimalist shoes for over 7 years now. I've ordered 3 times from SoftStarShoes.com (which is made in USA and has excellent customer service) and have had 2 Fivefinger shoes. They all have their pluses and minuses, but overall it's the only shoes I wear - for both running, hiking and walking.

The Ventures: the heel cup doesn't prevent much from getting in. Any off road use in these and I'm always stopping to get something out of my shoe. Additionally, I'm constantly tightening the heels which come lose throughout the day. I can't imagine how people can run in these things.

I also ordered my daughter the kit, and she can't wear the shoes without them flopping forward. My partner ordered the Ventures and have only worn them twice due to the pain it causes between his toes. Despite being a previous avid flip flop wearer, I also experience pain from the hard plastic that goes between the toes.

Had I receivedbetter customer service, I would be willing to try their newest model. However, I definitely won't be coming back due to how my situation was handled.

-True to the image you see. There are no extra embellishments or quirks.

CONS:
-Didn't fit my particular face shape.

-Wouldn't recommend for casual non-prescriptive use since the glasses get a terrible glare on them.

I bought these shoes before going to work on a site that I knew was going to very rocky and muddy (no paved roads). I looked around both at some cheap options (cheap in money and quality), and I looked at the high-end brands, but I'll tell you - the price and reviews on these convinced me to give these a shot, and I'm glad I did.

First of all, the sizing, which I am thankful others spoke to: I normally buy Men's Size 12 for my shoes. Realistically, I am probably between an 11.5 - 12 (but 12's are way easier to find in shoe stores than 11.5, so I deal with it). For these, because others said they ran big, I went with an 11. The first couple times I put them on, I could feel the end of the shoes with my toes and was concerned they were going to be too small. But by the 3rd or 4th time I wore them around the house, I can tell you that they broke in wonderfully and fit me perfectly. I wore them with "normal" thickness socks - certainly not thick hiking socks - so that would make a difference. But for me, the 11 has proven to be the perfect size. (On a shopping note, it helps that at the time I was shopping, the 11's were significantly cheaper than the 11.5's or 12's).

I wore these shoes for 3 weeks straight over a ton of different kind of terrain, including a hike up and down a mountain, but you wouldn't know it by how these shoes held up. The sole is very rugged and grips well, and there are no signs of the soles breaking or pulling away. Honestly, I had purchased a "cheap" pair of hiking shoes before I found these, but when I bought these (for only a few dollars more!) and held them side by side, these were night and day different.

I can't recommend these enough. Yes, get a half size to a full size smaller than you're used to (or just wear really thick socks). But they look great, feel great, support your foot well, and won't break the bank. Despite this being a brand I had never seen before shopping on Amazon, they now have a convert, and I wouldn't look anywhere else.

Ok, so if I was going to complain about something, the only "con" I would say is that small rocks/pebbles get caught in the thick treads and can scratch a floor if you wear them inside. I don't consider this a problem, as they are outdoor shoes, but just be aware of that when coming back inside. Just check the soles to make sure you aren't dragging any rocks. Such a minor, considering what they're designed for, I wouldn't even consider it worth docking a star.

Ok, I have a lot to say about these boots and how they tore apart my feet. 1st off I’ve never had issues with Vivienne Westwood/Melissa shoes in the past. I’m thinking that Amazon might get “irregulars” of Vivienne Westwood products (I also ordered a Westwood necklace & it was broken) because after inspecting this shoe closer I realized it’s unfinished! I seriously think these are unfinished boots! Vivienne/Melissa shoes are usually of superb quality and I hate to write a negative review about their shoes but these have to be unfinished! My Vivienne/Melissa “protection cowboy” boots are NOTHING like these! They are lined on the inside, top and bottom of the shoe & feel like you’re walking on clouds, so comfy!

So I got these in April & had tried them on & walked around the house & they felt ok. I felt it was odd that the soles of the shoes popped out on one when I took one boot off but figured I got them cheap so I’d deal with it. Little did I know how uncomfortable they’d be to wear in the future! On July 3rd I attended an outdoors art exhibit and much to my dismay these boots MANGLED my feet, esp my left one. I apologize in advance for the photos of my ugly, torn up foot but I want Amazon to see what these boots did to my feet! Esp my left foot. I actually had to leave the art exhibit after spending under 2 hours walking around because my feet were in so much pain! I swear that these boots are unfinished or irregular & that’s why they’re for sale so cheap! When I got home and took off the boots and then took off my socks my skin came off my left pinky toe! Under my big toe there was a mark on my foot, a cut, and my foot was bruised and discolored there. The other foot has bruises and cuts in the same parts as the other foot but not as extreme. I was expecting to change shoes and return to the art exhibit but was unable to because my left pinky toe is pulsating, missed a 4th of July part and plan to see my primary doctor tomorrow, yes it hurts that much! It almost feels like a burn since the skin came off.

I advise people not to buy these boots on Amazon. I’ve purchased my other Vivienne/Melissa boots from 6pm, yoox, Melissa’s direct page & Westwood’s too. I’ve never had an issue like this! Also these did not come with a dust bag as all my others have. There’s definitely something wrong with these shoes. I’d also like to point out that after wearing them for under 2 hours that the sole is coming off the right shoe. I also took a photo of that & a photo of the inside of the shoe. It appears the shoe parts are glued together but there’s some weird, hay looking threads coming out from the sole, where it connects to the boot, and also inside the boot too.

I notice there is one other negative review and a couple positive ones. I’m thinking that maybe some of the shoes Amazon sent out were defective and some were fine? I’m sure it’s not Amazon’s fault, unless they knew they were irregulars. I’m sure they didn't check each shoe individually but it appears I am not the only person to have had an issue with these shoes. I’m wondering if the other reviews were written after the people had tried them on & prior to walking in them for over an hour lol. Or possibly I just got a bum pair of unfinished boots. So if you do purchase these from Amazon I suggest you wear them around your house for longer than an
hour to see how they feel! And check inside of them, check to make sure there is a lining and that the soles liners are not coming out of the boots. So disappointed with these, esp since this happened 3 months after purchasing them. You’d think when you buy a quality product that you wouldn't have to worry about not wearing the item until a couple months later and find out it’s faulty and be sh*t out of luck! Buyer beware!

Be aware there are two different shoes here that fit differently. The ones with the white plastic buckle tend to run true to size or even a little big. I wear an 8 or 8 1/2 depending on the shoe and I wore an 8 in the plastic buckle shoes. The plastic buckle shoes also have a different sole. (see pictures below)  I like these the best even though the buckle on one broke immediately. It was an easy fix. The metal piece in the buckle came off. I snapped it back on and used needle nose pliers to crimp it so it does not come off again. Then I did this to all of the ones with a plastic buckles even before I wore them just to make sure it does not happen again. After wearing these a couple times, I no longer need to unbuckle them. I can just slip them on and go. These are by far my favorite.  Any spot that rubs my foot at all, I put a spot on. I do this with all my shoes and never have issues. Spots work miracles! The ones with the metal buckle fit differently. They seem to run a little small and for some reason were very uncomfortable for me in the toe area even in an 8 //2. I returned them after buying several pair and nothing felt good on my foot. I think the metal buckle ones are better quality. Look at the toe area between the two types. The metal buckles have smaller and less toe room. They are also a more flat platform.   In summary, the plastic buckle runs slightly big and has a different angle that looks fantastic and makes your legs look like you are wearing heels even though they are completely comfy. The metal buckle runs small, has a different sole and is more of a flat platform.  ALSO NOTE YOU PAY FOR RETURN SHIPPING IF THEY DON"T FIT IF YOU BUY FROM SHOE CENTER - So basically there is no return because it cost more to ship it back than the shoe is worth.   Here are the spots which you can buy just about anywhere. Also available in non-gel. http://smile.amazon.com/Foot-Support-Soft-Pads-VIVEsole/dp/B00SXSEM00/ref=sr_1_cc_1?s=aps&ie=UTF8&qid=1439485604&sr=1-1-catcorr&keywords=spot+cushions+for+shoes  I hope this review saves someone from all the returns I have done. No wonder the reviews are so conflicting.

The style, color and shape of these sunglasses is near identical to a discontinued model sold under Emporio Armani (model# EA2017Z) which, at this time can still be found on Amazon and elsewhere. Better prices await those who are willing to take the time to search the less popular avenues of the internet.
Having tried both, I can say confidently that the Armani quality is significantly higher. The Flowertree manufactured product seems to be made of a thinner metal. The Armani, feels more robust and has the side shields coated with color matching rubber. This will most likely add to the longevity of the product by protecting the metal from the wearer's perspiration. Additionally, the Armani side shields are held in place, and pivot on, tension pins that lock into the frame. This allows the side shields to rotate and be removed with relative ease. The Flowertree sides shields are positioned with screws which are destined to work themselves out over time with each opening and closing of the frame arms. Lastly, the Armani's are shipped in a semi-rigid protective case. The Armani distributer I purchased from also shipped them in a firm cardboard box so I recieved the item in perfect condition. Sadly though, a crush resistant case was not provided with my Flowertree sunglasses and my seller (Mulberry Trading Co. Ltd.) used only a simple bubble envelope. When I received them, the frames were bent beyond repair.
Conclusion: Buy if you have to have this style and are willing to trade quality for a bargain price AND (more importantly) if you can find a seller that will ship then in packaging that provides adequate protection; otherwise look elsewhere.

I wanted a pair of black pointed toe flats so I bought the Zariner and the Itzamor loafers to compare.

Sizing:
I'm a size 6 and both shoes felt true to size.

Comfort:
I have wide feet and both the Zariner and Itzamor felt a bit too narrow for me. These would be fine with people with narrow feet but people with "normal" or wide feet would find them too tight in the toe area. I do not think I would have been able to walk very far with these shoes on. I felt a pinch between my pinky toe and my 4th toe whenever I walked in either shoe. The bottom of both shoes are also a little slippery. If either loafers were comfortable for me, I would have taken them to a shoe cobbler to add a non-slip sole so I wouldn't slip and bust my @ss.

Style:
I like the style of the Zariner. It's got a plain toe but has a thin gold trim on the heel for some subtle flashiness. The leather was a little softer than the Itzamor.
The Itzamor has a fabric tweed-like upper which I did not love because it would get soaked if worn in the rain. I liked the patent leather but it felt a bit stiff.

Overall, these shoes look cute but did not feel comfortable enough to walk in. They were returned.

I needed head lights similar to The Friendly Swede, but they don't sell them unless in a pair and I didn't need rear red lights, just the white. I found this product very similar to their lights and decided to give it a try and it wasn't entirely what I was expecting. This is a very bare bones version. Lights of this type should have an internal structure, a plastic casing, followed by a rubber casing to cover the entire thing. This light only has the internal structure, no plastic casing, and a rubber casing; there's exposed wiring just uncovering the lights! If you stick your finger in the wrong direction or forcibly move the casing too hard, you risk damaging the whole light; don't drop it as it can't handle hard physical abuse! The light itself works though, it's bright as their competitor, though making it red on the sides was an odd choice of design. Overall though, the lights works and it's been doing well for me. However, I had to be extra careful whenever I have to replace the batteries, avoid dropping it, and avoid water exposure as it's not waterproof at all. A few well placed drips of water could destroy the exposed circuitry! Keep the lights dry! For lights under $4 though, you get what you paid for.

I ordered ASICS GT 1000 2 Running shoes (2 pair).  I received ASICS GT 1000 3 running shoe.  I've owned many pairs of ASICS GT 1000 2 running shoes.  The reason I ordered ASICS GT 1000 2 running shoes is because the shoes have "SPEVA" in the shoe as cushioning, as specifically identified in the product description. I gave this shoulder bag 4 stars because there is one glaring aspect that sets it back. But first, let's focus on the good things:

* Aesthetics: Looks great, really nice color scheme - the earth tones work great, with nice shades of brown that are easy on the eyes. There are handles, and an adjustable shoulder strap(which you can take off), so you have options to carry it in multiple ways.
* Material: Very nice high quality canvas/jean material - very thick and sturdy, it seems like it can take a beating and carries on and last you a long time. The flap that covers the top is a fake leather material, but it looks very nice and feels very soft.
* Crafstmanship: The stitching and seams look fine, I haven't noticed any issues. The metal studs are securely in place.
* Dimensions: The bag is approximately 16 inches long by 13 inches tall, and about 2 inches thick resting naturally without anything inside.
* Capacity:
- There are two outside pockets that span the length of the bag. The one on the front side is about 7.5 inches tall, while the back one is about 8 inches tall.
- There are smaller inside pockets on the inner lining for small items. One is zippered.
- There is a separated compartment for your tablet or small laptop(most likely up to 13-14-inch screens)

Now, to that one glaring issue. Manufacturers of lower quality bags always mess this up - and that is ignoring the quality of the zippers. Any good manufacturer knows that the zippers are one of the most important features - they can make or break the whole bag. So while this bag has mostly excellent features, their cheap zippers make them lose a star.
Low quality means: 1) they are of cheap quality and might break easily(both the tabs and the teeth) 2) they do not allow you to zip or unzip smoothly and easily, and get stuck - or even worse, misalign the teeth or even break them.

Overall, this is a good shoulder bag that is held back by its low-quality zippers. I always rate the product with the price in mind, because nowadays that is a key factor in deciding what you buy and whether you buy that particular product, or the competition. Taking into consideration its quality and functionality, I feel this is a good product at up to $50, because the material of the bag is excellent. But it can never be a 5-star product if they don't upgrade the zippers. Give this a try if you think you can work with the zipper issue.

I'm a Plant Engineer for a forging company in Texas. I've purchased Timberland Pro boots back in the '90's, but for the last 10+ years I've been going with Wolverines (specifically the McKay boot). After trying on these Timberland Helix boots at the local store, I decided to order from Amazon because of the better price. I tried the boots on last night: they fit well (I bought a 10-1/2D), feel excellent, look good (for now :) and are light.

This morning as I'm walking into the plant, I can feel something sharp stabbing the inside of my right heel. I get in my office, take the boot off thinking there is something that I dropped in there, but there's nothing. At closer inspection, there is a sharp object protruding from the footbed at the inside right heel. When I press on it with my finger, it has a spring to it, but it's fairly rigid and my heel does not apply enough pressure to deflect it.

Unfortunately, this appears to be a manufacturing defect. I'm very, very disappointed in this. I've ordered several of the Wolverine McKays from Amazon and never had any issue whatsoever. I've called my wife to bring me my old (year and half) boots so I can package these up and send them back. I'm not planning on trying another pair (the fact that you have to return it, wait on another - just irks me to no end).

In manufacturing, sometimes there are defects in your products - no different with us. We deal with internal rework and scrap all the time, but what we try to mitigate most is external rework, and worse yet, external scrap. These shoes are scrap and I'm not wasting additional time, money and effort by ordering another pair, hoping that the quality control is right.

*Sigh*. I really wanted to love the Boracay's as much as I love their counterpart, the Fresh Foam Zante, which is in my standard rotation of running shoes. When I wear tested the Boracay's for a 1/4 mile run at the shoe store, I loved the cushioning and roomy toe box and bought them on the spot. But after wearing these for 50 miles worth of runs over the past 8 weeks (ranging from 3 to 10 miles,) I'm tossing them in the trash. Why? Because they have *SO* much cushioning that I have no ground feel underfoot and end up pounding harder than usual, which leads to persistent pain in my left knee after 15 minutes of running. That's not something I could have discovered from a very short test run at the shoe store. Ever the optimist, I held out hope that the persistent knee pain was a fluke. But run after run, I felt the knee pain every single time--in these shoes only. Not at all what I had hoped for. I realize every runner has their preferences, so these may be the perfect shoe for some--but I can't give anything but negative feedback and do not recommend them.

Like Nike has been doing lately, these running shoes follow to trend of incredibly lightweight runners, thriving on a primary emphasis of mesh and thin synthetics. They are extremely cushy and quite comfortable to wear, not only run in. I also must give them props for appearance; they look solid. I think the Royal Blue color scheme looks by far the best; some schemes do not look too great in comparison. The flimsier design does make them bulge and look a bit fat our your foot, but that is only noticeably by the wearer, as I can't tell when looking at them in a mirror, from the perspective of another person. They look great then. The sole is also a bit fat in terms of thickness; I wish they weren't so prominent because I prefer the lower profile sole of the Nike Free line, but it again is something mostly noticed by the wearer. They also get a bit dirty easily, and it seems that durability will be a concern if you are an avid runner. I play sports on campus and my pair has the bottoms of the soles wearing down a bit quickly. I can see that these are great walking shoes, or running on hardwood or tar, but not concrete. All in all, regardless of these quibbles, these are a very solid running shoe choice both for casual or gym wear.

These are the worst running shoes I've ever used and actually caused damage to my right leg... first, the ankle bones became bruised, then shin splints.  I went back to my old (completely worn-down) shoes and the pain went away.  Tried these Adidas shoes again and got terrible sciatica pain.  Stayed off the shoes for several days and the sciatica pain lessed a lot (still not gone, tho).  Tested the Adidas again with a brief walk and the sciatica was back in full force.  I've been running for decades and have worn many different kinds of shoes, and none of them caused injury besides these.  These are the structural problems with the shoe, I think:  The footbed is flat, vs. slightly elevated in the heel, as just about every other running shoe would be.  Therefore, every step forces ligaments, fascia, and muscles to overstretch.  And it causes great fatigue as well... every step feels like you're going uphill, even when on flat or downhill terrain.  There is also zero arch support, and the footbed can't be removed to insert your own.  Seems that the shoe causes the foot to roll outward in a dangerous way.

I just received these shoes, but I can easily provide some feedback regarding my observations. I purchased these shoes as a nice summer shoe that could crossover between casual and casual dress. As a pre-qualifier, I ordered these shoes in tan/sand, I did not order these shoes from Amazon, I ordered these shoes in 11 1/2 and I got these shoes at a reduced rate.
1. As mentioned, I ordered these shoes in the tan/sand color. The color was as expected. I have not had the opportunity, but I plan to wear these shoes with jeans (already done) and dress them up a little with khakis.
2. I ordered the shoes 1/2 size larger based on reviews I had read. The shoe is very narrow and the upsizing was a wise (and necessary) decision.
3, The shoe comes with 2 sets of laces. 1 set of leather laces (or faux leather) and another set of stiff fabric laces. I am not a fan of either laces and I might look to replace them.
4. The shoe itself is very stiff. I expected a more supple fabric, but the fabric is hard and requires a break-in period for the shoes. The heel is creating some hotspots (areas of rubbing that could produce blisters). I hope to be able to break them in for wear without socks, but (out of the box) that is not an option.
5. The sole is what I would call minimalist. The sole is thin and definitely allows for a decent amount of ground feel. The interior of the shoe includes an insole that covers from the heel through the midfoot. The insole (non-removable) provides a little added cushioning in the heel. The sole does have a heel to toe offset (higher heel than toe), but I am uncertain what the off-set is. I would definitely not call the shoes comfortable. It's more about getting used to them than it is about comfort.
6. I wore the shoes to work the first day and have already received a compliment.
7. I cannot speak the durability of the shoes as I have not had them long enough.

All-in-all, I like the shoes. They are basically what I expected. I am hopeful that (after some break-in) that these shoes will become a more enjoyable shoe in my summer shoe rotation.hat I expected. My favorite Maui's to date. These are so light and comfortable, it's easy to forget their on your face. Even the lenses aren't constantly reminding your eyes that you're peering through a darkened piece synthetic material. They are plenty dark for the brightest of days, but transition quite nicely into cloud cover or more dimly lit environments. Seriously; it can be very easy to forget these are on your face, so please, don't forget and become that "indoors sunglasses-wearing guy" (nobody likes that guy). The lenses also give everything a nice sharp, clear, contrast.

I have a hard time finding sunglasses that aren't cartoonishly wide for my face/temples, but the Sugar Beaches have a perfect fit. I wouldn't call them narrow, but they do fit my "narrowish" temples exactly as I would hope from any pair of glasses. While these are styled like a pair of Aviators--and have very similar look when worn--they feel much more secure, "sporty", and block out more light from the edges in comparison. I feel like these wrap the face and cover the eyes better than most traditional Aviator-styled sunnies. I bought these after owning a pair of MJ Lighthouses for the past few years (same "sport" model glasses with different shaped lenses). The problem I had with the Lighthouse model was that too much light came in from the side and reflected back to my eye. This was especially problematic if the sun was more to my back; this would cause my eyes to sting and burn after a while. I do not have this problem at all with the Sugar Beach glasses.

I regularly wear these golfing and they do not budge when looking down at my ball or throughout my swing (unlike my traditional Aviator-styled glasses). And again, if the sun is to my back, I don't get a distracting reflection like I did with my Lighthouses or Aviators.

And if you're not familiar with Maui Jim's service, it is top notch if you have to send anything in for repair. I had a different "sport" model that broke at the bridge and right temple piece, and the lenses were LIGHTLY scratched. They were 3 years old at the time and out of warranty. Maui Jim gave me a "complementary" replacement set of lenses, replaced the temple for free, and only charged for the bridge and the service fee. As noted in my original review below, the soles immediately came off and I was so disappointed! I cleaned them very well (sand and old glue residue). I let them dry completely. I used Shoe Goo, Clear (available on Amazon for $6) and followed directions to reattach my insoles. I let them sit for months (it was the end of Fall). This last week, I dug them out and decided to give them a try. It was a week of my out-of-town relatives visiting, so the got used every day for hours on end, in fresh and salt water, thru deep sand,over rocks, and across parking lots. I abused them. They held up thru it all and I'm now in love with these shoes!! The only problem I had was on one shoe the little material that covers the sole has peeled a little by my toes, but that's no biggie at all...I'll probably just end up tearing it off.

Why the manufacturer does not use water proof glue, I have no ideal. It seems like it would be a no-brainer to me...otherwise these would be 5 star shoes!!! smdh As it is, they will not earn any extra stars-2 is the best they will get from me. $12 for the shoes, $6 for the glue. I would have gladly paid $18 for these if they would have used the right glue in the beginning!

Anyway, I'm sure you can find better shoes, but I am now in love with mine!

They look great!

They fit great! (I ordered size 9 B-I have wide width feet and vary between 8 1/2 wide and 9 wide depending on the shoe and these fit perfect.They are a little loose, but the little pull tab in the bag snugs them up perfectly.)

They stayed on my feet perfectly when swimming in the ocean.

CONS-

I got in the water and had to get right back out for something (3 minutes tops I was in the water). Immediately the insoles glue dissolved and the insole began bunching up. All day long I dealt with them bunching up and having to put them back in place. UGH.

These five star shoes went to two stars because of this HUGE FLAW.

The manufacture is completely aware these will be in the water, so why would they not use water proof glue?!! Or better yet, just make the soles rubber thicker/more comfortable in order to eliminate the need for the soles at all??

As a 30 year old who prefers fashion shoes to sports sneakers, this was a tough sell. I've been in a 2 year battle with plantar fasciitis in my left foot due to that aforementioned love for fashion, and these were sort of my "I give up" shoes after spending big bucks on a pair of Birkenstocks and a couple other pairs of shoes I had to return to the department store.

Appropriateness for Plantar Fasciitis
While I haven't had my foot doctor inspect these yet, by most of the PF shoe standards I've read about, these shoes do seem to fit the requirements for a good plantar fasciitis shoe. It has an inflexible sole, decent heel cushion and arch support and a minimally bendy, wider (though not round) toe. I would recommend taking them to your doctor and having her look them over before you wear them outside, just to be sure.

Style
Let's be honest, while much better than they used to be, these still kinda look like orthopedic shoes. Yes, they added dayglo green and silver to the hospital matte gray in a feeble attempt to appeal to a younger audience, but the solid orthopedic leather kind of defeats any attempt at stylishness. I switched the gray shoelaces out for aqua, which helps a little, but I always feel a bit dopey wearing these in public (but that's probably just me).

Comfort
I wear these mainly for the 2-4 mile walks I like to take around my paved neighborhood. Because I am wearing my own inserts, I can't give an unbiased review of how the shoes feel without them, but I can say that they do fit half inch inserts well with plenty of room left over. I've removed the factory inserts and put in a $75 pair my doctor gave me as well as some $6 Dr. Scholl's, and it does seem to minimize the pain. When I wore the inserts in my "incorrect" J-41 sandals, my foot would hurt significantly midway through the walk, and more afterwards, but I do feel like these provide better ankle support and leave me feeling a bit better post-walk, although no cure-all.

Biggest problem: Automatic Hot Foot
The biggest complaint I have with these shoes is that they have no mesh on them and are not particularly breathable. My feet typically get pretty warm when I walk, even in winter, and these can be stifling in hot weather. I'm sure these shoes would do wonders for my feet if I wore them all the time, but when it's 105, I just can't get past the idea of my feet incased in solid leather and roasting in sweat the entire day. If you have permafrost feet, these might be awesome, but otherwise...keep that in mind.

Overall
I bought these shoes because I needed good, quick, budget friendly walking shoe that wasn't completely horrendous and would not aggravate my plantar fasciitis. These do meet those qualifications well enough with inserts. However, because of the lack of breathability, I probably wouldn't buy them again.ter post-walk, although no cure-all.

These are minimalist shoes, so if that is what you are looking for these are absolutely perfect. Merrell's customer service was able to confirm for me that these are zero drop. I imagine these would be really comfortable for those with bunions because they stretch so nicely.

Despite the description of the foam footbed, these have next to no cushion. I can tell there is the tiniest smidge of padding because my feet don't ache after a long day the way they would in flats with a plain leather insole, but it is definitely not cushy and, for example, you can feel gravel etc through the sole when walking around outside. Again, this is perfect if you want a minimalist/"barefoot" type of shoe, but if you are looking for a standard "comfort" shoe, these will probably fall short. There is also no arch support.

Well, I am disappointed and of two minds in writing this review.

One the one hand, the construction of the shoe appears solid, and it is absolutely gorgeous. Rarely would I spend so much money on sneakers, after all! The design is as eye-catching in real life as it is on the internet. I really love the shoes.

On the other hand, the sizing runs small and is intensely narrow.They need to advertise this. I have a moderately wide foot and ordered a size 12 (my typical size), and it feels like my feet are being crushed. In all my years of shoe shopping (something I probably do far too much), I've never encountered anything even close to this. The size 12 shoe has a narrowness that feels appropriate for a size 10.5. I would like to try a size 13 and see how that goes, but Amazon are for some reason not offering that size, while other sites are. Very disappointing.

The shoe is leather and might adjust a little with some (definitely painful) shoe-training. But these are so narrow that the back part of the leather (as you can see in the pictures, the shoe has a front hunk of leather and a back half, with the two stitched and glued together) is being forced to pop out on both sides in a sort of ovular shape. This leaves me with little hope that training the leather could possibly do enough, so I'm almost surely going to just box these up and return them.

I will update my review if Amazon customer service is of any help in getting a size 13. As it stands, I'm only giving these two stars because of how pretty they are. As long as your aren't a size 12 and in need of the unavailable 13, like I am... You could get a fantastic pair of shoes by just ordering a size larger than your standard. In that case, I definitely recommend them.

EDIT:

I am upgrading this to three stars. I never ended up returning them, because there was no hope for a 13 and because I loved the shoes enough to take the gamble of wearing them a few times. After training the shoes while having them tied quite tightly (to prevent that ovular leather flap problem I noted in my original review), the shoes have started to conform better to my feet. Hooray!

I still completely stand by my original recommendation: Just order a size larger than what you would typically wear.

But if you're a wide size 12 and can't get a 13... I wore a pair of Vasque GTX boots through to the sole over the course of 10 years and spent about 6 months looking for a high-quality boot to replace them. Settled on Lowa because they were reportedly well-made and of high quality materials. However, I am not satisfied with these boots on several levels.

The sole is slippery when on a wet surface. I replaced the insoles that came with the boots with Superfeet insoles but that only helped a little. The boots still feel thin and hot...not at all comfortable just around the house...and even less so on when doing a lot of walking. The left boot fits differently across the top of the foot than does the right...which necessitates keeping the left laces looser to keep from binding the foot. Speaking of laces, the lacing system for these boots is a pain...the flat laces that come with the boots are too wide for the eyehooks...and they don't stay in place. But FINALLY - and this is by far the most irritating aspect of these boots - they SQUEAK with every step! I thought that it was simply because they were new but I've had them for a few months and they continue to do so. I don't know if it's the collar material (which appears to be of a different type material) or what but this is extremely irritating.

All in all, for the price of these boots (around $300) one would expect better comfort, a better lacing system and NO SQUEAKS. Would NOT recommend these to anyone.

Second, the shoe is very light and breathable as advertised.  The appearance is nice, almost more of a neon or bright orange, rather than a medium or darker orange. Third, the carbon materIal on the bottom is very stiff. Big change compared to my Nylon road shoes.  I can't believe retail on these shoes are over $300.  Not sure I see the value if you spend that much (which I didn't). Good looking shoe and am eager to ride more with them.  UPDATE:  So after a couple weeks now and numerous rides, I can add a couple of additional thoughts.  First the toe box does not wear or stretch out.  It is still a litte cramped with socks - even a thin pair.  It fits just right w/o sock, but wonder about those hot days when your feet swell a little.  Next, the heal and toe pad on the carbon aren't rubber.  They feel like a hard plastic colored in orange to appear to look like rubber.  They are slippery and scuf easily.  I wear the Look Keo Cleats with the rubber contacts to prevent slipping around on the ground and still walk gingerly.  Additionally, they are also not replaceable and appear to be part of the mold of the carbon outsole.  This is not a good design in my opinion.  For shoes that retail as high as they do, they should have replaceable parts.

I just had to leave a review after receiving these boots.  First -- (and this part is my fault) I was head-in-the clouds when I ordered, and jumped from Amazon to Ebay without paying attention. Paid $5 too much on Ebay and a return would cost me $40 including restocking and postage, which would have been free on Amazon.  So if you buy these, do stay with Amazon,  Now, the reason for my 2 stars: These are the most uncomfortable boots I've ever purchased, and I have quite a wardrobe of western boots.  These are my first Laredo's, and they are about equal in price to the average boot I buy.  The foot bed curves just enough to pinch my toes on the sides.  They appear wider than my other pointed toe boots, but they sure aren't.  The leather is so heavy and stiff (good for durability but not good for stretching) that it will take some doing if they even can be made comfortable. I think the problem is more the foot bed than the outer leather so they may never feel good. Dear Dr. Martens,

I felt compelled to write your company and tell you how extremely disappointed I am with the quality of your boots. I am 39 years old and when I was a kid your company was highly respected for making quality boots that lasted forever. Sadly your company has turned into a mockery of your once respected name.

As an adult I am required to wear steel-toe shoes due to insurance reasons where I work. However, I do not do any form of hard labor. I am an avionics technician. Several years ago, when my company mandated that the workers start wearing steel-toe shoes, we all sighed. However, my first thought was Dr. Martens. I immediately bought a pair of Dr. Martens 1919 which was perfect because although they were not truly safety rated boots they would pass our inspection for steel toe shoes and were not as bulky.

I wore those boots for about 3 and half years. I would have continued to wear them if it was not for the two holes that wore into each side of the one boot. Although I expected them to last longer I was not that upset since I almost got 4 years out of them. During my time of wearing them many of my co-workers thought the boots looked great and were impressed that they lasted so long and several of them bought Dr. Martens based on my experience. Mind you, there are 3000 employees that work at my company and we all hate steel-toe shoes and hate that we are being forced to wear them. Especially since the work we do does not risk our feet. So we are all always looking for better quality or lighter shoes.

After my experience, I decided to buy a pair of 8761's, they looked like they would last much longer and they cost even more money $140.00. I was excited to get them and as I did with my first pair I would regularly tell people at work that they would get more out of their money with Dr. Martens boots then they would get from other brands. Well all of my talk came to an end rather quickly with the 8761's. Within 6 months the damn soles started coming apart. People at work that were wearing generic Wal-Mart shoes were getting longer lasting foot wear then my expensive Dr. Martens. I felt like a fool and felt like I had been robbed. The company I work for gives their employees $65.00 a year toward shoes. I had wasted 2 years worth of money on a pair of boots that did not even last 6 months. You should see the boots now they look like they are 15 years old yet they are maybe a year and a half old.

Anyway, it is time for me to buy another pair of shoes. A lot of the guys at work have been having some good luck with steel toe shoes from Keen. I think I will give them a try. I don't feel like throwing my money down the toilet. I will leave that for un-informed pop punk teenagers that want to look cool, not the working class.

If your company feels that you owe me as I do, you are welcome to make a shoe donation to me and I am willing to give you another try but not on my dime. I wear a size 41 and you can contact me at propagnesiaaa@hotmail.com

Alright, I rarely ever find the motivation to write reviews, but after throwing down 100 bills for these shoes, and enduring the experience I have endured with them, I gotta say something.

Official score: 2.5/10

These shoes are pretty awful in most ways.

The suede is good not great, you'll get ollie holes after a hard 3-5 days of skating. That's whatever I guess, durability in suede uppers is never expected to be great, especially if you skate technical. Shoe Goo fixes that, so the upper is not what bothered me.

It's the SOLES.

Just awful soles. Each section of tread resides on its own raised platform, so there's all these little tunnels running between these raised platforms. Picture that? Google 'Nike Nano SB Soles' or something. The problem is that every time one of the platforms and its tread slides ever so slightly against the grip tape, which they do constantly of course, the tunnels around the platforms enable the grip tape to begin to RIP the treads off their platforms! You'll be cruising, shifting your feet, setting up for a trick, and you'll feel this floppy thick piece of rubber (the tread) bend and roll up underneath your foot. Its an incredibly frustrating issue. You can superglue the crap out of them, which I do, but it's a temporary fix. The ripping will occur again.

Alright, yes, the board feel is pretty superb. I have a pair of Nike Frees and I love them, that's why I couldn't pass the SB version up. I knew the sole would stretch, bend, and twist to my foot's every whimsical desire, but still, purchasing these shoes was a mistake, no doubt in my mind. I could of gotten two pairs of Lakais or Fallens for the price of these. Nike is onto something with the minimalist approach to skate shoes, but these soles need a complete redesign.

Oh hey last thought, shoe runs pretty narrow.

I have used several models of Sketcher street shoes with gripping soles as my golf shoe of choice for 15 years. Discovering these specialty golf shoes at almost half the price in local golf stores, I took the chance and violated my long standing rule of never buying shoes online and unfitted. They remain tight, especially in the vamp and uppers. Toe space is adequate and length is good, but like other Sketchers, they run smaller than actual sizing, requiring extra toil and discomfort to break in. Aug 2015 review:  I really wanted the smart and stylish Rockport Women's Total Motion Melora Captoe Dress Shoe in Nutella/Black. Boo hoo hoo. The shoe has a comfy looking footbed (a cushioned insole) designed by Adidas. Imagine you already have a comfortable pair of shoes. Now put cushioned insoles inside and they begin to feel less comfortable, maybe even too snug. That Adidas insole is a great idea, but the biggest problem with the shoe, in my opinion, is the insole because: (1) It is glued to the inner bottom of the shoe so it isn't removable or replaceable (2) It is an uneven surface which means that my foot rests on both the raised part of the cushion and the flat part, creating an annoying sensation as if I'm standing on a seam or something like that  IF the footbed was replaceable OR simply an even-surfaced soft cushion, the 7.5W would have been the perfect fit because, according to my typical shoe size, the shoe runs larger than most. I bought three sizes to be sure to get the right fit. None fit well. Rockport: I don't mind going up or down a size in a shoe but making the footbed removable and/or comfortable would change my rating to a solid 4.  Detailed info about the fit:  After reading several earlier reviews about the shoe being too large for some and too small for others, first I tried them in my regular size 8W (a finger-sized gap between back of shoe and my foot), then 7.5W (too snug, caused foot cramps but perhaps wearing them in --maybe for a week or so-- will stretch them into a comfort zone??), and finally 8M (too long and too narrow, caused foot cramps). Although both 8M and 8W were too long, I put in heel grips that kept the 8M but not the 8W from slipping off my foot. I wore them for about an hour last night and another 30 minutes this morning walking around in the 7.5W then the 8M, seekingcomfort with various shoe pads and heel grips.  If I didn't really, really like these Melora Captoe pumps, I would have boxed and returned them within 10 minutes. But this pair tugged my heart and my head because it's one of those timeless beauties that double as a workhorse and a class act. I hope Rockport and Adidas will get it right.

I received my boots today and am fairly happy with my purchase. Their are just two things I wanted to share with those who read these reviews so to be aware. I did quite a bit of research and had decided between the Kamik Jennifer or Hunter classics. I went with the Kamiks because of price and favorable reviews. Firstly I purchased the Black II color since I couldn't see a huge difference between normal Black and Black II. Now the picture of Black II on Amazon shows the boot with the Kamik shield on the side which I liked. The boot I received today does NOT have that shield. The Charcoal II pic does not show the shield so I was hoping the black II boot had it but was prepared if it didn't. I didn't think spending and extra $16 for the shield on the Normal black was really worth it. Secondly a large number of reviews stated the boots ran small and did not fit their ankles or calves and I was a little afraid they would be too small. This was not the case for me. I'm not petite and small and am about 5'8 142ish pounds to give you an idea. I wear an 8.5 shoe so went with the 9s. These are not too small but a little roomy. I have no problem getting them on or off and they are a bit big in the calves and ankles. I could see though how after awhile these could rub your ankles. To combat this I tried a thick leg warmer on with them and problem solved. Fills in the extra room around the calf AND keeps my ankle from rubbing against the thick rubber.

In all I am happy with these boots and will be keeping them. They do look much cuter than other rainboots, even w/out the Kamik label on the side, and they are sturdy and comfy. I also like the removable insole which adds extra cushioning and comfort than other rainboots I have owned. I gave these a 4 though instead of a 5 because of the misrepresentation of the pic online which is the sellers fault and not the manufacturer.

I have been wearing Croc flip flops for several years as a work shoe. I am a dog groomer in SW Florida and am on my feet for long hours. These give me plenty of support and are very light weight. This is my first pair of the Modi style shoe and I have a few cons:
- the toe piece is not molded into the shoe and creates pressure points until broken in
- the inserts tend to collect debris (dog hair) in the cracks
- the toe piece is fabric and absorbs moisture and odors

Pros are:
- extremely light weight
- fantastic arch support
- good gripping contact with floor
- well fitting, hug the foot
- foot conforming
- long lasting

Overall I am satisfied with my purchase but will likely change styles in a year and half to two years which is the length of time these kinds of flip flops last me with daily wear in all kinds of wet weather and walking conditions.

When I first got them, I put my foot in and it was swimming with all the room. Also, the two zippers on each shoe were pretty scratchy. And of course, they came with that chemically smell that all these kind of retailers from amazon have. Now with all these problems, why did I give 4 stars? Well, when I order things like this from amazon, I expect to have to work with them a bit. Now, since they felt wide when I tried them on (and I don't have narrow feet) I slipped on a regular sock (Hanes brand; not real thick, but definitely not thin) and to my surprise, they fit me perfectly. Maybe if you have narrow feet you'd need a thick sock, but I was fine with a regular one. Then, I had to tackle the problem of the scratchy zippers. I personally don't mind what the inside of my shoes look like, so I literally hot-glued scrap pieces of thick fabric on the inside of both zippers so that the poky part didn't come into contact with my skin. After that, these shoes have been wonderful. I've worn them all across campus, I've went out shopping in them where I walked multiple places and was constantly on my feet. Even after a day of walking around, they only hurt a little bit but the pain was gone by the morning. These little booties are perfect for walking around in and for every day use.
